review:
上一次打开巫师三已经是三年前了，刚开始玩就觉得我是手残玩不了，有这么多不同的剑油、煎药、药水，眼都花了。同时也百思不得其解为什么守卫一直要揍我，在去跑任务的路上等级低又一直死，于是乎就直接退坑。究竟什么任务我要被揍得这么惨，后知后觉是因为当着守卫捡东西（现在想起来都觉得很搞笑），才被集体围殴的，当时根本没反应过来，处在一个超级萌新的状态中。哦对，那时候还不会玩昆特牌，其实昆特牌是很好玩嘟！-3-

虽然重制版令我游戏崩溃+吞成就了无数次，但是还是能给一个高分。这次一口气一个月内把本体连带DLC都通关了，畅快，搜了很多相关的背景故事，有好好看介绍的百科，终于逃离了超级萌新状态，就这么因为剧情坚持玩下来了。对比以前的UI界面也变好看了一点点。没变的是杰洛特还是那么脆（打了坠落无伤MOD好多了，这个必打！推荐！）。不懂为什么给Ciri中配是很软萌的女孩子的声音，很喜欢英配的Ciri和Yennefer！中后期就切成了英配游玩。游戏里有很多角色是有带口音的，中配完全体现不出来，还是英配原汁原味。除了史凯利格海上问号都做完了，不想继续了，游泳潜水和开船好无聊啊。除去以上的毛病，游戏的支线故事、美术画面、音乐渲染，都很值得去慢慢地游玩感受！就是血与酒打完觉得葡萄园的小屋子不够大了，要有更多展示的地方放我的收集品那是最好不过~

CDPR你真狠，一个是巫师三一个是赛博朋克2077，两个游戏还互相有一点联动，真让我玩爽了。(￣∀￣)

review:
Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the greatest redemption stories in gaming history. What started as one of the most disappointing and rocky launches in recent gaming memory has evolved into an absolute masterpiece. It's genuinely incredible to see just how far this game has come. CD Projekt Red could have walked away, but instead, they put in the time, effort, and dedication to transform Cyberpunk 2077 into the experience it was always meant to be.

Night City is absolutely breathtaking. It's one of the most immersive, detailed, and atmospheric open worlds I've ever experienced. Every street, alleyway, nightclub, and skyscraper feels like it belongs in a living, breathing world. The characters are unforgettable, the storytelling is phenomenal, and the choices you make carry emotional weight. The combat is incredibly satisfying, the customization is fantastic, and there's so much freedom in how you approach your build and playstyle.

And then there's Phantom Liberty. Absolutely phenomenal DLC. This expansion is everything DLC should strive to be. The new storyline, characters, missions, atmosphere, and incredible performances elevate an already amazing game to another level. Dogtown is an incredible addition, and the storytelling genuinely rivals some of the best experiences in gaming. It doesn't feel like a small add-on; it feels like a substantial expansion that makes the entire experience even better. I would happily pay for more expansions of this quality.

What impresses me most is the dedication CD Projekt Red showed in rebuilding this game. The updates, improvements, reworked systems, and continued support turned Cyberpunk 2077 into something truly special. It's a reminder that a rough launch doesn't necessarily have to define a game's entire legacy.

I genuinely hope we get more stories, expansions, and opportunities to return to this incredible universe. Night City is a world I never want to leave, and I'd gladly spend another hundred hours exploring every corner of it.

Cyberpunk 2077 went from a cautionary tale to a masterpiece. Phantom Liberty took it even further. An unforgettable experience, an incredible redemption story, and one of the best RPGs I've ever played. Never fade away! 11/01/2026

review:
Cyberpunk 2077 hadir dengan premis naratif yang kuat dan eksekusi dunia yang solid, meskipun sempat melalui rilis awal yang penuh kacau. Daya tarik utama game ini sekarang terletak pada bagaimana CD Projekt Red konsisten merawat dan memperbaiki gamenya secara transparan. Mereka tidak membiarkan komunitasnya mati begitu saja setelah sempat hancur lebur (POIN TERBAIK UNTUK CDPR), melainkan membuktikan komitmen lewat perbaikan total hingga versi terbarunya berdiri sebagai sebuah masterpiece. Contoh paling nyatanya bisa dilihat dari stabilitas teknis di PC yang baik, berkurangnya bug gajelas, serta rombakan besar pada sistem combat, perks, dan Relic skills baru yang bikin kustomisasi build karakter makin seru.

Dari segi progres dan cerita, game ini menawarkan struktur naratif yang berkesan mendalam, terbukti dari total waktu main saya yang menyentuh angka 31 jam untuk menamatkan main story, DLC Phantom Liberty, dan sekitar 50% side quest (banyak banget side questnya). Perjalanan V dari awal menapaki kerasnya Night City hingga terseret konspirasi biochip Relic diracik dengan pacing emosional yang pas. Dinamika hubungan antara V dan Johnny Silverhand membuat alur utamanya hidup dan tidak terasa hampa. Terlebih lagi, pengalaman bermain game ini terasa semakin emosional dan perfectly nice setelah menonton serial anime Cyberpunk: Edgerunners setiap sudut jalanan Night City, mulai dari distrik Megabuilding hingga bar Afterlife, terasa punya nyawa dan sejarah kelamnya sendiri. [spoiler](Ada soundtrack anime yang masuk sebagai lagu, well played)[/spoiler]

Namun, puncak emosi dan nilai plus terbesar bagi saya pribadi terletak pada DLC Phantom Liberty dan dinamika karakternya, terutama Songbird/Song Seon-mi. Sejak awal, meskipun saya merasa ada gelagat yang janggal dan mencurigakan dari gerak-geriknya, kedekatan emosional membuat saya memilih untuk tetap bersama songbird. Saya mengabaikan segalapilihan berkhianat pada songbird di situasi apapun. Pilihan saya itu tetap setia di sampingnya sampai titik darah penghabisan, ngelewatin ketegangan dikejar agen NUSA, hingga benar-benar mengantarkannya terbang ke bulan. Momen perpisahan itu terasa sangat tulus, pilu, dan membekas sebagai salah satu cerita terbaik yang pernah saya mainkan. [spoiler]( ini terlalu subjektif karena saya emang cinta mati sama karakter Songbird pada saat pertama kali bertemu, Asian Supremacy)[/spoiler]

Melihat kualitas fondasi dunianya yang imersif ditambah dukungan jangka panjang yang solid dari sang developer, game ini jelas sangat layak dicoba. Perlu diingat, game ini menawarkan pengalaman emosional yang luar biasa bagi pemain yang fokus ke cerita. Kalau ada diskon wajib di beli bersama DLC Phantom Liberty-nya. Good Job CDPR! [b]Song Mi Supremacy♡♡[/b]

[spoiler]( ini terlalu subjektif karena saya emang cinta mati sama karakter songbird pada saat pertama kali bertemu, asian supremacy)[/spoiler] melihat kualitas fondasi dunianya yang imersif ditambah dukungan jangka panjang yang solid dari sang developer, game ini jelas sangat layak dicoba. perlu diingat, game ini menawarkan pengalaman emosional yang luar biasa bagi pemain yang fokus ke cerita. kalau ada diskon wajib di beli bersama dlc phantom liberty-nya. good job cdpr! review:
From a rocky start to a top-tier action RPG: Amazing redemption, but still room for polish.

Cyberpunk 2077 hardly needs an introduction: it’s an immersive first-person action-RPG set in the visually stunning, cutthroat metropolis of Night City. You play as V, a mercenary navigating a high-stakes story alongside Johnny Silverhand, building your character through cyberware, stealth, hacking, and intense gunplay.
A Remarkable Comeback
CD Projekt RED deserves huge credit for how far this game has come. Thanks to major updates
—most notably Patch 2.0—alongside the wave of hype from the Edgerunners anime, the game was truly given a second life. Today, it stands as a fantastic title that fully proves its worth.
Why It's Great Today:
Playstyle Variety: There are so many distinct ways to play. Whether you prefer pure netrunning, stealth, melee combat, or heavy firearms, the build progression feels deep and rewarding.
Night City remains one of the most impressively detailed and atmospheric open worlds in gaming history.

What Keeps It From Absolute Perfection:
Even though the game is in a great place, for a flagship AAA title, there are still minor physics details, vehicle interactions, and small technical quirks that could use one final polish update. Fleshing out these subtle environmental and mechanical details would truly elevate the overall immersion to the highest level.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a reborn masterpiece that is well worth your time and money. While we know major content additions have wrapped up, here's hoping CD Projekt RED might still drop a future update focused on these small micro-fixes to leave the game in absolute peak condition. Highly recommended!

review:
My favorite game of all time with the worst updates of all time.

Firstly, i got much more stutters and crashes in 2.5, despite the game being pretty unstable even before the update. And im relativiely lucky, saw many posts about performance issues for previous updates too. For some reason they also massacred the HDR settings, "color saturation" setting is under "maximum brightness" (also there is something off with it, definitely not the same setting as from pre-2.5), and there is no actual maximum brightness and UI brightness settings which were there before. Not talking about blackfloor level, which is elevated in any game that i've played in HDR.
Why do u never test ur updates CDPR? Not only do u not test them, but u're also straight up lying: "Introduced various performance optimizations" and "Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays". Sure buddy.

Secondly, that got me thinking about the content they give to us. 
Look, we have an objectively unpolished game with a lot of bugs, unstable performance and literally an incomplete city, there are still many unfinished areas. 
Maybe instead of adding small cosmetic/gameplay features (of which i only use delamain service sometimes, and the clampdown quest is decent) and some random side quests, u could use the resources to complete Night City? Or finally optimize the game and fix the bugs so that it doesn't feel like playing a janky piece of code? Or maybe (just maybe) instead of all these updates u could make the infamous Crystal Palace DLC?

I would not complain about the content if u hadn't taken away the somewhat stable performance and HDR settings from me (again, performance issues were the case in previous updates too, i was just lucky), and vice versa, i would not complain about performance issues and HDR if we got something from what i mentioned above (as long as the game remained playable ofc). After all, the updates are free. But i got none of that.

The only update this game actually needed was 2.0 (apart from the earlier updates that fixed critical bugs from release).

Oh and yeah, maybe they'll release a patch that fixes HDR and performance in this update, but there shouldn't be broken updates in the first place, and my critique about the lack of meaningful content and unfixed game in general, combined with these broken updates, is still relevant.


P.S. Forgot to mention the performance in Dogtown. I understand that its a dense location filled with a lot of details, but both Jig Jig Street and the area behind Tom's Diner are working much better than Dogtown, despite also being very crowded.

总得来说一直以来游戏就是一个半成品，哪怕是更新到了2.5版本也还是半成品，个人认为玩家完全是靠边缘行者的动漫ip支撑着把游戏玩下去，但实话说如果赛博朋克2077不是一个游戏而是一部电影，这种引人入胜的剧情可以说是让人沉浸其中，支线剧情把夜之城从底层到上层人民，从V的朋友到V的仇人等角色描述出了他们的血肉，让玩家仿佛和真实存在的人物共同生活在这样一座光怪陆离的城市；主线剧情又牢牢把握住了V的现实处境，让玩家想要主动推动剧情，甚至幻想自己就是生活在夜之城这个未来都市里！

敬夜之城

Overall, the game has consistently remained an unfinished product; even after being updated to version 2.5, it is still incomplete. I personally believe that players have continued to play the game solely on the strength of the anime IP Edgerunners. Frankly, however, if Cyberpunk 2077 were a film rather than a game, its captivating narrative would be thoroughly immersive: the side quests endow characters—from the lower to the upper strata of Night City, from V’s friends to V’s enemies—with flesh and blood, making players feel as though they are living alongside genuinely existing individuals in such a bizarre and dazzling city; the main storyline, for its part, firmly captures V’s real predicament, prompting players to actively advance the plot and even to imagine themselves living in Night City, this futuristic metropolis. Here’s to Night City.

review:
我希望第二部实现的五个突破
1. 让城市真正具备持续运行的社会生态。
帮派应当能够争夺地盘，企业行动应当产生社会后果，NPC 可以拥有可信的日常活动，玩家也应该通过行动改变自己在街区中的处境。如果你摧毁某个帮派的重要设施，该地区的势力、交易活动和安全状况应该在随后发生变化。不需要模拟每一个居民，但需要让关键行为产生持续性的世界反馈。
2. 让玩家拥有真正不同的人生。
公司特工、街头佣兵、网络黑客不应该只是技能配置不同。他们应当具备不同的信息来源、人际网络、任务解决方式和成长路径。例如同一个目标，黑客可以侵入企业网络，谈判专家能够利用利益关系，武装佣兵则选择正面突破。不过这些方案的后续代价也应有所不同。
3. 把人工智能从背景设定变成真正的系统主题。
我认为这是第二部最有机会超越第一部的方向。现实世界的生成式 AI、自动化决策、数字身份与数据所有权问题，已经让传统赛博朋克设定变得越来越接近现实。第二部完全有机会把数字人格、企业 AI、自主意识以及黑墙之外的智能实体发展成更深入的叙事主题。
4. 保留单人故事的核心价值，不要为了多人模式牺牲它。
我认为《2077》的真正竞争力是它的人物叙事，不是在线枪战。第二部可以探索可选的合作体验，但我不希望它被改造成重度在线服务型游戏，更不希望任务设计被赛季、刷取和商业化机制主导。
5. 不要盲目追求更大的地图。
如果第二部有两座城市，我希望它们在社会制度、势力关系、经济运作与角色生活方式上存在实质差异。否则，两座空洞的城市不一定胜过一座丰富的城市。我更希望 CDPR 把第二部的开发预算花在城市互动密度上，而不是继续增加无意义的地图面积。

review:
很多人聊《赛博朋克 2077》，只谈霓虹夜景和往日之影，但打动我的是那些冷门细碎的叙事。夜之城的魅力藏在背景音里：街角路人闲谈、电台里矛盾交织的广告与寻人播报，大企业的宣传和失踪者消息挤在同一频段，没有人是非黑即白的。
我偏爱佩拉雷兹市长支线，没有激烈枪战，只有记忆被篡改的冰凉无力，真相近在眼前，却抓不住证据。还有自愿赴死的赛博精神病、满口阴谋论的加里，克里支线里摇滚巨星被资本耗尽后的孤独，都比主线更有赛博朋克的味道。
V 的核心从来不是复仇，而是自我主权之争。Relic 缓慢吞噬意识，每一次和强尼拉扯，都是叩问：当记忆都能被改写，我该如何确认自己？恶魔结局压抑克制的镜头设计，很少有 RPG 敢这样剥夺玩家主动权。

review:
一坨吧。玩得也算久了，DLC我也买了，但没玩到那。
捏人不能第三视角看，有nuan用，第一视角玩一阵就要感觉吐，看镜子糊的一批，拿着武器看自己的影子糖的一批。
牺牲流畅性，玩不了，牺牲画面感，像在看恐怖片，各个长得是千奇百怪不可直视。
城市那么大，可互动的内容那么少，所谓的超梦也是虎头蛇尾，靠mod救了救。
总之，这游戏就像一个大盒子，盒子里装了个小小的过山车，主线+部分支线任务就是那个小小的过山车，玩完了这个过山车，你就只能盯着空盒子傻愣，最后啥也干不了。（我打了一辈子仗,就不能享受享受吗?）
起初看宣传以为是GTA，到如今的2026，我依然无法释怀——宣传诈骗。
我不是一个喜欢打差评的人。但当这个游戏我花了钱，却依然经过漫长磨合无法自适应后，我才会选择打差评。

review:
[h1]BE THE LEGEND[/h1]
在全成就达成的今天，写下这篇评价。
其实感受有太多，根本不是几段话能写完的，聊记一二吧。

想起游玩的初期，觉得现实和游戏的差距似乎不太远了，科幻即将变成纪录片，但深入吸收剧情、芯片、广播和数据库的内容之后，地区、阶级、阵营、冲突等概念在脑海里编织成网，回过头才发现自己已经在这个世界里沉浸得那么深了...
感谢CDPR制作出如此伟大的游戏，我永远也不会忘记玩2077的这三个月了。T T

简评一下本体结局吧，最先达成单刷荒坂塔的太阳结局，省时间、战斗爽、无亲友伤亡，最畅快的一条路！非常喜欢任务标题“以我残躯化烈火”，轰轰烈烈地活过，成为城市传奇，也不负时日无多的生命了。没想到会在最后见到蓝眼睛先生，可惜CDPR并没有做水晶宫的内容，V只能在太空遥望一下了。
恶魔结局确实是叛众离亲了，不过这条线的对话非常有意思，一路上会欣赏到荒坂塔的室内和景观设计；和竹村并肩战斗的感觉很棒，如果不是立场和原则的冲突，应该能和他能一直做好朋友吧。赖宣和华子关系微妙，三郎复活过来还挺令人毛骨悚然。结局烂完了，草间太啥哔了，只比个中指我觉得自己太文明了，拧魔方更是吓我一雷。
星星结局也是一路战斗，但不那么流畅，阿德卡多是真把我当家人啊，不过习惯了独来独往，竟然感觉需要适应这种群聚共战、别人乐意为我牺牲的状态。最后坐在魔蜥上吹夜风，很美的镜头啊。

关于DLC，剧情和任务质量已经和本体不在同个档次了。我心所选的是权杖国王结局，高塔结局太让人难受了，经历之后彻底领悟到“窝囊活不如壮烈死”。圣杯国王结局这条线视觉和故事性拉满，虽然在Cynosure设施里搞追逐战太阴森了，但补全了公司战争的背景，流窜AI传信设计得相当对味。如果不体验全结局，会错过很多好剧情。

总之，目前2.5版本更新的任务没做，车和枪都没体验够，我还会常回家看看的。

review:
我好像做了一场梦, 置身于一座陌生的城市, 以旁观者的视角, 看着每一个充满代价的选择, 一段成为传奇的经历, 两个不完美人格争夺一具身体, 最终迈向注定死亡的悲剧. 
这场梦越到后来越不像冒险, 而像一场缓慢的清算. 夜之城用霓虹许诺自由, 却用账单、义体维护、公司合同和生存期限把自由折算成价格; 它让人相信身体可以更换、记忆可以购买、意识可以上传，却从不回答替换血肉之躯后“我”还剩下什么. V 与强尼共用一具濒死的身体, 一个想活命, 一个想赎罪, 一个用谎言争取时间, 一个用愤怒证明存在；互相入侵、互相辩驳、互相在对方身上留下无法擦除的影子. 
当我以旁观者之名按下选择, 实则每一次选择都在分配失去：失去朋友、失去身体、失去记忆、失去自我，或失去让“自我”继续存在的可能. 
所谓传奇，不过是夜之城把一个人的挣扎包装成可消费的故事；所谓结局，也没有胜利者，只有不同形式的代价. 在高科技、低生活的社会里, 技术没有兑现救赎, 只是把压迫做得更精密, 把人的身体、情感与意识逐项标价. 当技术成为权力、身体成为商品、意识成为数据, 人便被迫在最狭窄的缝隙里回答那个古老而残酷的问题——我是谁? 而赛博朋克最冷峻之处正在于: 它不提供完美选择, 只逼你在不完美的世界里, 带着代价确认自己曾经活过、爱过、反抗过，并在系统收走一切之前, 留下一个未必胜利却仍属于“我”的答案. 
梦醒之后, 夜之城依旧灯火通明. 只是我已分不清哪一段记忆属于 V, 哪一段属于强尼, 哪一段属于真正的“我”.
全成就通关, 感谢陪伴.

review:
The parkour, and being able to get into windows on random floors — these are the only decent things in this game. And they are crippled by the fighting system which degraded so much that I simply avoid fighting zombies instead of slashing through them wherever I go.

Like, it is supposed to be a zombie-slasher game, but for some reason the zombies so rarely get sliced, that most of the time you just bluntly beat them half to death before executing a finisher move that has just a couple of predefined animations.

That was not the problem with Dying Light 1 — there I could aimlessly roam around the world, slashing zombies for my own amusement. In Dying Light 2 though, even just mindlessly parkouring is no fun, since there's nothing fun to explore.

Therefore, my playthrough quickly deteriorated into running through the story or side quests. The problem is, neither is good. There are some decent side quests I found interesting and engaging, but even they are usually half-assed. Like that time I fetched a toy stolen from a little girl, only to NOT EVEN RETURN IT to the girl. Or like when each time I decide to snitch on a culprit, the plot conveniently makes me kill them instead. But to be fair, the plot with the lost kids and dog was a particularly well written one, and overall implemented fine.

The main plot, as far as I played, could be enjoyable enough if not for the weakest illusion of choice I've seen in a game with the most absurdly written dialogs that I've simply started skipping — they didn't say much anyway, but sure used a lot of words. And that's a shame, because the characters seem interesting and memorable, and the factions have a very good composition. 

As for the world where the story takes place, it is so far off from the original Dying Light world, that I simply don't like it — it fails expectations set by the first game. Stylistically, that is. In general, it works well enough for the gameplay — the parkour is good enough, and the idea of having a lot of open windows to get into is very nice.

What I don't like about the gameplay, is just how obviously they copied Far Cry in the various base-capturing mechanic. tldr:  Dying Light 1 was an action horror game featuring parkour with stealth elements and opportunities.
Dying Light 2 is a stealth horror game with action elements and parkour opportunities.  

There's nothing in Dying Light 2 that can't be found being done better in zombie games like the first Dying Light, Dead Island, or Dead Island Riptide.  If you're a fan of those games, and are hoping Dying Light 2 is going to keep the high energy parkour action going---well, it's just not.  Dying Light 2 is a ponderous slog compared to its predecessor.  Watch the first Steam trailer and notice how all the player POV is during DAYLIGHT . . . because nighttime is all about creeping and stealth and is boring to watch in a video.

In DL1 the most terrifying and dangerous zombies haunted the darkness, so not being out at night was a primary device creating tension in the game.  At night the zombies were faster and deadlier and stealth becomes a key consideration to player survival.  With the exception of a couple missions, it was entirely up to the player how much of this "night game" they wanted to play, allowing for players to shape the tone and expand the action of the game for themselves. 

From the outset Dying Light 2 seems determined that you WILL spend a lot of time in slowly, carefully, tediously creeping around in the dark.  In DL2 the "day game" "night game" choice has been functionally removed from the player.  G'bye parkour-filled, action-packed "day game" fun we experienced DL1.  

I'm just not interested in being forced to do a lot of stealth in a game I bought for its parkour mechanics and zombie slaying violence.

I'll never get my money's worth out of playing Dying Light 2 because it's not a game I would've ever spent any money on if I'd known it was going to be such a bore.

review:
Dying light 2 is not at all what I expected it to be. The game is decent at best and its a very biased opinion to rate this game as "decent". 

The parkour is about the only good aspect of this game, though it loses its realism in grounded parkour. They introduced a new kind of grappling hook which was pretty cool. The horror aspect of the nighttime in this game is garbage, I was able to kill a volatile very quickly in to the game. I was level 4 farming volatiles, safe to say that if you want to play a zombie horror game this is not the game for you. The CO OP is super buggy, constantly glitching me and my friends out of the elevator, despawning enemies forcing us to log back in to the game.

 The game is heavily server sided and it auto teleports you evertime your teammate gets close to the mission point. I heavily dislike how arcadey and parkour game with zombies this game is. You have to go out of your way and go to a badly engineered safe zone for the simplest thing like repairing your weapon. Aiden is a pussy, he gets punched in the face every other time and he can not tell a traitor from a billion miles away. The dialogue in this game is extremely stretched and the npcs are talking about nonsense majority of the cutscenes.

The paraglider makes it extremely easy to avoid any kind of danger and it fully removes the terrifying aspect of running away like the 2 other games. Dont even get me started  on Hakon and Lawan.. I am 99 percent sure Hakon is gay with all the time he caresses aiden and constantly wants to talk to this guy. I swear the dialogue with hakon adds  up to 2 hours of the game. And most of the missions were genuine slop, "get lawan's shoes"... what does getting lawans shoes add to the story? other than finding out that hakon is not truly gay and has been with a woman and isnt the incel he appears to be nothing else is added to the game. Most of the quests are turning on stuff and going places getting absolutely nothing done.

The game started off strong, introducing inhibitors and the bracelets really added on to the post apocalyptic  vibe that people are settling in and getting used to life in the apocalypse. Other than that the story is rushed and the premise that you are looking for someone you havent seen since you were kids and knowing that she isnt even your biological sister is trash as fuck. The story is extremely rushed and to cover it up, techland drags it with 3 minute dialogues. I also do not understand how techland decides to make us listen to a jackass dying and talking to us like we have been friends with them for a while. majority of the times we have never even met the characters that have a 4 minute speech while they are bleeding out.

Bloody ties is the worst dlc the game couldve introduced. I also do not understand how a game that you as a developer know isnt as strong in terms of story like the other games gives you the brilliant idea to give the character stamina while climbing. Majority of the parkour other than the basics is just button smashing and hoping to do a move you have yet to see. The skill tree is no where near as exciting to grind for and neither is it hard or challenging to upgrade but the combat skill tree sucks balls. It is also just forcing you to keep playing by not making you fully level up your skill tree and making you redo the entire story again just for you to get 3 more skills in the skill tree.

The bossfight is a massive letdown. The boss is a super easy fight and hyper repetitive. as soon as waltz hits the last phase all he does is just run away. When you get to the final cutscene a disabled chick does more convincing than aiden and you just stand there like a cuck until the key is thrown into the lava. At least with the ending I got. Everytime you think you are going to win a boss segment, you get knocked out and lose the dopamine of beating  the low lifes that tried fighting you. The renegades straight up sound goofy and are  not intimidating at all, they sound like frogs.

Overall this game has its pros but is full of cons, if you expected that this game would be peak because of the 5 years of support it has been getting, no it is not and it looks like a mobile game with all the ads in the loading screen. If you want to parkour and live though this post apocalyptic world, this game is for you, but dont expect it to be a fun grind. Although, if you are looking for a scary game with a compelling story this game isnt for you.

review:
Dying Light 1 feels incredible to play, both its main game and DLC. Story isn't great but it feeds the gameplay well. It's also the first time during the console generation switch (360 to xbone) where I felt the game truly took advantage of its new hardware, looking incredible and feeling dynamic in both visuals and gameplay.

So, snagging DL2 on the steam sale I felt it was time to finally try things out. Not only does the game feel like a mobile game, it plays worse, too. Sure, I've only played about an hour of the game, but immediately the combat feels off. Not only do the weapons have virtually no impact, there's the introduction of these quick-kills by pressing F that are sometimes short, sometimes long, and ultimately remove me from combat.

Also, admittedly, the aesthetic of the game is very strange. It feels very coorporate, whereas the first game felt focused. It opens explaining the world had a cure, preventing the spread of the disease, but then a new strain wiped out the planet (so... why tell me there was a cure?) so everything's post-apocalyptic. But, also, our characters all dress in medieval wear. It all feels very LARP-coded (as in actual Live-Action Role-Play). It's not an aesthetic I would have considered "Dying Light" coded by any means. 

I only knew the game had a bad launch, but learning the game has been greatly altered since it released feels strange. The prologue is skippable, but I decided to try it because it's basically the tutorial of the game, but then read it has been changed multiple times. I guess I'm not that bothered by it, but it's a weird choice that kinda speaks to many other choices I've near-immediately noticed seem... off. I imagine this game went through multiple iterations, director changes, and all-in-all feels like its held together by tape and twist-ties.

Idk. I'm gonna try it out for another 50-minutes, but I don't want to cross the 2-hour mark because I'm seriously considering refunding my purchase. I'll jump into The Beast since I hear that's a better game overall. It also looks more aesthetically like the original game. Cause this feels like an absolute mess. If I return it, maybe I'll rebuy it when it's VERY cheap. But after playing through the first game a second time, then playing through The Following and really enjoying a lot of that, this immediately feels like several steps backward.

Obviously I enjoyed the game enough to play it for 90+ hours, but some stuff that I didn't enjoy is the following:
The map didn't want to be my friend as it would constantly forget that I had already found some locations and I would rediscover said locations a few times throughout my playthrough.
I already knew going into this that what was promised at E3 wasnt going to happen and the choices were not as impactful as I'd hoped.
I never felt like I made an impact or change by doing any story, side quests, windmills, etc 
The mission things were a complete waste of time and very disappointed that I couldn't get any more than a pistol because they're locked behind essentially what is the chore list.
Certain parts felt extremely repetitive like the electrical stations and metros.

review:
So I completed Dying Light 2 on the XBOX X when it was first released and still own it on disc. It was fun, and enjoyable considering the type of games I enjoy. Post-Apocalypse games, literature and media have always interested me. Especially zombies which is a given considering what most of us grew up watching and playing games about.

Harran of the original game was exciting, trying to survive by travelling by and at night avoiding the Volatiles. Villedor of DY2 is just as expansive, taking place in an Eastern European city that walled itself off to first contain the virus only for those very same walls to save it's inhabitants when the virus affected the entire world.

I quite enjoyed the Faction system; with the Peacekeepers and the Survivors, deciding who to help and assist with the Renegades as the enemy faction. Discovering outposts and deciding who would get it, with different benefits to whichever faction you side with.

The combat of melee being primarily your way of fighting the infected and the Renegades and other human threats makes a return, with guns coming in later in the game. 

Similar games have come a long way from say Dead Island, expanding in lore but also gameplay mechanics. For fans of the original Dying Light, the sequel is as enjoyable. For those who haven't played it, think Dead Island expanded upon in many different ways.

I remember paying half-price for DL2 on XBOX, and I didn't regret. This being Steam there are I would say daily events and discounts, or bundles of the Dying Light franchise so it's worth buying when one is on. Get lost in a world where humanity is in a corner, against all odds trying to scratch out a life and fighting the infected and humans who wants to rule the world. A simple concept. 

8/10

A lot of people that I've heard from say they don't like this game, which i do not agree with
ive played dying light 1 and it was great, the overarching story, the gameplay, everything about it was great, so i decided to play this one, and its just as good as the first one

the story is a lot different from the first one, but is still great, the storytelling, the references to the first game, the smooth gameplay, the character arcs, im very fond of all of it

the character you play as, aiden, is a lot similar to crane in the first game in a lot of ways, but they are also different in a lot of ways, making a great experience overall

the choices you get to make along the way and the different endings that tie to it, how the characters treat you depending on the paths you choose, its all just really interesting and overall tells a great story, playing as an infected also brings a lot to the game and adds a new fighting mechanic that i thought was extremely fun to mess around with

TLDR: some parts of the game are more boring than others, but you could say the same thing about the first game as well, overall i think the game is awesome to play, it feels just as smooth as the first one and even adds new mechanics as well as keeping a lot of the original gameplay the first game had, if you enjoyed the first game or are new to the dl universe, either way i highly recommend playing this game, you do not need to play the first one to understand this one either, it has a completely different story with many new characteres and interests

review:
The story sucks and for some number of hours the gameplay sucks. The main character is an idiot with a boring motivation that no one is going to care about. The cutscenes and dialog are awful. They serve to break up gameplay and take away player agency so that the main character can be an idiot and/or let plot happen to him. Gameplay is sluggish compared to DL1, clearly the DL2 was optimized for game pad use. You can even see it in the UI - huge elements as if they expected people to play from a TV.  I only played up to the end of the idiotic hospital visit, but combat and parkour feel terrible. I'm not willing to play more to get skill unlocks to make it more enjoyable since the story is clearly "things happen to idiot until idiot stumbles to his main goal". Also, not a fan of the idea of another mechanic to keep the idiot from turning into a zombie. So, refund requested.

My experience was with physical parkour. I played using Hard difficulty.

review:
[h1][b] TLDR: While the parkour remains excellent, nearly everything else feels like a step back from Dying Light 1. [/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
➕Parkour is great
➕Story-driven choices that impact the narrative outcome

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Enemy AI seems buggy and occasionally just “Shuts off”
➖Excessive pointless zombie spawns - literally 3 melee attacks suddenly spawns multiple fast infected
➖Sorting in inventory never saves
➖Narrative isn’t that interesting
➖Most quests are boring fetch quests
➖Obnoxious and constant audio cues that you cannot disable (constantly notifies of ANY nearby event)
➖Combat skill tree is boring

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/239140?snr=1_5_9__402]My review for Dying Light (DL1) is here[/url]

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world takes place in a city called Villedor in 2036, 22 years after the events of DL1. The setting is mostly similar to Harran, the city from DL1. There are two main areas, a smaller village-like starting area that is a bit more rural, and the city proper, with larger buildings and a downtown-like area. 
Regardless of the differences, every building interior looks like every other and no matter how sheltered or locked down a place has been for decades, there’s always somehow zombies waiting for you inside. The exploration is good, and there are tons of random things to do in the open world. Think like an Ubisoft game, and all the good, and bad, that comes with it. 


The narrative to me was a big let down. You play as Aiden who is a “Pilgrim”. Basically what Dying Light has branded to be some sort of long-distance parkour enthusiast deliverymen. Aiden has come to Villedor to find his sister and thus begins the search. 
The story is just all over the place. I really like how there are (seemingly) big decision points to make, but these don’t seem to have a big effect on the story other than some slightly different cutscenes, dialogue, and the ending cutscene. I got about 20 hours into it before I was starting to get bored of the disappointing fetch quest side missions, and the main story itself. While there are some revelations near the end, the story never hit a positive note after dragging on. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The general gameplay loop is typical of an open world game - completing mission objectives from one area to another. 
Coming from DL1, there are some big changes, and most of them are not positive. 
The parkour remains the best part of the game, by far., and I think it’s improved a bit. Jumping from the top of towers still gives that white-knuckle tense feeling, so it’s still great there. Adding to the already good traversal mechanics are the paraglider and a grappling hook. Though DL1 had a grappling hook, it’s not bound to a talent, you get it about 60% of the way through the story. 
The night elements have also changed. Now, you have a timer that forces you to either use a consumable or reach a UV light before it runs out, else its game over.
The RPG-like gear system has been expanded from just weapons to include gear. I didn’t find this very meaningful and the game could have done without it. 
Speaking of talents, there are two trees - combat and parkour. The combat tree I found terribly boring, but the parkour tree was good. 

The difficulty is more on the easier side. The few times I died were all because of failed parkour attempts and not the combat. Though with the combat, the Volatiles will still mess you up. The regular zombies are just a hindrance, and often annoying as the runners constantly show up when doing basic attacks against any enemy

[h1] [b] Technical (Graphics/Performance) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
I found the graphics to be this weird middle area between PS4 and PS4-era fidelity. The environments and world look great, if repetitive, but the character design and animations are a step lower. 
I played fully maxed and felt the performance was good. 
Of note is the constant bugs. I hear this has been improved with post-launch patches, but I still ran into things constantly. The most egregious is the enemy AI. The AI would occasionally literally “Turn off” and the enemies would just stand there. Also the Volatile chase sequences were a bit of a joke with how poor the AI is at following you 

1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD  

[h1] [b] Audio – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
The music wasn’t great. In fact, I ended up turning it down because it was getting annoying. 
There’s also a sound effect, like sort of deep “Ding” that plays when an event near you is active, which happens [b]all the time[/b]. I couldn’t find a way to turn it off, but it really takes you out of the game with the constant sound. 
The voice acting is good. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
There is NG+ and achievements. Perhaps the big draw would be co-op and the choices available within the campaign, even if they are a bit lackluster. Still, I think there’s some good replay value here. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Dying Light 2 (DL2) simply isn’t a great game. It lacks something that made DL1 so special. If I had to attribute this downfall to features specifically, it would be the narrative, and the lack of nighttime danger. 

DL1 didn’t really have an amazing story, mind you, but the narrative here is just terrible. As I got closer to the end, it was a struggle to push on and finish when I just didn’t care about any of the characters or the ending. While I like the touch of adding major decisions to certain parts of the story, even the outcomes just weren’t exciting enough to push the narrative to anything above mid-tier. 
As for the nighttime danger, it’s sad because the game is literally called Dying [i]Light[/i]. In the first game, nighttime often shifted the game from being an action game into a horror game. The tension and change were dramatic and noticeable. I never got the same feeling here. In DL2 night time is more of a stealth or parkour chase in the open world, or rummaging through samey-looking buildings due to the dangerous infected being outside. Even if you are spotted by a Volatile and a chase sequence begins, the AI is so dumb that it simply can’t keep up with the player. As long as you keep moving, there’s really nothing to fear. 

Just like DL1 though, the parkour continues to impress, and I do really like the traversal elements. But damn, if I only cared about the world at all. 
This is a hard one to recommend. As with most 5’s, I often struggle to recommend or not. In the end, I’m going to go with a recommendation. I love DL1, first-person games, RPG mechanics, and zombie games, so my love for the gameplay elements kept me interested enough to finish it, but barely. I would only recommend this if you loved DL1, and even then, prepare to be disappointed. 

[h1] [b] Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] [/b] [/h1]
[h1]Yes[/h1]
$60 is steep. I wouldn’t pay over $15 for this game. 

You can find my curator page here: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/Synik_GR

[h1][b] gameplay (mechanics/difficulty) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1] the general gameplay loop is typical of an open world game - completing mission objectives from one area to another. coming from dl1, there are some big changes, and most of them are not positive. the parkour remains the best part of the game, by far., and i think it’s improved a bit. jumping from the top of towers still gives that white-knuckle tense feeling, so it’s still great there. adding to the already good traversal mechanics are the paraglider and a grappling hook. though dl1 had a grappling hook, it’s not bound to a talent, you get it about 60% of the way through the story. the night elements have also changed. now, you have a timer that forces you to either use a consumable or reach a uv light before it runs out, else its game over. the rpg-like gear system has been expanded from just weapons to include gear. i didn’t find this very meaningful and the game could have done without it. speaking of talents, there are two trees - combat and parkour. the combat tree i found terribly boring, but the parkour tree was good. the difficulty is more on the easier side. the few times i died were all because of failed parkour attempts and not the combat. though with the combat, the volatiles will still mess you up. the regular zombies are just a hindrance, and often annoying as the runners constantly show up when doing basic attacks against any enemy [h1] [b] technical (graphics/performance) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1] i found the graphics to be this weird middle area between ps4 and ps4-era fidelity. the environments and world look great, if repetitive, but the character design and animations are a step lower. i played fully maxed and felt the performance was good. of note is the constant bugs. i hear this has been improved with post-launch patches, but i still ran into things constantly. the most egregious is the enemy ai. the ai would occasionally literally “turn off” and the enemies would just stand there. also the volatile chase sequences were a bit of a joke with how poor the ai is at following you 1440p @ 240hz | installed on ssd [h1] [b] audio – [4/10] [/b] [/h1] the music wasn’t great. in fact, i ended up turning it down because it was getting annoying. there’s also a sound effect, like sort of deep “ding” that plays when an event near you is active, which happens [b]all the time[/b]. i couldn’t find a way to turn it off, but it really takes you out of the game with the constant sound. the voice acting is good. [h1] [b] replay factor (longevity) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1] there is ng+ and achievements. perhaps the big draw would be co-op and the choices available within the campaign, even if they are a bit lackluster. still, i think there’s some good replay value here. review:
A decent game ruined by corporate greed.

The core game is genuinely good, and there’s a lot to enjoy in Dying Light 2. Unfortunately, Techland’s relentless monetization keeps dragging the experience down. The constant push to buy overpriced cosmetics is bad enough, with loading screens feeling more like advertisements than part of an actual game. And now they want to charge extra for spatial audio in their latest update? Seriously?

At some point, it stops feeling like a company supporting its game and starts feeling like a company squeezing every last penny out of its players. It’s a shame, because the game itself has a solid foundation, but these greedy practices make it difficult to respect the people behind it.

My advice? Stop rewarding this behavior with your money. If you absolutely want to play it, wait for a deep discount. Don’t pay full price just to be bombarded with monetization, and don’t encourage the idea that basic features and overpriced cosmetics are acceptable ways to milk a player base.

Speak with your wallet. The only language these companies seem to understand is money, and if enough players refuse to play along, they might finally reconsider these practices.

You have more power as a consumer than you think. Use it.

review:
This game is a direct downgrade from Dying Light 2, I preordered it with high expectations. On release u couldnt climb infinitely since climbing was tied to stamina which made no sense since Aiden is superhuman due to experimentation. Also nights had no volatiles roaming on release which was fundamentally flawed. The survivors are so incredibly unlikeable, and most of the characters regardless of faction are unrelatable and two dimensional. Also combat feels limb and weak in comparison to DL1. They addressed this later thank god with some updates and patches but the launch left a bad taste. 

The plot is pretty boring, convoluted, and dragged out and choices have no real meaning expect for a couple which I wont spoil. And exploring was kinda dumbed down since it marked everything on the map if u used ur binoculars, and even then the GRE buildings and GRE anomalies were the only ones worth totally exploring. Don't even get me started on how repetitive the GRE buildings are. I tried to gaslight myself into liking this game (hence my hours) but I really couldn't even after the updates to fix it. 

In summary DL2 Feels soulless and like an artificial playground, there's even huge yellow markers on the buildings telling u where to go like typically AAA slop. In comparison DL1 while not being known for its story, its still widely remembered and has emotional depth. Dl1 had an amazing deeply interconnected map with environmental story telling, and a soundtrack amplifying the atmosphere. I was so incredibly disappointed on release dyling light 2 didn't match the quality they achieved in 2015.

On the bright side the parkour is much better, human combat is actually fun, and there are more side quests than DL1 and a couple of them are really well written and have meaningful choices. Also the game is improving slowly its in a much better state now, most of my criticisms like easy night, limited climbing stamina, and combat have been fixed somewhat. I feel playing Dl1 and DLTB is much more worth ur while u aren't missing on much.

review:
Recommend if you care about gameplay, especially parkour and combat. I enjoyed both. Puzzles with capturing different structures weren't bad, but could be more varied. Most side quests are pretty generic and repetitive with nothing interesting to them outside of like two or three that actually had a pretty good story behind it.

Do not recommend if you care about the main story, which is a disaster. Most characters are insufferable (aside from maybe two) and make little sense in terms of their actions half the time. I kind of liked the way you are supposed to choose between the two factions but only very little of it had any larger impact story wise. That being said, I very much enjoyed that visually and functionally the city transformed based on your actions. Opening up the map and creating safe zones was one of the most enjoyable parts of the game.
With the severe cuts done to the prologue, some characters appear out of nowhere with no emotional impact. Aiden's main motivation is incredibly weak, especially since all you hear from Mia for most of the game is her yelling "Aiden babeiden" which just makes me want to kill her.

Some of the main story scenes and characters will make you want to slam your head into the wall if you care about the narrative at all. Thankfully, the story is a small part of the game and the gameplay does make up for it in my eyes.

I care about the story and the characters if they're good, if not, I can usually suffer through it for the sake of a good gameplay, so overall, I had a good time playing. Especially if I choose to believe that the entire last part was a fever dream. The game puts you back before those events anyway, if you want to keep playing, so it doesn't even matter.

review:
**A Fantastic Open-World Zombie Game with Tons of Fun!**

Dying Light 2 genuinely surprised me in a positive way. The parkour system is especially enjoyable. Running through the city, jumping across rooftops, and dodging zombies just feels incredibly satisfying.

The combat system is also impressive. Melee fights are brutal, the weapons offer plenty of variety, and combining parkour with combat creates some truly awesome moments. Things get even more intense at night, when the atmosphere becomes much more threatening and every mistake can have serious consequences.

The open world offers plenty to explore, tons of side quests, and many ways to develop and improve your character. Visually, the game also looks fantastic.

Of course, not everything is perfect. The story could have been better in certain areas, and some activities become repetitive over time. However, for me, the overall enjoyment of the game easily outweighs these flaws.

**Final Verdict:** If you enjoy zombies, open-world exploration, and action-packed combat, Dying Light 2 is definitely worth playing. It's a game you can easily sink countless hours into. The combination of freedom of movement, atmosphere, and survival elements is what makes Dying Light 2 stand out.

**My Rating: 9/10 – Highly Recommended!**

review:
和朋友联机玩了挺久，先说结论：单人能玩，多人一坨。
联机bug是真的一堆，还都不是小毛病。最典型的是坐电梯：电梯还在底下，人已经跑到电梯上面卡死了，在里面怎么走都出不来，只能让朋友拉过去传送，或者干脆退游戏重进。这不是偶发，基本上每次坐电梯都能撞上。
画面这块大问题没有，主要就是光影有一点点毛病。
最难受的是更新之后剧情被删了一大截。我和朋友联机打到后面，连结局的CG都没了，就这么没了！！！！！！！！！
道具系统也是折磨，一堆东西全得靠肝，任务又臭又长，点名贾伊，肝到怀疑人生。
剧情里的NPC一个比一个蠢，离了主角连路都不会走，这毛病跟一代一模一样。
十分我能给六七分，这六七分还是看在跑酷和画面上给的。
这游戏停止更新是好事，终于不用再被霍霍了，
（这是我本人的主观评测，如果你觉得不顺眼，点个踩就行了）
好了，说说这游戏的优点，这游戏创意还行，然后也有那种打击的爽感，音乐也是蛮好听的，但是跟一代的神作相比，差距还是蛮大的。
如果你是想史底入坑的话，直接入也还算可以，不亏，毕竟这玩意也蛮有意思的，那种晚上的紧张氛围感也十分的充足，就是这游戏真的有点像育碧的那种罐头游戏。
总的来说，这游戏史低入坑不亏，如果想体验那种跑酷，还有晚上躲夜魔的那种紧张氛围感的话，也还算可以，但是剧情的话就不用太指望了。

无休止的重复，复制粘贴的大楼，街道，不看地图都不知道自己在哪。

review:
抛开剧情、人设、中文配音、各类大小bug、操作手感、战斗表现等等，消逝的光芒2依旧是当下最好玩的丧尸末日跑酷生存游戏！
游玩到最终章还给我来了个死档的恶性bug，直接退档重来美美享受。
反派拉万的塑造非常成功，屡次想害死主角并且差点得手，站中间串四面八方也是主线剧情的核心冲突点；意气用事、冲动鲁莽、粗俗暴躁、毫无大局等性格特点也是经典反派形象了；外貌难评、脏话乱喷，还磕过药，一个底层混混形象跃然纸上；最后在主角的劝导下自我牺牲，这一反转大快人心，拉万终于悔过，尽显角色弧光。
剧情演绎到最终章才终于明白一名老父亲对女儿的深情，为了拯救女儿忍辱负重，不惜对自己生化改造，对抗各路妖魔神人，直到最后还想要利用导弹夷平城市，为人类铲除这么一个无药可救的鬼地方，正义之心令人动容。
相比第一代，这一作人类对抗丧尸末日明显轻松愉快得多，不仅幸存者众多，而且拉帮结派分成了三个阵营，还各自建立起了颇具规模的基地和各有特色秩序，而不用团结起来去对抗危险的夜魔和毒尸；不像第一部那样，幸存者都寥寥无几，安全点只能被迫建造在险峻的高处。看来到了第二部的时间点，人类战胜末日已经指日可待啦。
玩法上其实和第一部没有太大差别，钩爪的性能似乎更差一些，让人不爽。还给了不少多模式人任务，可惜单人玩家无福享受啦。（不要想着单人去挑战多人任务，牢）
建议打折到40元以下时，并且对第二部没有过多期待的游戏荒玩家再考虑慎重购买。好玩是好玩滴，毕竟消光系列确实有别于一大票经典丧尸末日游戏，据说相比刚发售时优化了很多，还给了一个拉万护眼版皮肤，现在肯定是能玩一玩的。坐等第三部困兽打折。

review:
困兽发售后过来评价下，首先游戏质量我认为对得起他的价格， 何况他经常打骨折。

2代我不喜欢的是华尔兹相关的主线剧情，因为很不喜欢最终BOSS是主角故人，对主角还心软有照顾之类的；最后是拉万非常不好看。除此之外的关卡和剧情体验沉浸感还是不差的，尤其是爬VNC楼和旁边几栋高楼的彩蛋非常刺激，让我记忆犹新，还有紧张的配乐延续一代的风格都是上乘。

二代的这套跑酷系统非常棒，配合关卡设计和地编非常有手感。当时讨论最多的话题是钩爪没一代好用了（主要是不能指哪飞到哪了当蝙蝠侠了），我觉得是二代的钩爪（蜘蛛侠吧😄）有一定拉进距离的功能，只是比较弱，但带来了新的玩法，更像是真正的绳索——如今发售3年了，跑酷系统被深入开发，大家也很少在对比一二代钩爪的好用与否了。

假如有一款游戏在消光的基础上，深入据点建设运营就更合我胃口了！

I want to love this game. On paper, it's everything I want from a game. But to be honest, I still don't get it. I appreciate the effort and the endless updates that have gone into this but there's something about it that just stops it clicking for me. 
I suspect it's the planets themselves. Despite there being lots of different biomes, every planet feels identical. Why does every planet have aliens on them? Why does virtually every planet have cat-bird-dog creatures wandering around? Why does every planet have relics? 
I feel like the entire idea of exploration would be to find these elements out in space and be a reward for exploration, but as far as I can tell, the first planet you get dumped on is fairly representative of the rest of the content.

review:
I bought this game when it originally came out and was so thoroughly disappointed that it was the last preorder I ever made. Now, I wait days after reviews drop to ensure I never run into that issue again.

Everything people were saying about the game back then was completely true. It felt incomplete, grindy as all hell, and you ran out of things to do as soon as you reached the final story mission.

What’s funny is that most of those criticisms are still somewhat true: the game can still feel grindy, the campaign still feels a little incomplete, and the gameplay loop can feel kinda rote by your 40th hour.

What hooks me now, though, is the massive amount of content added through updates and expansions, along with all the custom sliders. You can tune it into a hardcore space sim or turn down the difficulty and resource management to play it as a cozy, low-punishment game.

At the end of the day, I keep coming back for the procedural generation of planets and activities, as well as some of the most beautiful visual sights you can see every time you boot it up.

My opinion of Sean Murray has come full circle—I hate him now for a completely different reason: he won't let me give him more money after a decade of free updates!

review:
Great game, honestly! As someone who knows the struggle of making games like this, and how hard it is to store player data and keep planets looking like planets, I think the devs did a fantastic job. I could never reach this level, even with help. The game they’ve built over 10 years is amazing.

I’m a relatively new player, so I don’t know all the bits and bobs yet, but even when I’m older I bet it’ll still surprise me with new things, animals, and places. It has its glitches here and there, like the odd object floating in the air or clipping into the ground, but nothing major. Honestly, awesome game, and the devs did great to get it where it is today.

The graphics are beautiful too. The colours, the skies, and the planets look stunning, and they still amaze me even though the game is 10 years old. Every time I land on a new planet I stop just to look around.

There’s so much to do as well. You can explore, build bases, trade, fly around in your own ships, and play with friends in multiplayer. It even has VR support, which makes exploring feel even more real. The devs have also kept adding free updates for years, which is rare these days and shows how much they care about the game and the players.

If you check my PC specs, you’ll see basic, bottom-of-the-line parts you probably wouldn’t expect. If your PC is like mine and not too great, GET THE DARN GAME! I get 60 FPS in most scenarios. If you’re worried your PC is “too bad” to run it well, don’t be. The optimization is crazy! Like I said, 60 FPS is pretty good for my PC. Seriously, get the game. It has endless fun and activities, and I’m still not bored. Trust me.

Easy recommend from me!

And there is so much to explore out there! But I’ll let you, whether you’re a newcomer or an old player, figure those things out for yourself. Now go and happy exploring!

review:
I've been playing NMS since launch, and the laundry list of improvements is almost as vast as the universe it's set in.  The game is very enjoyable, but I do have some gripes with it.  

As an example, for all the things I can do in the game, it doesn't really feel like the game is willing to let me pursue any of it, as it's always lighting up my communicator with something else it wants me to check out, "Hey" it whispers, "Go check out that thing" and not even half way through doing so I receive another ping "Hey, there's this other thing that's really cool, go look at that".  Sometimes I just want to shut all quests off and pursue my own thing, but the game doesn't allow for that, and you will forever be interrupted with a to do list that is also nearly as vast as the universe in which the game is set. 

For another the hand holding, annoying as it is, doesn't even do that good of a job explaining what you can and cannot do.  It took far too long for instance, for me to realize that you don't need to do very much gathering of basic resources in the game beyond the first hour or so because you can duplicate most everything else with certain other resources.  Oxygen is a major player in this and is one of the very few resources you need to make sure you have tons of so you can just make the other stuff, but nowhere does the game inform you of this.  And the list is so large you kinda just need to keep the wiki open while playing the game.

These really are just minor gripes though and don't really change my opinion in terms of recommendation.

Easy purchase.

review:
First off I have bought this game twice now and have about 200 hours in it. With that experience I can comfortably say the game is fantastically well polished with immense amounts of content. Including story and quest lines, monthly expeditions, system battles, ship and planet hunting, freighter and frigate acquisition, base ship and freighter building, fishing, music making, (Pokémon like) fauna battles, garbage disposal, and much much more.

Some things to note are:
The initial quest lines are a bit extraneous but that is to be expected for being a decade old. Resource gathering, and travel are a major part in this game, and base building can be limiting for knew users, due to the required steps to get all of the currently obtainable components, and limited un-gliched placement options. While the addition of corvettes does certainly help this argument, if you are playing for the building sandbox experience, I would look else ware.

This game is definitely more enjoyable when playing with friends, due to the often repetitive nature, and long story lines if you choose to do them. The first few hours can feel slow, without sufficient amounts of currency or recourses, but it isn't too hard to obtain trillions of units, millions of nanites, and resourced are gathered just by playing, at witch the survival game feels similar to creative mode. 

Additionally Hello Games is now very consistent with there free updates, so it's not unreasonable to say you can expect new content to be dropped every few months. The downside is it can be a lot to pick up as a knew player. Though YouTube guides are abundant, and didn't take me too long to learn about three years back. 

Overall my experience with the game is great, however if you are running a lower end pc such as myself, you can expect a bit of struggle, though nothing that ruins the experience. (It is playable on Nintendo, and now mobile after all). I would personally prefer a bit more freedom when it comes to base building, and customization of such. - But hay that's what Minecraft's for.

If you have yet to give this game a try, I greatly recommend it. 7.8/10

review: I've had NMS in my library for years. I played it once waaay back after buying it at a price that was almost nil because of the bad luck and press the devs had received starting before 2020. I THINK I played it but it might have been Elite Dangerous (ambitious but .... nah). But it always forced itself on my radar. Then I watched an old (6 YEARS!) episode of Internet Historian on YouTube titled "The Engoodening of No Man's Sky" and as old as it was?  To tell the story It started off rough and then after watching Hello Games almost pushed up a giant & tall tree farmed by press and expectations (and ridiculous deadlines) into awkward and untenable positions as they climbed up and then fall hitting every branch on the way down? My heart felt for them. Having it (humorously) all broken down bit  by bit and everything that led to the fall from a height that they never expected to be at when they were shoved. Then get up, dust themselves off and get back to work making the game they promised with free updates and then go beyond adding more free updates (yes even this year as we recently experienced) for almost a decade after people had completely written NMS sky off? Is an incredible and dedicated come back story that is tribute to the perseverance of everyone at Hello Games making sure their vision and the expectations of the fans (and jilted early owners of NMS) were met and vindicated. And the history I watched (as I said) was 6 years old! Then I saw a new huge update coming for NMS and decided to wait for release and finally PLAY it. I have to say I had to watch a ton of tutorial videos on YouTube (after sifting through the videos that can date up to 10 years old). It was hard catching up as I noticed what huge international player base existed. I still have my questions about certain things large and small that I have to research or just put on hold unless it is a "need to know now" situation involving gameplay or mechanics. So.... is it good? Yes, it is great. Does it have a learning curve involving a buttload of information? Yep. But I am making my way just fine. Still have stop and do research if I can't find it on my phone right away. But therein is the greatness of this game. Making tutorial to a game that is always getting updates is HARD. But getting in the game and "getting caught up" to understanding how to play the current build is worth it. If you are on the fence or have been bored by other space exploration games that were ballyhooed as the next "Big Title" that turn sour? Don't let that or anything else stop you from jumping into No Man's Sky. So much has been endured by other players and so much work has been relentlessly put into this game. Odds are, you will experience that to your enjoyment. 354 hours in, I can safely say that I recommend this game..... Haha!

review:
No Man’s Sky is easily one of the best and most feature-packed space exploration games out there. The sheer amount of content, freedom, and things to discover is absolutely incredible. Whether you want to explore the far reaches of the universe, build an empire, become a space pirate, collect exotic creatures, or simply settle down on a beautiful planet and build a home, this game gives you the freedom to play however you want.

One of the most impressive features is the seamless transition between space and planetary exploration. You can fly directly from space down to a planet's surface without loading screens, fly like a plane through a planet's atmosphere, explore the terrain, and land practically anywhere you want. With the right technology installed, you can even land on water!

And there's no shortage of places to call home. You can build elaborate bases on planets and even underwater bases, construct outposts on massive asteroids, create your own space stations, and even build and customize your own massive freighters, which essentially serve as mobile bases you can take with you across the galaxy. You can also claim abandoned or NPC-operated space stations, renovate them, expand their interiors, and make them your own. If that's not enough, you can take control of planetary settlements and develop them into thriving little cities, making decisions that affect their growth and development.

The sheer scale of the universe in No Man's Sky is almost impossible to comprehend. There are 256 unique galaxies to explore, each containing roughly 4.2 billion star systems per galaxy, with an estimated 18.4 quintillion procedurally generated planets and moons across the universe. That's 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 possible worlds to discover! Each one can have its own landscapes, environments, wildlife, plants, weather conditions, and points of interest. No Man’s Sky’s universe is so unbelievably massive that you could spend your entire lifetime exploring and still barely scratch the surface. You'll never come close to seeing even 1% of its universe.

Exploration is a huge part of the experience. There are countless planets to discover, each with different environments, landscapes, wildlife, plants, weather conditions, and sometimes extremely dangerous hazards. You can discover strange alien creatures, scan plants and animals, uncover ancient ruins, search for buried treasures, explore abandoned facilities, and stumble across all sorts of unusual discoveries. There is also deep-sea exploration, alien ocean life, submarine vehicles and underwater base building. You can even name planets, creatures, and star systems you discover yourself.

Space exploration is also a huge part of the experience, and there's much more to it than simply flying between planets and star systems. You can discover and explore abandoned, procedurally generated derelict freighters drifting through space. These massive ships are filled with dangerous environmental hazards, hostile enemies, valuable loot, and technology waiting to be recovered.

There's also Space Hulk exploration, where you encounter massive abandoned ships that can be dismantled and salvaged for valuable resources, technology modules, and blueprints. Using a gravity gun built into your multitool and a ship-mounted tractor beam, you can literally tear these enormous wrecks apart piece by piece. But it's not without its risks! These operations can be extremely dangerous, as you have limited time to salvage everything before the wreck explodes. You also have to be careful about which sections you remove, because pulling the wrong components can trigger an explosion prematurely. It's a fun, high-risk activity that adds another exciting dimension to space exploration. 

There's also an incredible amount of variety when it comes to missions and activities. The game has numerous questlines, side missions, storylines, and challenges to keep you busy. There are special community events and limited-time Expeditions that introduce unique objectives and challenges, often rewarding you with exclusive ships, cosmetics, decorations, companions, and other items you can bring back to your main save.

Speaking of companions, you can hunt down, adopt, and tame all sorts of alien creatures. You can customize and genetically modify them, even introducing mutations to improve their stats and abilities. You can take them on adventures, use them as companions, and even participate in creature battles against other players and NPCs.

If you prefer a more relaxing experience, there's fishing, too! You can find different types of fish, collect them, and cook them into meals that provide useful buffs. There's also a farming system where you can grow a variety of plants and harvest resources to craft ingredients, create food, and produce valuable items. Cooking itself is surprisingly extensive, with all sorts of recipes to experiment with.

For those who enjoy ships and space combat, there's plenty to get into as well. You can discover, purchase, collect, upgrade, and customize different types of starships, each with its own design and purpose. From nimble fighters and explorers to massive haulers and exotic ships, there's something for everyone. You can engage in space battles, fight pirates, raid cargo fleets, participate in dogfights, and even become a pirate yourself. You can also assemble and command your own fleet of frigates, sending them on expeditions to gather resources and rewards.

One of my favorite features of No Man’s Sky is the incredible ship customization. You're not limited to simply buying ships and upgrading their stats. You can actually salvage and dismantle many of the smaller starships for their individual components, then use those parts to construct and customize your own ships. This allows you to mix and match different components to create a ship with a look and style that's entirely your own.

And then there are Corvettes, which take ship building to an entirely different level. These are much larger, fully customizable ships that you can purchase or build yourself by collecting the necessary parts and components. What makes them especially cool is that they're practically small mobile bases! You can walk around inside them, decorate their interiors, and install useful facilities such as crafting stations, healing stations, and storage. It's almost like having your own personal spaceship that you designed from the ground up.

There are also several different exocraft vehicles you can unlock, build, upgrade and drive across planetary surfaces. These range from fast, nimble vehicles (a bike or buggy) for getting around quickly to larger, more heavily equipped vehicles designed for exploration, combat, and resource gathering. And if exploring on land isn't enough, you can even build and pilot a submarine to explore the depths of those incredibly deep oceans, discovering underwater creatures, resources, and points of interest that you wouldn't otherwise be able to reach.

There's a deep crafting, gathering, and resource-management system that gives you plenty of reasons to explore. Mine resources, refine materials, manufacture technology, upgrade your equipment, improve your multitool, and constantly work toward making your character, ships, and bases better. There's also an extensive trading system, allowing you to buy and sell goods, take advantage of different galactic economies, and build up your wealth.

Multiplayer adds another layer to the experience. You can explore the universe with friends, build bases together, participate in missions, visit other players' creations, and take part in community activities. The game even has a shared social hub (The Space anomaly): A social hub where you can meet other Travelers, access missions, purchase upgrades, and interact with other players and embark on adventures together.

You can explore the universe with friends, build bases together, participate in missions, visit other players' creations, and take part in community activities. review:
With 150 hours under my belt and the Main quest now at "New Beginnings", I think a review is due.

Started playing a few months ago somewhat on and off; knowing of it's history and the comeback it's made since it's debut. Man is this a great experience. From the base building and resource collecting, to having freighters and space stations. From the Companion Battles to the Corvette building. This game has so much! Even the story while very simple in execution, was very enjoyable with it's message about finding purpose in an infinite universe. As for the main gimmick of the game being the scale of a galaxy with trillions of systems, I can enjoy it's scale and variety. Though there is one negative from this.

Every system and planet is procedurally generated so they should be unique (Which they are technically). But even if they are different, they do sometimes feel the same. Mostly barren planets with the creatures simply having certain assets mixed up. Maybe if there were a few planets every 30 systems that had a decently sized city or 2 on their surface with it's own gimmicks and events. Maybe if the animals had slightly better AI and more unique ways to interact with other than getting food or for Companion battles.

Even with these nitpicks, I still believe that the rest outweighs them. Also, I got this on sale when it's usually $60. It was $24 which was a steal. So it's definitely worth trying it out when they do start these sales. 

If you like space and Base Building games, it's a no brainer. I truly believe this is a comeback story that will go down in history for gaming. Here's to more updates to this huge game.

8.5/10

review:
该玩，入手绝不亏
也是近500h了该测评了，一口气玩到300h时就觉得有写必要了。
广而不深：四字包罗了无人深空更新了十年的弊端，它就像极了人类现在对宇宙的探索程度，像你就知道宇宙应该更加深邃，内容应该更加丰富，但现实却只有这些还只能如此，只能怒制作组不争，等你玩进去了玩到头了，你再回顾历程时会感些许失落，因为它本来可以做得更好。
首先该说说游戏历程：从生存挖矿建家起，逐步升空得船，再到探索星球发掘宇宙，挖掘bug彩蛋，加mod，整建模。
不得不说，现在入坑的玩家能站在先人凝聚的肩膀上几乎无所不能。有着随时能摇人救援的联机模式，也有各种便利的mod,。最棒的莫过于每当你有了新的需求，你总能在各平台收集到信息后，挖掘到这款游戏隐藏着的全新的宇宙，你会发现总有人能救你所急施与援手。像N网有着各种各样的mod与工具，一些绕不开的像，存档编辑器（替换飞船种子），任务进度器（解决bug），乐土、飞船探针程序等极大的改善了游戏体验。像oogc社区存有大量建模玩家耗费心血打磨的飞船建模，能免费下载。现如今简直就是这款游戏的黄金时代。
前100h游戏体验类似<深海迷航>，<方舟生存进化>之类的挖矿造家单机游戏，等做完主线解锁符文传送门能随时抵达玩家间留传的坐标时，这款游戏的魅力才会真正开始显现。
探索未知风景，寻找类地乐土建造小窝，跟随玩家坐标拿到造型帅气或者非常乐子的飞船，或者干脆狠下心装mod整建模打造真正自己想象的护卫舰。解决自动化矿场，发掘特性bug等等。这些内容足以撑饱你玩到300+h。再之后你就该去钻研钻研游戏外的神秘力量，想方设法的在玩家间留下些深刻印象了。
再说无人深空联机也不赖，作为一款半单机半网游的游戏，玩家的素质道德普遍较高，一方面是社区活跃的头部玩家们都有着极强烈的助人为乐精神，一方面价格的门槛筛选了不少人，再或许玩家们都见识过”无人“的深空会自发的维护”有人“的美好。像深空救援，异像乞讨，团建跳舞，建筑串门等等，这样互帮互助，偶尔整活，社区非常有活力，这样的氛围就是一大享受，现这样素质的社区可不多见了。
风景与奇观：各类星球环境风景迥然不同，一时半会根本看不完。再各玩家类似温馨别墅，整活建筑，甚至空间站奇观，景点真不少，就当是纯来联机旅游，也绝对不亏。像帝江号空间站，烟花星空间站，时序加速器，小明星红色教育空间站，教堂，酒吧，宾馆，别墅等等等等，无人深空有着大量会搞建筑会整建模的玩家，定会让你大开眼界的。
还有自建护卫舰：无数太空游戏玩家梦寐以求的功能，无人深空做到了，虽然大概率得借助mod甚至blender的力量才能完成心中的效果，但是他能啊，他真能开出去让别的玩家看到，能好好的在玩家聚集地炫耀一番。
总之，折后的无人深空超值，无论什么游戏你都能在这里找着影子，这里人很棒，游戏也不错。但我想如果你不是太空发烧友，可能没那么感冒，还有这半熟的玩法机制终归是要扣分的、、、
综合评价应给到四星半，次神作，该玩，入手绝对不亏。

review: 好玩，不卡利用bug慢慢去玩是很有意思的，我很喜欢这种慢慢积攒材料搭建生产线路，完善加工环境来达成高的价值产出，且本游戏产出的货币不像别的工厂产线类型游戏一样只是数值或成就，我认为这个游戏主要部分是探索建造，探索需要钱建造需要材料，所以赋予了这些材料产线极大的意义，探索部分我认为已经相当成熟了，可以探索的内容非常之多，玩家可以通过不断地探索拿到仅属于自己与众不同且稀有的飞船，武器，宠物，这让我很有成就感，产线搭建完善后拥有足够的建筑材料后搭建各种好看的建筑也非常有趣，整条游戏路程下来游玩自己所发现的所得到的所创造的所走过的路让我有一种说不出来的成就感，太空环境星系探险做的非常棒，以上这些都是建立在不利用bug锁生存模式才有的体会，再多人方面，当在探索的过程中遇到别人留下的建筑或者留言，在这个游戏的剧情背景下让我深刻的感受到那句话，“你不是孤身一人”这种设定非常沉浸，新的联盟系统更是可以把和朋友们一起努力探索发现的东西量化，更直观的看到我和朋友在这个游戏中获得的成就。以上是我认为的优点，但是我看了本游戏的一些宣发视频，我感觉官方后续更新可能不会很多了，这让我有些失落，因为我觉得还可以完善很多东西，例如此游戏的boss怪物太少了，我们拿到了很厉害的武器很厉害的飞船但是没有用武之地，联盟的竞争属性我认为也存在很大问题，我觉得游戏方应该多鼓励认认真真玩不卡bug不开修改器的玩家，现在的联盟排名囊括了所有类型玩家，锁生存不卡bug的玩家不可能和开着修改器或创造模式的玩家竞争。另外游戏的生存要素较少，最重要的就是bug太多了，如果这个游戏bug能少一点，没有那么多恶性bug就会是最棒的沙盒探索游戏，例如精炼机复制bug，这个bug真的很尴尬，有这个bug在可以说我搭建的各种产线都是无意义的，虽然可以说靠自觉不用，但是大多数玩家都在用的这种环境下，多少给真正好好玩的玩家有一定的落差感，不是一定要修复所有bug而是尽可能不要出现影响游戏的恶性bug，这个bug存在很久了一直没有修复，我认为这很影响游玩心态，另一方面我认为游戏应该继续完善一下材料生产部分，本游戏如果不卡bug这些材料产线我认为是很有必要的，但是目前的产线没有任何自动化成分，只是让材料能固定产出，而合成精炼部分没有自动化产线的功能，可能达成那种核融起爆机自动量产产线很难，但是起码精炼部分我认为可以完善一下，在货船加入自动精炼物品的功能，或许可以设计成那种控制面板例如货船内部装一个新的工作房间，这个工作房间可以统一调控货船上已有的精炼机，玩家设定好配方以及最低保有量后开始批量自动精炼，现在我每次缺钱都要一直反复机械的在熔炉里操作一个小时，另外我们需要更好的二氢产出路线。

最后这款游戏，我是真的很喜欢，也很感谢每一个在太空异象里面给我们萌新送物资的大佬哈哈哈哈。感谢爱我的女朋友圆了我儿时的梦，也希望早点上架安卓呢哈哈哈哈（虽然手机移植难度太大），我也希望官方了解到有那么一群人真心喜欢这款游戏，没有商业点评，没有避雷指南，只是真心想去和爱的人一起玩一款游戏。

review:
I'm surprised I never wrote a review for this game.

I could just write "It's great. Buy it now." and that alone would be a valid review, but I'll go just a little further.

If you've ever played the persona games and enjoyed making the most out of your time or wanted to be rewarded for planning ahead, this game is definitely for you. There may be some things that you can't plan for on your first playthrough until you find out they exist, but odds are you'll eventually want to start a new farm anyways, whether it be to try out different stuff, be more efficient, or check out something you may have missed the first time. 

HOWEVER, if you'd say you're more intrinsically motivated and do stuff just for the sake of it, that's fun too! I find the game intrinsically fun and it's made the game very replayable as a result. Unlike real life, doing just about ANYTHING can generate you money. Not all money-making methods are created equally of course, but you have options nonetheless.

The music and atmosphere in this game is great too. The winter themes specifically are my favorites.

There's also mod support, so you can make the game more fun by getting a modded farm layout, new NPCs, QoL mods, new crops, new areas, resprite characters, etc.

Try the game out sometime, even if none of this may have sounded cool to you. There's quite a bit to do in this game with plenty of polish, and I recommend not playing with the wiki or anything until later and you've found yourself wanting to go beyond what you've already figured out. If that never happens and you just end up mining 24/7 because you find it funner than anything else, that's cool too!

Unfortunately I don't find myself having the time to write as good of a review as I'd like, but hopefully this will do.

review:
In short, this game is well worth the money for offering a cozy farming gameplay, with a lot of optional challenges and assets that you can utilize to create your ideal country life.

As for a lengthy review however, i would like to mention about my first exposure to this game. It was around 2020 when i was watching a youtuber who playthrough of minecraft modpacks. Suddenly one day, he posted a video series about Stardew Valley. Seeing something far different from the usual contents that the youtuber made, i was pretty hooked and then watched the series myself. The vibe of the game felt so fun for me, someone who at the time still find farming flash games to pass the time, with its top-down perspective and colorful design. Sadly however, the series only lasted until summer yr 1, and the youtuber himself moved back to doing minecraft modpacks. Feeling a bit upset that i couldn't be able to see more about the game itself, and mind you, i myself back then didn't even know Steam's existence, which further makes me want to try the game myself.

Fast forward to 2022, i finally get myself a PC, and i get to know some "unusual ways" to "install" games onto my PC, so i tried to get Stardew Valley onto my desktop as quick as possible. Even though 2 years have passed, my experience with the game itself doesn't change at all. The vibrant color design, the cozy feeling of a country side farm, which further fuels my excitement to finally get an experience of the game. First time getting into the game, it was a bit tough for me to understand the story and how some buttons work. But by utilizing my experience from watching the video series, i did manage to plant some parsnips and greet all the villagers. Fast forward to day 3, i finally set my foot to the shore to meet the fisherman, and he gave me a fishing pole. And oh boy, i spent so many days fishing for extra cash. Many people in the community may consider the fishing minigame to be hard, but that's the thing that hooked me, the pain of trying to get a catfish at lvl 1 fishing was so worth it. After a while, i finally checked the mailbox after countless days of fishing, just to see that the very first event of spring, the egg hunt has already passed away. i was a bit upset over that fact, so i went to the central town to check the calendar if there're any other events coming up and slapped straight to my face was the community center cutscene with mayor himself. We went inside to see how ruined the community center was, and the mayor asked me to help repairing the community center, else he was gonna sell it to a nearby establishment. I thought to myself, "guess i should check this out after-" and right at that moment, a apple-looking creature appeared behind the mayor. My character was shocked, and so do I. Looking at how the mayor said i was probably sick or something made me so annoyed, since the creature is literally right behind him all the time, made me yelling "IT IS BEHIND YOU!!!" so loud that my mom came to check what i was doing. After some explanation to my mom, i went back to the game and checked around the community center, which was when i found a tablet that was written in whatever language that i couldnt even google translate it. After that, i went out of the community center and check the calendar to see the next event is the flower dance, which is in the 24th, and it was the 19th when i checked the calendar, so i went back to the beach to enjoy my past time with my fishing pole. The very next day, when i was about to do another fishing trip, i saw the the mail notification. I went to check it to see a letter from a wizard wanting to meet me at his hut in the forest. So instead of going to the beach, i went to the forest to check on him, The wizard was a bit rude to me, and gave me a strange brew that made me hallucinate a bunch of trees here and there. But after all that, he told me i could understand the tablet. Leaving the hut, i made my way to the community center to check the tablet again, and indeed i could read it now. The first tablet had a bundle that requires spring forageables, which i already have some at home, so i fulfilled the first bundle to unlock the next one. One by one, i get to see myself skipping so many aspects of the game. First was farming, i barely planted anything other than the first parsnips the mayor left for me to begin my farm. Second is mining, i wasnt paying attention that there is a mine i could work on. But hey, i left those all behind, because i liked fishing more than anything at the point. I  then again fished until the 24th of spring, where i participated my very first event. Seeing the villagers anticipating such a gorgeous event with beautiful flowers and happy dancing couples was fun, though it was sad that i couldnt get anyone to dance with me, since i spent all my time fishing, meaning my relationship with everything was low, aside from the fisherman himself, since i gave him some of my catches whenever he passes by. And after that event ended, i had to end my playthrough right there due to some complications within my family.

Now, moving to the year 2026, being in college with some free time and money i can spend for hobbies, i recall of Stardew Valley, so i grabbed the game on Steam when a sale happens. Even though i can buy the game and play it for however long i want, one thing that i miss having is the carefree mindset i had back in the day, to spend so much time fishing without a care of other aspects. Even though i missed the feeling, i still think that by reaching perfection and finishing the achievement tab, i have fulfilled my desire to experience the game fully back in the day.

All and all, grab the game and enjoy a cozy farming experience. 🏠

review:
For people who are looking to be creative in a very relaxing environment.

The progression can be very slow, but in some ways its good because that means even after hundreds of hours, there are things you haven't unlocked.

The side quests aren't all clear, but they do make the game more challenging. You need to learn what NPC's like to befriend them (or marry them), which is fun. 

The storyline wasn't really all that important, felt like it was something added just to give context on why your character is on a farm. (which is fair I guess, but still could have been more story related events imo)

The different seasons really make this game what it is. The mechanic of needing to go to sleep and the days progressing make you learn how important every minute of your day is. Did I replant all my crops? Did I visit all the NPC's I needed? When's the next town event? 

Definitely more of a relaxing game, but that doesn't mean its not challenging. If you're someone who struggles to manage their time and someone who puts random items in random chests when playing minecraft, you will definitely struggle here. Still worth the play.

Overall I really enjoyed the game, but would say for anybody like me who has to min-max and tries to be as effective as possible to just be wary of this game.
