This game, is just, unabashedly, one of the best 'cozy farming games' out there. Like, straight up. There's a reason that every new cozy game is trying to copy this one. Firstly, ConcernedApe made this game entirely on their own. That shit is so goated-

Sorry, secondly, this game has so much you get to do. If you don't like one aspect, try another. There's so many ways to make money and find enjoyment out of this. If you don't like mining, just don't mine. If you hate fishing with a burning passion, that's real! Go back to the farm. There are animals. You have pets and cattle and you can pet the animals.......... There's complexities like the seasons with different main crops and there's different sell prices and who doesn't love automation and such???

I'm just saying, if you loved the slime market from the slime rancher series you will LOVE selling stuff in this game. It is so fun getting into the numbers and how to maximize profits.

Not to mention, if you DON'T like something, this game has some of the easiest modding mechanics I've seen for a game besides, like, rain world or something. This game is only beaten out by 'subscribe to item on steam workshop'. THAT'S how easy!! If you hate fishing with a burning passion! You can make fishing easier! In many ways!!!!!!! There are MULTIPLE WAYS TO MAKE FISHING REDUNDANT! HOW COOL IS THAT-

Okay, I might REALLY like this game. But like......... You'll see why.........................

Any gripe you have with this game, can probably be solved by the modding community. They are some of the craziest of the modding communities I have seen for games. And that's assuming you even find a gripe to begin with, because gosh there is just so much to love about Stardew Valley...

AND IT WAS MADE BY ONE PERSON???????????????????????

其实我爷爷根本不会写字，不可能给我写信，而且他说的是陕北话，我听不懂。
上小学的时候，爷爷来家里住过一段时间。人很好的小老头，个子小小的性格很温吞，他总是不厌其烦地和我讲很多老家的故事，然而我能听懂的只是寥寥。有次我在看电视觉得他吵抱怨，他也不生气，用我听不懂的家乡话说着大概意思是“我说完这些就不说了”的话，然而没过多久他就回老家了。
后来，爷爷90大寿，爷爷的后辈乌泱泱的一大堆有些人我都不知道他们叫什么，都能给爷爷磕头，但是我不能，因为我是没出嫁的女娃，我不太懂。
再后来，有天爸爸急匆匆回了老家，爷爷给我打了一个视频，和我说了些让我好好学习之类的话。那天我们都觉得不会有事，因为爷爷没有生病，之前也有过这样的情况。可是爷爷当晚就离开了，他把他悉心保存的几百块钱全都给了我，但他有很多孙子的。
很多年过去，爷爷从来没有给我托过梦，更不会给我的农场打分，是觉得我不懂方言所以从来不找我说话吗？回老家上坟的时候，我看到旁边的山沟沟里面居然有一条比较宽的小河，爸爸告诉我河边的那些柳树都是爷爷一棵一棵亲手栽的。柳树茵茵，荞麦花也开得很好，如果我现在告诉爷爷在这里苹果28天就能结果，他一定会滔滔不绝的和我讲怎样真的种出一棵苹果树。只是那样的对话再也不会有，那些故事我再也不会知道。

review: （搬运一下之前小黑盒上的评价）嗯嗯。。玩了快两百个小时，但完美进度其实才40％左右。嘛。。。但无所谓啦，我会一点一点玩下去，最喜欢冬天了，但即使冬天结束了，我也会很开心地等待下一个冬天。星露谷给我一种家的感觉，一种活着的感觉。有事情要做的时候，努力到两点钟终于赶不及地在家门口晕倒了，没有事情做的时候，就在海边听着浪声钓一天的鱼也没关系。大家经常去小酒馆喝酒聊天，这一次笑得很开心的聚会，下一次还会有，赚的钱很少也没关系，下矿时不小心死掉掉了很多东西也没关系，总能慢慢来也总能重来。和塞巴斯结婚以后，冬天出门时，雪刚好落下来，他站在门口，我就会调好距离和角度拍很多照片，或者海边，或者其他时候，这些都会让我很开心。如果你真的存在，我肯定会很珍重地写很多封情书，先用白色的信封和粉色的心形状腊封，再颜色反过来用一遍。我也喜欢艾米丽，总觉得，如果是她的话，肯定会懂我平时莫名其妙说的话，会明白我为什么突然蹲下捡起一片叶子或者一块石头，艾米丽，你真的是一个很可爱的小女孩，我们是朋友这件事真的太让人高兴了，我喜欢你，如果我在的话就好了，夏天的晚上，我们可以一起穿着喜欢的睡衣，躲在被窝里说悄悄话，说到犯困得不行迷迷糊糊时再牵着手一起睡觉，第二天醒来时，我的手可能会搭在你的肚子上。前期赚的钱很少，但我也总会花很多钱在装饰和收集上，其实什么我都想收集，就放在家门口一列一列的箱子里，这个喜欢，这个也喜欢，什么都喜欢，大家都是可爱的，都有存在的意义。当时买了家具目录以后，我花了整整四天来装修我的房子，后面又装修了我的地窖，我的蘑菇洞，我的车站，到处都暖融融的。还有很多地方没有装，一点一点慢慢来、慢慢改变的感觉也好幸福。就这么一直一直下去叭，就让鹈鹕镇的雪一年一年地下好了，直到百分百完美也不停止。

review:
Slay the Spire relies heavily on luck. Two runs can be similar but aren't the same. There's a lot riding on your first Act because it doesn't matter what build you want to play, there's either going to be a build you get to play or a death if you don't make it come together. Along with deck order being pre-determined as a fight starts(a wise move to prevent save scumming, just noting the mechanic) it's a management game long term more than anything. In order to be truly good at the game, you need hours and hours and dozens and dozens of runs for true progress. Because the game is geared on that it really feels more like I'm zoning out hoping for a good run or managing a dead run mid to late game. While it does excel at small rewards to keep the player invested including progress on death I won't pretend it's a style of gameplay I'm super into. But for it's genre I think it's done very well.

This isn't my genre but I think it excels at what it wants and if you get it on sale specifically you'll be pleased for at least your first dozens runs.

Tips and tricks for the interested:

-Large decks are usually a trap, burying the best cards or your intended build under energy wasters. 15-20 cards or less is my advice

-I almost always try to gun for Events and Rests over Elites after Act 1

-During Rests, if you can, I'd recommend upgrading cards. Specifically any beyond the basic Defense and Attack you start with

-Avoid bias with your deck and adapt. Re-evaluating even endgame can help win your fights, and never expect to get the exact build you are looking for

review:
The other benchmark. FTL and this one are the two games I hold every roguelike up against, and most of what comes out does not make it. People call this a deckbuilder and it is, but I think that undersells it. It is a decision game. The cards are just how the decisions show up.

What Slay the Spire understands, and what most of its imitators never do, is that every card you take is a bet on where the run is going. Not a bonus. A bet. Take the big attack and you are committing to a deck that wants to end fights fast and you had better find the draw to support it. Skip it and you are saying you trust the defense you have not found yet. Fifteen floors later, that one pick is the reason you won or the reason you are staring at the heart with no answer, and here is the part that matters. The game is clear enough that you always know which pick it was. You never lose to something you could not have seen. You lose because you made a bet and it did not come in, and you can trace the line back to the exact floor where you made it. That clarity is rare. It is the whole reason the game is replayable, because every loss is a lesson instead of an excuse.

The other thing it gets right is that nothing in it is wasted. Every character is a different game with the same rules. Ironclad plays like a brawl, Silent plays like a trap, Defect plays like an engine, Watcher plays like you are holding a loaded gun the entire fight. The relic system means that even two runs with the same deck plan feel completely different, because the relics are what change the math. And the ascension ladder is the best difficulty system I have seen in anything. It does not make enemies spongier. It takes things away from you, one at a time, until the run you used to cruise through becomes a real fight again. There is always a next ascension and there is always a reason to go for it.

There is no story to speak of and it does not need one. The run is the story. You remember the run where you found the one relic that turned a dead deck into a monster. You remember the run where you had the heart at ten health and drew the wrong card. Those are the stories and they are better than most games manage with a script.

Honest criticism. The art is functional and that is being generous. The game is a decade old and it looks it. And if you do not like thinking three turns ahead you will not like this, because that is the entire game and there is no mode that lets you skip it.

I own the sequel now and I have been putting real hours into it. But when someone asks me where to start with roguelikes, this is still the first thing I say, because everything that came after is standing on it. Shout out to Mega Crit.

Weird thing is, I like this game. Played it a lot. Have not left a review before because I thought they might sort out the problems with one of the DLCs or something, but I have been waiting for them to fix the AI of your dudes in single player forever now. 

Several DLCs released and you still have to mod the game to fix the AI and that only works a little. They will not respond to commands sometimes, will not face angles properly etc. Some rooms they are fine but others they will just not know what to do. They will flashbang themselves and you. You can have four fellas stacked up on a door, guns ready, someone opens the door before you breach and two of your men will be dead before they decide to shoot the guy. Sometimes they will just get confused by a door being open inwards or something and take about 6 seconds to get into the room after a flashbang. Very frustrating that you feel like you cant let them do anything reliably. Also I wish the gas was a bit more powerful but its probably realistic haha.

Everything else in the game is cool, guns are really good, shooting feels great. Love shooting peoples hands off with shotguns. The sound is fantastic, music it good. Only performance problems I had were in the last level for where I got some weird lag spikes, other frame drops were not that bad and my pc is pretty old with a 2060. 

But very cool game, just cant recommend the single player. If you intend to play this with friends though that wont be a problem of course. So negative but good game lol. Hopefully they fix it one day but I doubt it at this point.

review:
It's overall a reasonably good game with most of its systems being well-fleshed out. However, the balancing needs some work, and the enemy AI needs to have their crack taken away. It's been almost 3 years now, people have been constantly telling VOID that the AI are skynet terminators, and they have stubbornly refused to acknowledge this and fix them. So I'll stubbornly refuse to give this otherwise good game a positive review, because it is ruined by atrocious AI, which become way worse on Hard difficulty and require bug abuse or incredible luck to finish missions.

Other problems include the SWAT AI being complete nincompoops by comparison, excessive suppression effects on the player yet enemies suffer no such thing as suppression, ridiculous and unrealistic weapon sway while moving, no rubber bullets for the dozens of guns we have, some traps being virtually invisible and impossible to manually disarm (either due to being hard to see or because some particular doors don't swing out far enough), bomb vest suspects can still get animation locked (stun one by any means, then start disarming the bomb before they recover), and there really isn't a good reason why we should have to take terrorists alive; and any armed suspect in general conscious; for the best score. Many of the missions also don't have great variety and some missions are more linear than they really need to be, especially Relapse. If you're going to make it so that players have to restart a mission over and over again to clear it, why not at least allow for more variety and routes?

Finally, the DLC are overpriced and the base game doesn't really have enough content to justify buying at full price. No, the taser does not need to be nerfed again. It was fine after the first time, stop nerfing it.

review:
I Came for a Tactical Shooter. I Left a Different Person.

There are games you play to pass the time. There are games you play because you're bored. There are games you play because your friends are online.

And then there is Ready or Not.

I genuinely don't know how to put into words what this game has done to me. I installed it expecting a tactical shooter. I expected guns, missions, suspects, some good old-fashioned door kicking and perhaps the occasional questionable decision from my teammates.

I was not prepared.

I was not prepared for the silence before entering a room. I was not prepared for the sound of footsteps on the other side of a door. I was not prepared for the moment when a suspect refuses to surrender, when a teammate shouts for cover, or when everything goes horribly wrong in a fraction of a second.

But most importantly, I was not prepared for the emotional journey.

Every mission feels like it means something. Every corner feels like it could be your last. Every time I hear someone shout "POLICE, DROP YOUR WEAPON!" I feel a little part of my soul leave my body.

And yet, I keep coming back.

I have laughed. I have screamed. I have questioned my intelligence. I have stared at a loading screen wondering where my life went wrong. I have watched my carefully coordinated tactical operation collapse because one person forgot to check a corner.

But I have also experienced moments of genuine brilliance.

The feeling of clearing a building with your squad, covering each other, communicating properly and somehow making it through an entire mission without everything descending into absolute chaos is something I struggle to find in any other game.

There is something special about a game that makes you slow down. A game that makes you think before you act. A game that reminds you that sometimes the most important thing you can do is NOT pull the trigger.

And that is what makes Ready or Not so special.

It isn't simply about shooting people. It is about restraint, responsibility, teamwork and the weight of the decisions you make.

The atmosphere deserves its own appreciation. The sound design, the lighting, the environments, the voice acting, the tiny details scattered throughout every mission. Everything contributes to an experience that can be genuinely uncomfortable in the best possible way.

There are moments where I have genuinely forgotten that I am sitting at a computer playing a video game. I am no longer thinking about my keyboard or mouse. I am thinking about the room ahead, the people inside it and whether my squad is going to make it out.

And then someone on my team gets stuck in a doorway.

Immersion shattered. Humanity restored.

I also want to acknowledge the people behind this game.

To the developers, artists, sound designers, programmers, writers, animators and everyone else who contributed to this project: thank you.

I know that making a game is not easy. I know that behind every little detail that players might overlook are hours of work, problem-solving, frustration and dedication.

Most players will probably never stop to appreciate the amount of effort that goes into making a single mission feel believable. They might never think about the sound of a distant gunshot, the positioning of an object in a room or the way an environment tells a story without saying a single word.

But somebody made those decisions.

Somebody cared enough to make those details exist.

And somebody, somewhere, spent an unreasonable amount of time making sure that a door opens in a particular way.

I hope those people know that their work matters.

Because it does.

Games like this remind me why I love gaming in the first place. Not because of graphics, not because of achievements, not because of how many hours I can put into something, but because of the experiences that games can create.

The memories.

The ridiculous moments with friends.

The missions that go perfectly until the final thirty seconds.

The missions that go catastrophically wrong from the very first door.

The times when everyone is silent because something genuinely terrifying just happened.

And the occasional teammate who thinks a flashbang is a substitute for basic communication.

I don't know how many more hours I will spend playing Ready or Not. I don't know how many more missions I will complete, how many more times I will get shot through a doorway, or how many more times I will have to explain to my squad that perhaps we should try a slightly different approach.

But I do know one thing.

Years from now, when I look back at the games I played, I suspect Ready or Not will be one of the ones I remember.

Not because it was perfect.

Not because every update was flawless.

Not because every mission went according to plan.

But because it made me feel something.

And that is becoming increasingly rare.

So, to everyone at VOID Interactive: thank you for creating something that people can genuinely lose themselves in. Thank you for putting so much detail into a game that could so easily have been just another shooter. Thank you for giving us something worth talking about, laughing about, getting frustrated with and returning to.

And to whoever designed the AI that can somehow identify my exact location through three walls, a filing cabinet and what I can only assume is divine intervention:

I hope you sleep well.

You have ruined my life.

In the best possible way.

10/10. Would risk my entire squad's wellbeing again.

Ready or Not. Because apparently, I wasn't.

I gave this game a negative review because apparently players are expected to fix it themselves!

If, like me, you're experiencing severe LOD (Level of Detail) and texture pop-in issues, here's a potential fix:

Press  Win + R and enter:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ReadyOrNot\Saved\Config\Windows`

Open Engine.ini and add the following lines:

[SystemSettings]
r.ViewDistanceScale=5
r.StaticMeshLODDistanceScale=0.1
r.SkeletalMeshLODBias=-2
foliage.LODDistanceScale=3

Save the file and restart the game.

These settings increase rendering distances and force higher-detail models to remain visible at greater distances, reducing noticeable LOD transitions and object pop-in.

Be aware that this may reduce performance depending on your hardware, although I personally haven't noticed any measurable difference.

It's ridiculous that players have to resort to manually editing configuration files to fix such obvious graphical issues. This is something the developers should have addressed themselves, not left to the community to figure out.

review:
I love this game, but I get so insanely irritated because of some really specific quality-of-life and gameplay issues that make me want to claw my goddamn eyes out. Those being:
>Non-lethals will sometimes do literally nothing to enemies, sometimes they'll instantly stun them, but other times it'll take dozens of shots for them to finally give up. Lovely when your own weapon is completely unpredictable.
>This game is ungodly buggy. People clip through floors, weapons clip through floors and walls, NPCs get stuck crawling through walls or just stand outside of cabinets infinitely. You'll also sometimes notice pressing "F" to restrain does nothing except make the prompt flash.
>When you lose a mission you still have to sit through a score breakdown screen when you probably already know why the mission is unresolved / failed. (You died, duh.) This isn't annoying on the face of it, but when you're replaying a difficult mission it gets grating fast.
>Having to track down the final civilian who's probably sprinting around the map or hiding in some stupid corner is really annoying. I get it means you probably didn't sweep thoroughly enough, but having SOME sort of hint after you've cleared all the enemies would really make me NOT want to blow my brains out.

Minor Gripes:
>Stealth is not really an option. Enemies, even on standard, immediately see you even if they're not looking at you. They'll just yell, "FIVE-O" and sense you or some shit. It really makes silencers completely pointless and lame.
>Ranged weapons are kind of useless because 99% of this game is tight corridors, wish there were some missions more centered around ranged combat, but then again there'd be almost no way to non-lethal consistently from a distance so who knows.

Anyway, skill issue i get it, lol.

review:
Love this game. This is my favorite tactical shooter to play single player, and has no doubt revolutionized the tactical shooter genre in many ways, but the friendly AI needs some sorely needed updates. The amount of times I'll tell my team to do something for them to bug out and not do it is crazy. The friendly AI also seems to be part time pacifists, sometimes holding their lethal gun fire on suspects when they are being shot at, and abstaining completely from shooting noncompliant armed suspects trying to evade orders when my team have non lethal weapons like my beloved beanbag shotgun. Besides this, none of your team mates can throw a grenade into a room to save their lives, consistently throwing them right on the threshold or the side of the door where the cops are.

review:
Squad AI is quite neglected, making singleplayer a rote and frustrating experience. SWAT members sometimes fail to react to being shot, cannot throw grenades properly, and demonstrate all the wrong initiative. Because squadmates don't understand how to safely take and secure a room - they do not recognize even the most obvious dangers and occupy vulnerable positions while monitoring the least dangerous angles - the player is forced to use wedges as a final recourse. And when a danger evolves into an active threat, they do not respond to that either. They usually only react to what is in view (and sometimes not even that). Thus, gameplay becomes a process of using wedges on every single door, as it is the only way you can guarantee security. Micromanagement rather than team coordination.

But even that is difficult to do safely. Sometimes squadmates do not follow orders, and when they do, it can lead to undesired behaviour. To place a wedge, the door must first be closed. The squadmate can close the door, but if there's a downed suspect or some evidence on the other side, they may choose to reopen the door to collect the evidence/restrain the suspect (possibly dying in the process, which is often followed by you or the rest of the team dying). So it is safest to close and wedge doors yourself, but again, you cannot trust your teammates to protect you in the process without specifically ordering them to do so, which - since you are often exposed from multiple angles - requires several orders for something that any human would have done automatically and without hesitation. In the time it takes to set up those orders, a threat may have appeared from any of the thresholds you are trying to secure. But all of this could have been prevented if the AI was aware of thresholds and could identify them as threats and treat them accordingly.

A big part of the issue is that most things the AI does seems to be baked into the map. Often the squadmates will delay carrying out an order because you are standing in their magical golden path when they could just walk around you while respecting your line of fire. This is sometimes fatal, as you are usually trying to provide security for them, and moving would not only endanger but often you as well. Or you may even be trying to engage suspects and they might cross your line of fire, or force you to move (destabilizing you) because you consider their task time sensitive. It isn't clear if those paths are baked or calculated, but they are too inflexible all the same. The angles that the AI hold after clearing, however, appear to be baked. Reasonable for performance and consistency. But the algorithm used to bake them isn't aware of lines of sight; It is aware of doors. The most obvious example of this is cases with windows or counters such as the lobby of the Mindjot Datacenter. The reception desk is partitioned into a separate logical room (it has a door, so this makes sense). But the reception desk "room" has a door to the kitchen. The squadmates don't know that the kitchen effectively connects to the lobby, so they don't cover it. This frequently results in suspects coming through the kitchen into the reception area, which is not covered by any teammates, leaving a nasty surprise for the player. This is compounded by the fact that two squadmates will always be standing in the corner watching the corridor door and the double doors. Those squadmates are immediately cut off from the team should a suspect move to the reception desk. This makes an otherwise safe and obvious room for double entry quite perilous, all because the squadmates can't "see" what is obviously the second most dangerous door in the room.

clearing, however, appear to be baked. reasonable for performance and consistency. but the algorithm used to bake them isn't aware of lines of sight; it is aware of doors. the most obvious example of this is cases with windows or counters such as the lobby of the mindjot datacenter. the reception desk is partitioned into a separate logical room (it has a door, so this makes sense). but the reception desk "room" has a door to the kitchen. the squadmates don't know that the kitchen effectively connects to the lobby, so they don't cover it. this frequently results in suspects coming through the kitchen into the reception area, which is not covered by any teammates, leaving a nasty surprise for the player. this is compounded by the fact that two squadmates will always be standing in the corner watching the corridor door and the double doors. those squadmates are immediately cut off from the team should a suspect move to the reception desk. this makes an otherwise safe and obvious room for double entry quite perilous, all because the squadmates can't "see" what is obviously the second most dangerous door in the room.

review:
ai队友有些神经，虽然现在来看，行为逻辑已经好了很多，但也是有缺陷的。
比如，在转角击毙一名敌人，掉落的枪支会让ai队友强制性去收墙，从而导致被转角后的敌人袭击，关键被打了，ai队友也不知道停下来，就这么送人头。
还有，命令ai队友进入房间排查危险，个别情况下，会有一个ai队友绕一大圈，跑到后门去，他还就真进去了。我在前门等了许久，这三个ai队友也没反应，直到房间里传来枪声，我自己进房间去看，才发现有一个ai队友跑后门去了
两年前，这个游戏的第三章地图，在别墅的后花园小山上有一个房间入口，连通地下室的那个，ai队友在上那个小山的寻路有问题，容易卡住，两年也没看改的
其余就是那人质太傻逼了，还一个fuck的叫，叫他妈叫呀，真想弄死他，还乱跑，要找半天
最后，如果你是真心喜欢cqb或特警反恐作战，那非常推荐，无论是枪械手感，还是游戏逻辑，都是目前能找到反恐题材中最高的

review:
小时候做梦都想玩的游戏
可以说是目前的战术类游戏行业楷模，美中不足之处便是BUG较多
每次大更新就是对你的MOD进行大肃清，时不时云服务器储存的存档全部丢失让你从头再来
更招笑的是在20年代居然还在用P2P，联机全凭房主网络，搞不好你连进都进不去
部分地图设计规模巨大，地图完全是摆设，加上阴暗地图戴久了夜视仪会头晕脑胀
全体队员包括自己全都是老寒腿，走路慢的比不上80高龄老太婆，对方恐怖分子一个个跑的跟短跑冠军一样，人机队友各个都是靠关系进来的，精准度极低，对面跟开了锁头一样
人质还到处乱跑，消灭敌人5分钟、找人质30分钟
指挥官模式很有意思，高难度下还是别尝试了，这游戏更建议多人玩
有成就有中文无卡牌
有待改进

蛮硬核的战术射击游戏，难度越高变数越大，看似投降的嫌疑人若不及时逮捕，很有可能转头拔枪突突你，甚至在逮捕过程中也有小动作，敌人设计的还是挺好的，就是指挥官模式下AI队友的智力还有待提高，经常出现五个人挤进一间小房间导致几个人卡死在里面半天出不去，平民也可以优化一些，经常出现让ta离开作战区域结果ta乱开门导致被嫌疑犯突突空悲切的情况，真的很火大，再者就是地图理解很重要，一些比较难打又很大很复杂（例如葡萄藤之躯，复发，新美国）一般都会翻车好几次，记一下NPC刷新点位，炸弹位置等等多来几遍就OK，虽然打完容易打出PTSD，但无妨这是一款很优秀的作品
推荐打折的时候入手，Dark Water和Boling Point这个DLC里的三个任务都偏快节奏偏难，不建议新手购买，最好是熟悉基本操作和适应本体游戏，完成第一个dlc家园入侵再尝试购买，偏娱乐的话就别买了

review:
Black Myth: Wukong is a compelling soulslike/action game, however, I personally had a few issues with the game. 

The story is set after the journey to the west, but I found it confusing to follow for the most part. 

Level design peaked for me in the second location and steadily declined thereafter. Levels follow a very linear pattern but don't feel particularly rewarding for exploring the few side paths as most of the time you will find upgrade materials that you end up having an abundance of by the end of the game anyway.

The bosses felt like a quantity over quality situation. The major bosses are very well designed and were frankly really cool, but the other 80% of bosses felt like fodder and didn't really do much for me. There is also a major difficulty difference between every single boss except for the final boss and the [spoiler] secret boss [/spoiler], which feels inconsistent.

Overall I give the game a 6.5/10, I do recommend it as the experience is quite good, but I wouldn't be urging anyone to pick it up as a must play.

review:
Black Myth: Wukong was one of the biggest surprises I've played in recent years. Going in, I expected a solid action game, but what I got was a visually stunning adventure packed with memorable boss fights and incredible set pieces.

The combat is easily the highlight of the game. It's fast, satisfying, and gives you plenty of abilities and transformations to experiment with. While many compare it to Souls games, I found it more accessible and focused on spectacle rather than frustration. The boss battles are some of the best I've experienced in an action RPG, and every major victory feels earned.

Visually, the game is absolutely breathtaking. The environments are rich with detail, the creature designs are fantastic, and the Unreal Engine 5 visuals truly shine. Playing in 4K was a treat, with many moments that looked straight out of a CGI movie.

The story, inspired by Journey to the West, is intriguing and full of mystery. While some parts can be difficult to follow if you're unfamiliar with the source material, the atmosphere, cutscenes, and world-building kept me invested from start to finish.

Performance-wise, the game ran surprisingly well. I experienced only minor stutters here and there, and overall the experience was smooth and polished.

Bottom line: Black Myth: Wukong proves that Chinese developers are absolutely cooking right now. The level of quality, ambition, and attention to detail on display here is incredible, especially for a studio's first AAA title. It may not reinvent the genre, but it delivers stunning visuals, excellent combat, and unforgettable boss encounters. If you're a fan of action games, this is an easy recommendation. I thoroughly enjoyed it. 🔥🐒🎮

review:
it took me 66h to 100% the game and i definitely have some thoughts

The game is visually stunning with or without ray tracing (i played without), the environments feel alive, the sound design helps bring it all together and immerse you fully into the game. 
The enemies are tough but you always feel like you are learning and not a single enemy felt unfair (Except Earlang, f that guy) and with enough tries you will beat them, im fairly new to the souls like genre and i could beat the game fairly easily so i dont think its too difficult, which is good. 
The story is quite confusing at times, or maybe its because i played the game over multiple weeks but the combat was so much fun that i honestly didnt really pay too much attention to it.
There are quests and missable things in the game which are not explicitly stated anywhere and you only understand with clues from dialogue (i used a checklist since its easier especially since there is no way i can beat the game 100% in one sitting) but i see this as a positive and it incentivizes exploration.

Now some of the bad
Some places that look like you can walk over/trough are blocked by invisible walls (not super common but i did get stuck in a few places in Ch4).
if you get close to ledges that you are able to jump off, it will automatically make you jump, meaning some parts of the game with tight bridges are super annoying because a slight misstep will make you jump off and die.
Sometimes id get random visual glitches that would fix themselves in a few seconds but it would mess with vision
Sound would cut out if tp to a shrine to farm enemies.
Speaking of RNG drops, i got very lucky and pretty much got all RNG drops in about 20-30 mins of farming but ive seen some people having to farm for hours, this for me takes away from the game a bit as i want to explore not hit the same guy for 20mins straight.
The Pagoda part of Ch3 does not have enough save points, especially with the debuffs on my first playthrough it took me about as much time to beat Pagoda as it did the rest of the chapter, some people might enjoy it but for me it was the worst part of the game.
Some Achievements would not pop properly so i had to do alot of extra boss fighting in NG+ purely due to the achievement not working. 

I did not touch the Challenge modes, though they are there and give some special weapons, but as it was not needed for 100% and im not super into tournament style battles i left it alone.

Overall a great experience that im glad i came back to finish, i started the game back in 2024 shortly after release and did not enjoy it at all, but today i can say that it is worth a play and has inspired me to look into the books that this game is based upon.

review:
# One of the Best AAA Games I’ve Ever Played

*Black Myth: Wukong* is easily one of the best AAA games I’ve played, and it has definitely earned a spot in my Top 10.

The game is heavily story-driven and draws inspiration from *Journey to the West*. I recommend learning a little about the original story beforehand if you want a deeper understanding of the game's narrative and characters. However, even if you go in completely blind, like I did, you'll still have a fantastic experience.

For me, **the combat and boss designs are among the absolute best parts of the game.** Every encounter feels exciting, and the variety of bosses keeps things interesting throughout your journey.

One thing worth mentioning is that the game isn't as punishing as many other Souls-like games. In fact, I wouldn't consider it a traditional Souls-like, despite what some people might expect. That doesn't mean it's easy, though! Certain bosses can be genuinely challenging, and you'll sometimes need to experiment with different builds, abilities, and strategies to overcome them.

The game is also packed with secrets and hidden content. There's no shame in looking things up on YouTube if you get stuck or want to discover something you missed. Even after completing the game, there's still plenty to explore, and a second playthrough can be well worth your time.

**Overall, I absolutely love this game.** It's easily one of my favourite gaming experiences and has secured a place in my personal Top 10.

I would definitely recommend *Black Myth: Wukong* if you have the patience, enjoy action RPGs, and want a game that offers fantastic combat, memorable boss fights, and a satisfying level of challenge. Absolutely worth getting!

The main issue was that Wukong’s hair often looked dotted, grainy, or distorted. Foliage and thin environmental details also looked unstable and shimmery. Lowering sharpening made the character’s face and clothes look too blurry, while increasing it made the visual artefacts stand out even more.

The combat and world seem promising, but I spent too much time trying to fix the graphics and could not enjoy the game in this state.

Black Myth is a fast paced, high octane, risk and reward game that is insanely addictive to play.

review:
Journey to the West is one of my favorite mythology tails, so I knew I'd been playing this sooner or later.
Sadly, 20ish hours in I just don't feel compelled to progress further.

There are many aspects I like: for one, haven't played a combat this satisfying since Ghost of Tsushima. Mastering your own evolving skills and learning enemies patterns really feels rewarding - choreography and cinematics are great and I never felt frustrated once.
Obscure lore is big plus for me in the way it's presented and delivered. Voices in the wind, riddles and a lot of hinting to Sun Wukong's myth are amazing. And visuals are really top notch.

But there are some huge problems that such bright sides can't hide for long.
There are basic upgrades hidden behind missable NPCs quest.
There are missable bosses and encounters that lock themselves until NG+ without any hint.
Most things don't have any trigger to signal the player something has changed, or that his actions had an impact - resulting in potentially missing stuff you actually unlocked or progressed towards.
Some bosses / encounters straight up negate some builds, not letting you use whatever playstyle suits you the most.

These points are straight up bad design choices that ultimately hinder the two best aspects of this game, leaving it carried by its visuals. If you like souls-inspired boss rushes, I'd suggest buying at a fairly discounted price.

review:
Incredible game. Not that difficult (first tried 90% of bosses), but it doesn't have to be hard because it is so fun! I knew nothing about Journey to the West, aside from 3 things:
- Wukong is a mischievous monkey that achieved Buddhahood
- He has a boar-human friend
- He is the inspiration for Goku
So it was a bit weird seeing a bunch of talking animals, but you can still easily follow the story. So you'll still have fun. Banger music, especially "Listen Not". 

The game runs fine?????? With my laptop, the gameplay (the important part) runs smoothly on the default setting, but the cutscenes stutters a bit, which is odd since it is a cutscene? The game also has this weird afterimage effect when something moves, I don't know if it is normal, but I have seen other peoples' gameplay with the same effect.

The combat is super fun. It might get a little stale using the same weapon the whole game (I used the Thrust Stance all the way through) but it just makes the final boss more fun because [spoiler]he has your moveset BUT cooler and you will easily recognize these moves and lock in, due to already being familiar with their game[/spoiler]. Despite that, my favorite boss is actually a secret boss [spoiler]Erlang Shen[/spoiler], which was also the hardest boss here (22 attempts). He is super fun and has a great rhythm to the fight, which is really enough to sell me on a fight.

This game feels like it wants to be a Boss Rush with how many bosses there are, and it great! All bosses are well designed and fun to fight, except Yellow Loong, and Bishui Golden-Eyed Beast, those 2 are dookie and not fun. The Fire Mantle only makes the fight bearable, not fun. Honorable mention to Cyan Loong, but once you figure out his tell for his stupid twirl forward attack, he becomes easy.

If you plan to 100% this game, you are required to do a ng+, at least up to chapter 5 and fight the Bishui Golden-Eyed Beast again for some materials. LITERALLY I DON'T WANT TO FIGHT THAT THING AGAIN!!! I AM DONE WITH FIRE!!! 

-1 for the Bishui Golden-Eyed Beast.

VERY fun game. I may not get all the references, but I am glad the devs made a game THEY want to make. I would recommend this to most people who wants a fun action game.

As Indonesian Chinese who grow up watching TVB 1996 & 1998 Journey To The West (also known as Kera Sakti in Indonesia) and familar with JTTW lore, I just want to say......I LOVE IT!!!

Black Myth : Wukomg took adapt JTTW faithfully while adding their own twist on certain parts, making the theme much more like dark fantasy. The story are divided into 6 chapters, the lore can be interpreted in many ways. The graphics are fantastic, details are amazing and the game rewards you for your hard works because it know it's difficult. The combat is fast paced, while the underlings enemies are quite monotone but the Yaoguai Chief and Yaoguai Kings are definitely there to hand your a** on silver platter.

The music? I ADORE IT, to the point I'll fly to SG to watch the concert because the game is worth watching for its music alone.

Cons : I hope they hire better English translateor because I think a lot of Chinese are lost in meanings when translated into simplified English and I hope they put subtitle on every lesser yaguai sentences and every songs, every animations because I definitely want to see the meaning.

The Best Game I've Ever Played!

Rating: 10/10 – An Absolute Masterpiece

I've been playing video games for years, but I can confidently say that Black Myth: Wukong is the best game I've ever played in my life.

Everything about this game is extraordinary. The breathtaking graphics, incredible environments, unforgettable boss fights, stunning soundtrack, and deep connection to Chinese mythology create an experience unlike anything I've played before.

What truly makes Wukong special is the attention to detail. Every location feels like a work of art, every battle feels meaningful, and every victory brings an incredible sense of achievement. The combat is challenging, rewarding, and incredibly satisfying. Even after hours of playing, I constantly find myself amazed by what this game has to offer.

But beyond the visuals and gameplay, there's something truly magical about its atmosphere, storytelling, and world. It's the kind of game that makes you want to explore every corner, discover every secret, and never let the adventure end.

Game Science has created something genuinely special. You can feel the passion, creativity, and dedication behind every part of this masterpiece.

I've played many incredible games throughout my life, but none has left such a lasting impression on me.

Black Myth: Wukong isn't just a great game. For me, it's the greatest gaming experience of my life.

A true masterpiece. 10/10.

The game looks amazing, but even on a high-end rig a stable 60–80 FPS without frame gen and artifacts is impossible. Without ray tracing it looks rough and buggy. With it, it looks great, but then you need DLSS and frame gen, which add input delay and artifacting. It is a must for a game like this to run smooth and clear. The game is 0/10 for me on my PS5 Pro since it looks and plays like shit. Unreal Engine 5 slop. 

Most of the relic bosses suck and rely on BS for difficulty, but the vast majority of the other bosses are really good and unique. Unlike Elden Ring, bosses aren’t recycled just to fill out the world.

The 100% is a pain: tons of missables and time-gated RNG drop farming.

All in all, a very good skill-based boss rush game with a really strong story.

review:
I loved it at the beginning, but the more I progress the more boring it gets. You have magic abilities that do a huge amount of damage, but these have a long cooldown. They can also be interrupted, restaring the cooldown. For some bosses, doing melee attacks is almost useless so you basically run around waiting for the cooldowns to end. Some bosses have incredibly long combos that kill you off if you do not evade most of the attacks, and the drawn-out feeling of the boss fights makes learning them a chore.
You also frequently fight the camera, not only because sometimes you simply don't see anything if you stand near a wall or a tree, but also because it is very difficult to actually estimate the range of your charged melee attacks, so you charge up an attack only to have it end an inch in front of the boss. I have some problems with the combat, mainly being spells and heavy attacks are too easily completely nullified if you slightly mistimed them. Feels bad to heal as well, it takes a long time and the button is often unresponsive….? Same with charging heavy attacks I have the button held down with stamina to spare and often I have to re-click and hold.

Stance system also feels weird on a first playthrough, there are not nearly enough sparks (skill points) to meaningfully spec into more than one stance without a detrimental loss to other stats and skills.
Duplicates (spell) having collision with the player is also bad design IMO. Causes your character to miss key attacks and tanks frame rate too.
Some audio stutters and missing audio completely from some cutscenes.

General unreal engine slop - terrible frames, stutters, and 1% lows for the first ~10 minutes upon startup or when teleporting to another region. The game has VERY long load times on a gen 4 nvme as well.

review:
[h1][b]Black Myth: Wukong[/b][/h1]
[h3][b]My Journey to the West — 130+ Hours Later[/b][/h3]

I had not anticipated that the game would take more than 130 hours. And yet, I find myself approaching the conclusion of my personal "Journey to the West." I took a methodical approach, exploring at my own pace and occasionally optimising my equipment more than was necessary. I was pleasantly surprised by the extensive range of content available. Each chapter unveils new features and storylines, consistently maintaining my interest. I was rarely bored, and best of all, I was so immersed in the activity that I did not notice the time passing. Indeed, I am still playing to increase the difficulty with highly optimised gear.

[h3][b]Gameplay, Combat & Progression[/b][/h3]

In terms of gameplay, I found the difficulty level to be fairly balanced for a first playthrough. However, the difficulty level of some bosses was notably higher than others. I particularly appreciated the variety of skills and upgrades, which allowed for customisation of combat styles.

Depending on the boss, certain stances proved more effective than others to vary their approach rather than sticking to a single strategy. The game offers a wide range of weapons that prioritise power or critical hits, as well as skills that can be developed. In addition, there are armour sets that combine to offer additional bonuses, allowing plenty of room to experiment and fine-tune your setup.

The healing system is well-designed, with various flasks to unlock and drinks to combine for bonus effects. The bestiary is also impressive, featuring creatures and bosses with meticulous designs. 

The weapons and armour are impressive, and each discovery stimulates the desire to explore new possibilities. I would also like to express my appreciation of the ability to reset my skills at will, thus allowing me to experiment with different combat styles. Furthermore, I would have appreciated greater flexibility in the use of armour upgrade resources. In my personal experience, I have sometimes held back on certain items due to concerns about wasting them on equipment that I was planning to replace. This has sometimes resulted in missing out on potentially beneficial upgrades.

[h3][b]Visuals, Art Direction & Sound[/b][/h3]

Visually, I was extremely impressed. The settings in the various chapters are stunning, but it is the animation, the creatures' movements, and the visual effects that truly set this production apart. The art direction is a complete success. Even the animated sequences are charming and well-executed. The music skilfully transitions from a supporting role to a more prominent one during the most intense scenes. The key benefit of this approach is that it does not rely on visual cues or secondary characters to guide the user.

However, it should be noted that there are some aspects that could be improved. The most significant issue I have encountered is the presence of invisible walls, which can be frustrating when attempting to navigate detailed environments.

[h3][b]Story & Lore — A Journey Worth Knowing[/b][/h3]

In terms of the storyline, Black Myth: Wukong is set in a highly detailed universe, although the narrative world is not always clearly explained. The game draws inspiration from the famous Chinese novel Journey to the West, which recounts the journey of the monk Xuanzang to India, accompanied by the iconic Monkey King, Sun Wukong. This character is renowned for his cunning, his power, and his ability to shapeshift, making him an iconic figure in Chinese mythology. In addition, he was the source of inspiration for the character [b]Son Goku[/b] in the well-known manga [b]Dragon Ball.[/b]

I found the references to Chinese mythology to be of great interest. However, it should be noted that without prior knowledge of the subject, certain events may appear confusing and difficult to understand. At times, I would have preferred the storytelling to be more immersive, so as to better grasp the story's stakes. The animated sequences are of a high standard and significantly enhance the overall appeal of the adventure.

[h2][b]Conclusion — Worth the Wait[/b][/h2]

After such a long anticipation for this game, it was only natural to have some reservations, as is often the case when expectations are set too high. However, I was incorrect. Black Myth: Wukong met my expectations and even exceeded them thanks to the richness of its content. Despite a few minor issues, these are outweighed by the significant enjoyment derived from extensive gameplay.

I therefore have no hesitation in recommending it. The memorable combat, the exceptional bestiary, the sublime art direction, and an adventure that lasted much longer than expected all contributed to making this game a worthwhile purchase. Following 130 hours of gameplay, my sole objective is to reconnect with my team members and commence the adventure once more. Finally, it appears that the Monkey King has gained a valuable life lesson: material wealth is not necessarily a prerequisite for happiness. In contrast, the key elements of happiness are a capable team and the ability to overcome challenges. If you are having difficulty following the narrative, there is no cause for concern. Simply read Journey to the West, or acknowledge that the intricacies of Son Goku's tale exceeded initial expectations.

review: 就这破游戏的完成度加上人均谜语人的剧情以及数不清的空气墙简直就是一坨。只能说动捕演员和制作组确实辛苦了，游戏的CG和模型以及配音配乐都是顶级。只可惜制作人是个NC。就一沉浸在自己的艺术里无法自拔的神经质。顺带叠甲：本人预购玩家，游戏时长115小时，此言论仅针对冯冀一人其他制作人员辛苦了。游戏里不会讲人话就算了，微博和新视频预告（那首说唱）也是不说人话。还让玩家猜。没拿奖还在WB发小作文阴阳。就这样剧情的游戏还有这样的制作人要是没有国产滤镜一块钱我都嫌贵。别的游戏比如老头环都会用大量的文本来构建世界观，黑神话也有但是明显撑不起这样的世界观。而且其他游戏后期也会让玩家逐步发现线索拼凑出剧情。黑神话真就全程谜语人。开头莫名其妙结局也是莫名其妙。然后从其他方面比如模型和动作看得出制作人员已经尽力了，能力也是顶级，但摊上这么个NT制作人也是没辙。以后再买游科的游戏我就是啥X。

review:
美术很顶，黑风山的层峦叠嶂，黄风岭的大漠黄沙，小西天的雪域佛国，盘丝岭的诡谲地穴，火焰山的灼热熔岩，花果山的广袤绿地。前四章视觉体验极佳，后两章开始回落，火焰山和环山公路一样，小怪换皮感有点重，但是火焰山土地和红孩儿的boss战很劲，一个水墨画风的阴阳空间表现力极强，一个火尖枪打铁花的演出效果很赞；花果山地图太大探索体验不是很好不过筋斗云还是很爽的，浮屠界的红眼特效有点晕。
音乐也很顶，唢呐三弦灵吉的陕北说书，不白的往生咒，大圣残躯的云宫迅音，大圣的出场实在帅，如意金箍棒飞出来那一幕我能记很久，黄眉那一长段鬼扯也很惊艳
动作游戏玩的不多对我来说还是有点难，第一章大头，白衣秀士尤其这白蛇死了30多次，第二章虎先锋和它二弟疯虎也把我猴头啃烂，第三章寅虎老师那个抬头杀给我看吐了打的我头晕眼花，后面等级法术什么的上来了就舒服很多了，二三周目纯爽游，连战用牛魔套也是打过了，就是复战齐天杨戬和大圣给我难吐了死了不知道多少回，不过好歹啃下来了。
章节动画也是神中神，就是剧情有些遗憾，还我四妹！最后天命人集齐了六根获得了大圣的记忆，这也算另一种复生了吧，希望有生之年能玩到续作。

review:
本来不想这么早（2024-10-24）玩这游戏的，可实在是太火了，连上小学生的侄子都知道，说要来我家玩，所以就提前下载安装并游玩了。游戏质量确实是够硬，画面质感很棒，怪物设计也各有特色，很多需要对应的解法，以及埋藏了不少的隐藏要素，需要根据NPC提示解开。
其实第一周目的前几关，玩得并不是特别爽，技能太多，技能点不够的问题之前在古剑里，现在在黑神话中又出现了，就导致需要频繁洗技能……看似很人性化的设计，为强迫症玩家带来给多纠结。而且，就算是更高级的技能，在伤害方面没有明显的提升，也会感觉爽度不太够。导致这问题的还一关键在于对敌人的技能不熟，高周目打的时候，敌人虽然难了，但看机会破招，以及各种技能的叠加，也很容易把BOSS玩死（除了大圣）。
最后为了刷成就，我居然打了四个周目，就是因为下毒手这武器。一周目我基本没看攻略，根本不知道有这玩意。二周目我是打完了才想起来有这么个东西。三周目我是以为打断两只手就有……结果发现是因为看错了条件，需要打断四只手……由于这自动存档系统的设定，害我又得来一周目，解锁了所有根器，体验了只有在四周目的大圣模式（然总体并没有多大变化）。还要吐嘈一点的是泡酒物这该死的掉率，我刷了几百个人参才出来，然后发现很多攻略其实并不全，如果程序里是给某颗参100%掉率而其他不掉那我就原谅你而去怪那些攻略视频了。
关卡设计方面前四关都各有各的不错，第五关和第六关却有点敷衍了，特别是第六关刚上筋斗云应该是个很兴奋的设计，然而飞上天没几下就迷路了……这大片的森林设计得真心迷。
人物设计方面除了主角是个哑巴之外都不错，二郎神、弥勒、蜘蛛精等等。真的，主角不会说话代入感还是缺了那么一点点。以至于特别喜欢八戒在身旁的时候，有个人一直陪伴吐槽的感觉很好。
总之，这游戏的巨大成功是件好事，应当对国产单机游戏有很强的推动力，像是仙剑、古剑这种老牌游戏都难产的情况下，更能激励新单机的诞生。

review:
This game might not be quite as good as Borderlands 2, but it's still a lot of fun and has a lot of content to enjoy, especially if you get both season passes.  I went for 100% completion and got every achievement in the game, but I got a little fatigued from it after 197 hours and decided not to pursue every vehicle paint job, especially since some of the paint jobs are not even obtainable anymore.  Parts of the game were very challenging and near impossible without finding and adding another player to the party (which can also be a challenge in itself since the game is now old and it's hard to find other players).  I played Moze the Gunner in this game and had trouble trying to survive in a challenging area alone until I found out that the character, with the right spec, can transfer aggro to her robot/mech suit (called "Iron Bear") with an ability called Auto Bear, which allows you to exit the mech and still have it in the field for 15 seconds, making it a kind of NPC tank.  Once the 15 seconds are over, the Iron Bear charges an enemy and explodes.  But even before it does that, the ability is refreshed and you can just summon it again.  Exit the vehicle immediately and rinse and repeat until you win!

I also enjoy the elemental status effects, which gives you good reason to carry multiple weapons outside of the four gun slots you eventually acquire. review:
A few years ago, back when I finished Borderlands 3 for the first time, my opinion of it wasn't exactly a confetti bomb. I recognized how smooth and fun the gunplay was, but I abhorred the story and characters.

Now, funnily enough, coming back to it as an older adult, my opinion of it has actually improved. See, I still think the main quest has horrible pacing and that most instances of conflict only happen because the characters are mind-bogglingly stupid, but it didn't bother me that much this time around. I attribute that to a personal change more than anything.

I grew out of the "constantly angry nerd" phase. I play things more relaxed. I don't check social media feeds as much. And who would've thought? Our parents were right. It's the damn phone that's the problem.

Now I was able to enjoy the fantastic gameplay without stressing so much about everything else. I still hope for a genuinely great main quest in the future, but BL3 is definitely worth a shot for the gameplay alone, even if everything else bothers you.

review:
Borderlands 3, truth be told I really enjoy this game. The looting, shooting, traversal, level design, enemy design, sound design and soundtrack. Pretty much everything to do with the core gameplay is fantastic. The drop rates and selection for items I personally think is the best of all the BL games, it tows that line of,  you will get legendaries to drop a lot but whether you get good parts rolls determines the viability of them which I greatly enjoy and tickles the loot goblin in me. The Gunplay is still the slight edge of wackyness and realism that previous titles brought, and each vault hunter is viable and has very fun unique action skills. Swapping between those action skills and crafting builds I think is the strongest here over the previous games.

Now the story, is all over the place for me. The main campaign storyline is definitely the weakest its ever been, but there are still many many likable characters (along with a few unlikeable) that are still written decent for what they're trying to be. The DLCs are where they definitely improved greatly on the story telling, and actually impressed me with how much better the writting for the DLCs is. 

In short, Its a very fun game to play, don't get too attached to the story/characters, blast psyco's in the dome and get Shlootin!

review:
Surprisingly, I had a lot of fun with the game. I wasn't a huge fan of BL1 and BL2 - both were kinda mid in my mind.
I remember there being a huge hate bandwagon about the 2 main villains on release - and yeah, the dialogue and writing in this game is mostly bad, cringy and unfunny, with a decent amount of gross out "humor" to boot.
But the gameplay and gunplay really do carry this game, with visuals (despite the ugly cel shading) and audio also being pretty good, and they all are better here than the previous two games by a wide margin.

[h3]The guns, loot and gameplay[/h3]
Undeniably the best part. Yeah, it starts slow with guns that have poor accuracy, like in previous games, but it picks up fast and by the second half I was drowning in legendries, so much so that I was wiping most bosses, including the final story boss, in under a minute, just because I happened to kill an optional animal mini-boss on the way there.

I did like the new feature of guns having alternative firing modes. Most of the time its something boring - a burst/auto switch, but for some guns they have cool gimmicks like the underbarrel grenade launcher or a shotgun, elemental type switch, auto aim puck, etc., depending on the gun manufacturer.

The guns are kinda weird though.
Most pistols seem to just be SMGs. This makes the SMG archetype pointless. Rocket Launchers also appear to be extremely underwhelming, at least in my playthrough and build, they did no more damage that regular guns, and had extremely poor ammo economy and slow firing speed, making them useless in my view.
Then there are the weapon manufacturers. At least half of them have weird gimmicks - slow charge up times, throw-away reloads, overheat mechanics, slow projectiles, etc.

What this all culminates in is that I stuck with like 3 "boring" manufactures, and mostly pistols and assault rifles, because that's what was most effective. The other 6 manufacturers and 4 gun archetypes were just immediately trashed, because they are either too weak or too annoying to use. Why would I use a cool looking gun that takes 10 shots to kill an enemy when I can use a boring gun that does it in 1? This becomes even more of a pain point on post-game Mayhem mode - where enemies can insta-snipe you from far way, making any non hitscan guns just non viable.

The loot drops are also not really all that exciting when you realize, like with most games that have loot systems and leveling - all your guns WILL become obsolete. This works great to force the player to try new stuff, but makes loot less exciting. Yeah, I got a strong legendary. Maybe it looks a bit different from a normal gun. It will be useless in 10 levels.

UI was kinda annoying, it seems to run at 20-30 FPS at all times regardless of your game performance, bugs out sometimes, and multiple times I crashed when in my inventory.

They finally added a very hidden switch to turn off mouse steering for vehicles - and vehicles now have more upgrades which is cool.

Other dislikes:
* Online server BS
* Some exploration stuff is hard locked behind main story progression with no indication of when you might unlock it. One of the collectibles can only be accessed after beating pretty much the whole main story. This really did disincentive exploration for me, and therefore doing all the side quests as well.

[h3]Story[/h3]
It's not all bad. But it's kinda bad. Especially the dialogue writing. There are so many unfunny jokes as well as cringe and groan inducing dialogue, and there's a lot of dialogue in general, so much so that it is a common occurrence of voice overs overlapping or canceling each other out, especially when collectibles are involved.

The overall story is not THAT bad, it's typical borderlands - bad guys, vaults. Some decent side quests here and there. References to other games and stuff that are actually entertaining.

review:
The sad paradox of BL3 is that it features the best gameplay in the series, balanced out by the worst story to boot.

Gearbox were a couple of steps away from making a generational masterpiece but somehow managed to cook up the most underwhelming narrative, annoyingly bland characters, and AI-level dialogue that silenced most of the redeeming qualities that the game had going for itself.

The strangest part is that the DLC content in this game is absolutely phenomenal, and for the most part, feels like a polished product when looking back at the base game campaign.

The story is what it is, but in the defense of Gearbox (yes, I cannot believe I'm typing that), there is a great game under the surface of the awful storytelling choices they made. 

On the other hand, the gameplay is addictive like crack cocaine, which is unironically the best in the series with its tech tree builds and unique weapon variety. BL2 andies will take offence to this, but hey, you can't win them all, so f_ck them as far as I'm concerned. Their judgement holds the same value as legendary drops in this game. 

I remember playing through the entire game and DLC content with one of my friends, and we had an absolute blast, which the Discord mod-level dialogue couldn't touch. 

Come to your own conclusions after trying it out.

The game is frequently on sale for ~$10 and at that price it is a must buy.

review:
My complaint about the dialogue:

There's too much damn idle dialogue. in the first few hours, most of the game is spent standing around waiting for characters to either stop talking or to finish a walking animation. In Borderlands 2, most of the dialogue was during a task, so you were still playing the game while the characters were talking. But I guess the devs forgot that the point of a game is to play it, and they added too much idle dialogue. Even with the dialogue skipper mod, there's so many times where you just have to stand for about 30 seconds for characters to finish their animations.

My feelings about everything else:
There's a lot of QOL things added, however there are many things that they changed for the worse. For instance, the map scroll and panning speeds are terribly slow, it makes navigating them so unbearable awful. While BL2 required its own BL2 fix mod for the gun drops and levels, this game seems to have fixed that which is good. There's also too much walking and barely any checkpoints, it's another issue that I had with BL2. At least in this game you can TP to unlocked TP points from any location, you don't need to walk to a TP to teleport. But the issue is there are barely any TP locations, so even if you do TP, you have to either walk or drive an entire map's length to get to an objective, and when each mission has 5 objectives that go back and forth, it's pretty annoying.
The gunplay is a bit different, it's fine I guess. It feels a lot more arcadey than the second, I honestly prefer BL2 gunplay more (and no it's not nostalgia, I never really played borderlands as a kid).
The performance was really weird. My pc specs are attached, and usually I can hit pretty high fps with most graphics settings in most games, but my fps seemed capped around 120ish despite my gpu and cpu sitting at 40% usage.

Personally, I would not recommend the game because of the dialogue and minor QOL things, just get BL2 and download some mods before playing (a bit tedious but def worth it).

review:
It's alright. If you're sure you want to get into it, be sure to grab the ultimate edition and get the extra skill tree (yes, things like skill trees are locked behind DLC)

I'm not one to lose my mind over "X-plotline kills off this character that I love or ruins this character" cause I'm not the most invested in Borderlands games, but I can sympathize with the people upset about that as there are games where that was a major problem for me. Gearbox has a pretty good (or bad, depending on your perspective) reputation for pulling this kind of stuff in their writing and game design though, so it's par for the course.
What I will say is that your character and your party at large constantly feel like they are secondary, side characters to the *ACTUAL* side characters who push the plot forward, every sense of accomplishment you have from advancing the story gets overshadowed by whatever they're doing. Especially towards the ending, and that's pretty annoying to me. It's pretty abysmal storytelling and character development. 

It's fun, the different classes and skillsets is a step up from earlier games in this series that I have played... but you definitely have to overlook some pretty irritating game design and writing decisions to keep having fun. There are some questionable decisions here and there, some that can be solved with modding, others not so much.

There are also some bugs, nothing that hardlocks the game but you might have to reset sections, go to main menu and restart, which sucks when you've looted some awesome gear and will now never see it again. 

6.5/10.

review: 著名刷子神游，但你不能接受画风和前期的乏味，可以出门左拐了。刚开始的确玩不进去，因为并不“爽”，角色没技能，没好枪，剧情云里雾里（实际上通关了依旧如此），伤害刮痧，玩的特工又容易死，地图灰黑一片，很难有探索欲望，可一旦熬过某个节点，解锁了更多机制，就能体会到刷子的快乐了，而你只需要付出一定的耐心。至于经常被提到的中配，其实在当时确实很棒，但说实在的放现在就有些尬且僵硬，或许是翻译问题，即使这样总的来看配音也只能算中上游水准，还是专注于爆出来的装备品质和词条吧。

挺好玩，就是主线剧情很没参与感的同时，也很无聊。玩的赞恩切枪流，打架对我来说很有趣，但是现在我40多级，打起怪来基本都是秒杀，玩多了说实话有点腻。加上主线剧情cg根本没有我玩的角色露面，非得让我看那个低质剧情演出，而且剧情也非常逆天，看起来非常无聊，哦对了，它还有单机fps设计最垃圾的跟随角色，听角色讲废话，玩起来非常影响心流，玩得正爽呢，打完一个战点不求你搞个解密，起码别搞这种跟随吧。

review:
推荐，非常好玩。
先说缺点，一个角色玩腻了想试试别的角色需要单开一个档，重新过一遍剧情，虽然可以跳过，但还是比较麻烦；然后虽然是出了很久的游戏，但社区缺乏详细且热门的攻略，需要花一定时间在查攻略上。谁懂搜攻略第一个视频点进去跟着跑图刷了几十轮都没出，又去查了阅览量小很多的攻略，然后看评论区才知道还有前置任务。虽然做攻略是纯热爱，但是既然要做至少要做全吧，当然也不排除老资历做攻略的时候距离当时已经过了很久，都忘记要做前置任务了；还有一个缺点就是这是个刷宝游戏，但刷装备很复杂。你打完boss没出，要退回标题再重进游戏刷新boss，这一点比较烦。如果是单人的话，反复刷花不了多少时间，但是多人的话就不行，很麻烦（而且这游戏居然还是鼓励联机的，在游戏说明中，联机的掉宝率会提升）

然后是优点。各个角色都很有意思，可以构筑不同的流派玩法，每个角色都很有特点；剧情的话中规中矩，而且dlc里的剧情有点辣眼睛，但是中配很有意思；说是刷宝游戏，但其实也可以当作是割草游戏。谁懂构筑好想玩的流派之后，在最高难度的怪堆里游龙割草的爽感啊！

总的来说，有一定缺点，但是值得一玩。

Here's the part they don't tell you. Halfway through the game, a "special" monster starts following you around. Between areas, across the different mission modes, everywhere. This monster, Bazelgeuse, will be drawn to the sound of you fighting monsters, and will carpet your battlefield with bombs. These will damage you heavily, even with heavy armor, chain you into other ones, and light you on fire, which you then have to sheathe your weapon mid-combat and roll; or dodge repeatedly to put out, all while Bazelgeuse and what you're fighting suddenly stop fighting each other and begin attacking you. It's possible alone, probably, but later on, you will want to bring a team, unless you relish a half hour of fighting a boss enemy (true story!) Also, the DLC is an obvious scam, adding only a handful of new areas and effectively paywalling a tool that a lot of established players will insist is a necessity and a convenience, all at 2/3 the base game's price. What a bargain!
Get it on sale or don't get it.

review:
Probably in the ball park of about -1000 hours across all platforms. I've been playing 'World' on- and off now since around 2020, and have never considered the game to be bad. No matter how long my break is I always end up revisiting it for a couple of months at a time. I have beaten every monster, (excluding Safi, and Kulve*) solo; so as far as reviews go- the average solo player can look to me to get insight on what the experience will be like. I want to leave this review to really open up a gods-honest opinion, giving a good and bad part about every instance in the game. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE GRIND: 

Yes, monster hunter is grindy. You should absolutely not expect to play this game without sinking upwards of 50+ hours in farming- and gear grinding. In reality, that estimate is probably much larger depending on a variety of variables. The game has tedious mechanics at times- and can definitely impact a long time playthrough without breaks, which could lead to burnout. This grind only exponentially grows throughout the game, as the base game is generally much more manage-able than the DLC. With this being said, the grind is absolutely not as demoralizing as one might expect. As far as I was concerned, I still had tons of fun farming, and sometimes- although arduous the feeling of finally getting a rare drop or finally crafting a piece of gear more than made up for the time spent getting it. You can really dump hours upon hours into creating your own builds, and experimenting with different weapons.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTWORK:

The monsters- and characters are some of the most memorable things in the game for me. I love the artwork and design of the creatures you fight in this game, and how they embed themselves into the environment. The immersion comes from the danger, and that some monsters are outright- terrifying to come across. The nature, and geography of the locations you traverse through are also gorgeous, and have proper- depth and design. A lot of the creatures develop their powers from the locale which they are most commonly found- which helps again to build on that immersion. The design of the armor is honestly a 50/50. Some sets have stunning looks, while others can look really funny. There is no shortage of "fashion" or designs out there, so the possibility of customizing your character is really endless when it comes to color, monster parts, or themes.  In-fact, a substantial amount of my playtime was also spent getting vanity gear, which includes cosmetics to drip out my character.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMUNITY: 

Don't reference your experience to isolationists who villainize the game by targeting people who don't use their weapon. The monster hunter experience is wonderful, and is intended to be played as you see fit. Although there are definitely do's and don'ts in multiplayer, id say probably around 90% of the player-base are genuinely helpful, kind players. I love this, as coming from previous games It felt as if the community for monster hunter was a really welcoming experience when I started out. There are some utterly jaw-dropping clips, and speed runs out there. The talent of the community and the competition between fastest-speed runs never ceased to amaze me as an average player. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DIFFICULTY:

There is some stigma out there- that confuses difficulty for annoyance. Some monsters in this game are annoying to fight, with gimmicky mechanics. That is not the same as difficult monsters. Besides the obvious endgame challenges- there really aren't too many monsters that the average player couldn't beat or would have trouble fighting. Hell, even Fatalis- which took me about a month of planning fell eventually, which was done multiple times with un-optimal builds and countless mistakes. Everything can be learned, and no one should be deterred by a monster just because it seems difficult. This game is really not too challenging, and for the most part, the average monster will at-most, just keep you on your toes rather than require you to completely focus on it. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STORY:

I'm going to be honest. The story in monster hunter is really nothing to go all crazy about. The characters lack depth, and have corny- random lines. The beauty in the story doesn't really come from the acting or narrative, but rather the climax. Most end-fights or fights that are big canonical moments make up for little filler monsters. For example, I really enjoyed Valkanas's ark, as well as the Shara-Ishvalda story, regardless of how their fights were. The characters do have interactions with each other but they seem quite dull, and lifeless at times. To be quite frank, the story is also really not what we want out of the game- as we more than make up for its qualities with strong combat and mechanics. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
100% TROPHY:

So that just about covers it- community, experience, and game design. The last thing I wanted to touch upon is something that I myself have been apt to. There are many, people out there who consider themselves completionists. This game, naturally- comes along with a set of 100 achievements which can be completed throughout the story and the side-quests. My honest- truth is that if your are thinking about going for the platinum trophy on monster hunter-DONT. I am not even going to get started on the implications of some of these achievements, but the only thing that anyone needs to know is that a general sum of the achievements are solely reliant on RNG. RNG numbers in-fact- that are not common in the slightest. I want to make it clear that a 100% trophy in this game will come up to 600 or more hours of playtime for the average player- especially if your playing solo. I am currently at the 500 hour mark on my character, (which i started in December of 2024), and have just-now, gotten to the "endgame" achievements AKA crown hunting. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I am personally planning on completing world in the foreseeable future, getting my platinum and getting the hell out of dodge. My experience with this game has lasted me through some of the most memorable moments in my life, and because of it this game belongs to a special area in my heart. I know that deep down, I will always admire it- but I would love to move on to 'Wilds' at some point. So for those who have played 'Wilds' - and want to check out other monster hunter experiences, try World. The UI and initial loop of the game can be confusing for brand new players but in the long run- I expect that there are more than a few who might enjoy this game as much as I have for the last six years of my life.

review:
My first Monster Hunter game, and honestly, I had a great time with it. I'd definitely recommend giving it a try, whether you're playing solo or with friends.

The gameplay is all about learning monster movesets, observing their patterns, and getting better at your own weapons. It's not just about getting the biggest numbers and hoping for the best. Or you can just button-mash and hope for the best. We've all been there.

There's a huge variety of weapons, so you're bound to find something you enjoy. And the gameplay loop is pretty fun: hunt colossal monsters, turn them into cool armor, and dress up your cat in matching gear. Yes, your cat can wear monster armor too. Fashion is important, even when you're out committing monster genocide.

The visuals are vibrant, and the environments look great. Some assets are showing their age, but you can always grab the high resolution texture pack. The maps aren't huge, but there's a surprising amount of detail, and each biome has its own ecosystem.

Even though Monster Hunter Wilds is more popular now, there's still a decent player base, so finding people to hunt with isn't a problem.

Now excuse me, there's a monster out there that would look great as a hat.
