review:
Watch Dogs 2 is a pretty decent game and I had a good time playing it, but I wouldn't call it anything special. The story is okay, the characters are interesting enough, and the open world is fun to explore at first, but the game has quite a few problems that keep it from being great.

One of the best things about the game is definitely the main missions. There are some genuinely fun moments, and Robot Wars was easily my favorite mission in the entire game. It was creative, entertaining, and actually felt different from the usual missions. Unfortunately, most of the other missions follow pretty much the same formula: break into a building, hack something, get the information you need, and leave. The hacking itself is fun initially, especially when you use drones and different gadgets to avoid enemies, but it gets repetitive after a while. I really wish there were more types of hacking mechanics and more variety in how you approach objectives.

I also tried a few side missions, but honestly, most of them were pretty trash and didn't really motivate me to keep playing them. The open world has plenty of activities, but quantity doesn't always mean quality.

The characters are decent, and Ray was easily my favorite. He has a lot of personality and brings some entertaining moments to the story. Dusan, on the other hand, reminded me a bit of Joseph Seed from Far Cry 5, both in appearance and behavior. The story itself is okay, but I never found it particularly amazing or memorable.

Driving isn't bad either, and the cars handle well enough, but I barely used them because fast travel was simply more convenient. I honestly don't think I've ever gone somewhere without using fast travel unless a mission forced me to drive. The city looks great, though, and exploring San Francisco is enjoyable, especially with all the hacking opportunities and things you can interact with.

I also like that the game gives you different ways to approach certain situations. You can sneak around, use your gadgets, distract enemies, or go in more aggressively if things go wrong. Playing stealthily and using your tools creatively can be really satisfying, even if the underlying objectives start feeling repetitive.

Overall, Watch Dogs 2 is worth playing, especially if you enjoy open-world games and messing around with hacking mechanics. It has some great moments, likable characters, and a fun setting, but the repetitive missions and underwhelming side content hold it back. It's a good enough game, just not one I'd consider particularly memorable.

For me, the first Watch Dogs is still clearly superior, especially in terms of story, atmosphere, and the overall experience. Watch Dogs 2 is more colorful and playful, but I personally prefer the darker tone of the original.

Final verdict: 7/10. A fun game that's worth trying, but it could have been so much better with more mission variety and a stronger story.

**Played on PS4 in 2021, now giving it another chance on PC**

I first started playing Watch Dogs 2 on PS4 on April 17, 2021, but stopped playing on July 12, 2021. Back then, I probably just lost interest after playing for a while and moved on to other games. Sometimes you leave a game unfinished, not because it's bad, but because you feel like playing something else.

Now I've decided to give it another chance on Steam. I want to revisit San Francisco, enjoy the hacking mechanics again, and experience the game from a fresh perspective on PC.

It's interesting coming back to a game I played years ago and remembering an experience I left behind. This time, I hope to enjoy it again and maybe finally get further into the game than I did on PS4.

**Recommended.** Sometimes it's worth coming back to an old game and giving it another chance.

review:
[h3] A Different Side of Watch Dogs [/h3]

Watch Dogs 2 is one of those games that makes you appreciate how much personality an open world can have. Coming back to the series after the first game, it's interesting to see how different the sequel feels while still keeping what made the original enjoyable. San Francisco is a fantastic setting, full of life, colour and things to discover. Exploring the city never really gets old, and the soundtrack fits the atmosphere brilliantly, giving the game its own identity and making the world feel alive. One of my favourite parts is the story and the DedSec crew. The characters each have their own personalities, and their interactions bring plenty of humour and charm. Although the tone is much lighter than the first game, the story still explores interesting ideas about privacy, surveillance and the power of technology. It makes you want to see what happens next. The gameplay is another highlight. The hacking mechanics give you plenty of freedom in how you approach missions, while the RC Jumper and Quadcopter make things even more enjoyable. Experimenting with different approaches keeps the gameplay fresh throughout. Of course, the game isn't perfect. Some of the humour doesn't always land, and parts of the story feel a little uneven, but these issues don't take away from the overall experience. Overall, Watch Dogs 2 is a brilliant sequel that takes the series in a different direction and makes it work. With a memorable cast, an incredible setting and entertaining gameplay, it's a game that's easy to get lost in. It may feel very different from the original, but that's exactly what makes it stand out.

review:
旧金山的城市底子、黑客沙盒玩法本身有可取之处，但部分主线关卡的设计和遗留bug严重消耗游玩耐心。
 
刚打完HAUM章节最后的逃离任务，遇到大量脚本bug：追捕状态下持枪上车交互卡死、角色原地抽搐；就算成功跑出任务划定的黄色区域，追捕脚本依旧无法正常终止，警察与直升机无限增援，杀完一批立刻刷新一批，根本不存在“清完追兵脱身”的选项。
 
紧接着推进到镜中世界的夏浪派对任务，预期只是拍照剧情，结果剧情结束后强制开启限时黑客连线挑战，而且进入该任务场景后主线被锁定，不完成这个挑战就无法开启其他主线案件。长段无法跳过的重复对话，叠加限时解谜压力，关卡目标转折突兀，完全没有提前给到玩家预期，反复重试还要一遍遍重看对话，大量时间被无效消耗。
 
可以感受到制作组想营造黑客竞赛的紧张氛围，但完全忽略玩家的节奏感受：刚从高强度追捕、bug折磨里脱身，立刻被扔进另一个高压限时任务。沙盒游戏本应给玩家选择空间，但这段流程几乎没有绕开的途径。
 
如果你是冲着流畅主线体验来的，这几段很容易让人心态崩溃；只想随便在城里黑客闲逛、不在乎主线进度的玩家可以酌情考虑

review:
一、核心玩法循环
玩家扮演黑客 Marcus Holloway，在旧金山湾区执行 DedSec 的行动。核心循环为：接取行动（潜入戒备森严的建筑、提取或破坏数据）→ 运用黑客工具箱化解威胁 → 完成任务 → 累积"粉丝（Followers）"→ 解锁更强力、更远程的黑客能力。
- 黑客工具箱：智能手机远程入侵（红绿灯、摄像头、ctOS 联网设备）、四轴无人机（高空侦察 / 标记）、RC Jumper 跳跳车（狭小空间潜入）、环境陷阱（爆炸管道、叉车、吊车）与社会工程。
- 三种推进风格：幽灵（全程不进入区域）、潜行、以及正面火拼——批评普遍认为战斗是最弱的一环，游戏最佳体验来自非致命的智取。
- 粉丝系统即进度机制：粉丝越多，黑客范围与强度越大，形成清晰的成长曲线。
- 任务与模式：主线行动、支线世界故事、双人无缝合作（自由漫游 / 合作行动）、可选 PvP 入侵（赏金猎杀 / 黑客竞速），以及收集品与赛车等。
- 合作与 PvP：支持双人无缝 Drop-in 合作；PvP 入侵为可关闭的可选内容。
二、画面与音效表现
画面：明亮、鲜活的旧金山湾区复刻（金门大桥、渔人码头、硅谷写字楼），街头动态（涂鸦、路人、撑伞市民）营造出"城市旅游模拟器"般的真实感；美术风格为风格化写实，氛围轻松。不足：复杂场景中视觉信息密度高，守卫的红色描边难以辨识，影响潜行判断；过场为 16:9 带黑边，超宽屏与 HDR 需借助 Mod 才能较好支持。
音效：原声与电台配乐广受好评，贴合科幻 / 恶搞基调；环境音与黑客提示反馈到位。整体"不拖后腿"，但无突破性表现。
三、性能与优化
- 硬件门槛低：官方最低为 GTX 660 / HD 7870 + 6GB 内存，推荐 GTX 780 / R9 290 + 8GB；50GB 安装体积。在主流及旧硬件上 1080p 流畅，PC 移植在早期被评价为顺畅。
- 物理帧率上限：游戏物理按 60 FPS 设计，高于此帧率可能导致布娃娃 / NPC 异常。
- 现代硬件已知问题（2026 年玩家需重点关注）：
  - NVIDIA RTX 30 / 40 / 50 系严重闪烁：天空盒与阴影持续高频闪烁，官方至今未修复；社区 workaround 为 NVIDIA Profile Inspector 驱动级覆盖，或 DXVK 包装（但会禁用联机 / EAC）。
  - AMD 显卡崩溃：可通过修改 WD2_GamerProfile.xml 中 DeferredFxQuality="pc" 缓解。
  - 卡顿：建议装于 SSD、关闭多人功能或 EAC、对进程关闭 Control Flow Guard。
  - Windows 11 24H2 启动异常、现代 Core i9 的 E-core 调度问题（可用 Process Lasso 仅保留 P-core）等亦见报告。
- 综合来看：本作在"能跑"的旧硬件上体验稳定，但在新 GPU / 新系统上需手动调校，门槛主要体现为兼容性问题而非性能不足。
四、付费模式与 DLC（买断制）
- 性质：一次性买断制，非免费游戏；DLC 为额外付费层。原价约 $60/£40，现常年深度折扣（完整 Gold 版在促销期常低于 $5）。
- 版本差异：
  - 标准版：游戏本体。
  - 豪华版（Deluxe）：本体 + Deluxe Pack（仅外观）。
  - 黄金版（Gold）：本体 + Deluxe Pack + 季票（Season Pass）。
- 季票内容：十二宫杀手任务、Defalt 套装、载具与武器皮肤、T-Bone 内容包（含 Mayhem 合作难度）、Human Conditions（3 段世界故事 + 精英合作）、No Compromise（俄黑帮世界故事 + Showd0wn 合作模式）。
- 外观包：大量 Mega / Supreme / Ultimate 等捆绑包，均为纯外观；Ultra 材质包免费。
- 内购标注：Steam 页面带有 "In-App Purchases" 类别（Ubisoft Connect 内可能存在少量便利 / 外观向消费），但核心玩法不依赖微交易，无抽奖 / 抽卡机制，也无侵略性付费墙。
- 客观评价：作为买断制作品，其变现克制，主要付费点集中在 DLC 剧情扩展与外观，且当前价格极低，性价比高。
五、新手体验
- 门槛较初代更低：基调轻松、角色讨喜（Marcus、Wrench、Sitara、Josh），粉丝系统提供明确成长反馈，黑客工具箱有引导。
- 战斗短板影响手感：角色偏"脆"、掩护系统尚可但敌人爱绕侧、无翻滚闪避；若依赖枪战，新手容易受挫，更推荐以潜行 / 智取推进。
- 潜行识别困难：部分批评指出无人机侦察偏"流程化"，且场景中难辨敌人， stealth 体验偶有挫败。
- 联机入侵建议关闭：入侵模式常匹配到经验老到的玩家，对新手体验不友好，多数建议初期关闭。
- 启动摩擦：Ubisoft Connect + Denuvo + EAC 三层叠加，且新硬件需额外修复步骤，首次上手有一定门槛。
六、长期可玩性
- 内容体量：单人主线约 30 小时，叠加世界故事、季票与合作 / 在线模式后显著拉长；开放沙盒鼓励"整活"式自由实验。
- 衰退因素：支线活动被认为有育碧"罐头"重复感；主线冲突张力偏弱、反派脸谱化；部分玩家指出刷粉 / 任务结构后期趋同。
- 维护现状：游戏已发售约十年，育碧基本停止主动维护，RTX 闪烁等已知问题长期未获官方修复，社区普遍认为 IP 已被搁置。
- 价值定位：在深度折扣下，其开放世界品质与创意黑客系统仍被视为育碧开放世界口碑高点之一，长线"性价比"突出。
优点
1. 创意黑客沙盒：幽灵 / 潜行 / 强攻多路径，自由度高。
2. 鲜活、有生命的旧金山湾区开放世界，氛围与配乐出色。
3. 角色讨喜、基调轻松，粉丝进度系统反馈清晰。
4. 合作体验佳（无缝 Drop-in），PvP 为可选且可关。
5. 买断制、无侵略性微交易，无抽奖；当前价格极低。
6. 在适配硬件上 PC 移植顺畅、配置门槛低。
缺点
1. 战斗 / 射击手感最弱：角色偏脆、无翻滚、敌人绕侧明显。
2. 现代硬件兼容性差：RTX 30/40/50 闪烁、AMD 崩溃、W11 24H2 启动、E-core 调度等需手动修复。
3. DRM 叠层（Ubisoft Connect + Denuvo + EAC）带来启动摩擦。
4. 潜行偶有"流程化"感，场景辨识度低影响体验。
5. 支线重复、主线张力弱、反派脸谱化。
6. 已停止主动维护，已知 Bug 长期未修；物理锁 60 FPS。
适合玩家群体
适合：
- 喜爱开放世界沙盒、强调"自由解法"的玩家；
- 偏好潜行 / 非致命智取、厌恶无脑枪战的玩家；
- 看重合作 PvE、轻松幽默基调与实验性玩法的玩家；

不适合：
- 以枪战手感 / 射击爽快度为首要诉求的玩家；

内容体量：单人主线约 30 小时，叠加世界故事、季票与合作 / 在线模式后显著拉长；开放沙盒鼓励"整活"式自由实验。 - 衰退因素：支线活动被认为有育碧"罐头"重复感；主线冲突张力偏弱、反派脸谱化；部分玩家指出刷粉 / 任务结构后期趋同。 - 维护现状：游戏已发售约十年，育碧基本停止主动维护，rtx 闪烁等已知问题长期未获官方修复，社区普遍认为 ip 已被搁置。 - 价值定位：在深度折扣下，其开放世界品质与创意黑客系统仍被视为育碧开放世界口碑高点之一，长线"性价比"突出。 优点 1. 创意黑客沙盒：幽灵 / 潜行 / 强攻多路径，自由度高。 2. 鲜活、有生命的旧金山湾区开放世界，氛围与配乐出色。 3. 角色讨喜、基调轻松，粉丝进度系统反馈清晰。 4. 合作体验佳（无缝 drop-in），pvp 为可选且可关。 5. 买断制、无侵略性微交易，无抽奖；当前价格极低。 6. 在适配硬件上 pc 移植顺畅、配置门槛低。 缺点 1. 战斗 / 射击手感最弱：角色偏脆、无翻滚、敌人绕侧明显。 2. 现代硬件兼容性差：rtx 30/40/50 闪烁、amd 崩溃、w11 24h2 启动、e-core 调度等需手动修复。 3. drm 叠层（ubisoft connect + denuvo + eac）带来启动摩擦。 4. 潜行偶有"流程化"感，场景辨识度低影响体验。 5. 支线重复、主线张力弱、反派脸谱化。 6. 已停止主动维护，已知 bug 长期未修；物理锁 60 fps。 适合玩家群体 适合： - 喜爱开放世界沙盒、强调"自由解法"的玩家； - 偏好潜行 / 非致命智取、厌恶无脑枪战的玩家； - 看重合作 pve、轻松幽默基调与实验性玩法的玩家； - 趁深度折扣低价入库、追求性价比的玩家。 不适合： - 以枪战手感 / 射击爽快度为首要诉求的玩家； - 期望现代游戏持续维护、开箱即稳的玩家； - 反感启动器 / drm 摩擦、需要原生超宽屏或 hdr 的玩家； - 追求强叙事张力或 pve 终局深度的玩家。 小结：作为一款约十年前发售的买断制开放世界作品，《watch dogs 2》凭借创意黑客系统、鲜活的旧金山湾区与轻松基调，仍是育碧开放世界中的高点之一；其低价格与克制变现构成显著性价比。主要不确定因素来自两方面——一是战斗手感偏弱、叙事张力不足，二是现代硬件（尤其 rtx 30/40/50 系）上的兼容性 bug 需玩家自行修复。是否入手，主要取决于你能否接受"手动调校 + 智取优先"的游玩方式，以及是否看重折扣期的极低入手价。

review:
First and foremost I'm a life long and very absorbed student of weapons and war - both by education and passion. For absolute breadth there is no game like it and it's absorbed me for countless hours. It's an addictive hobby, but no more so than most others military history nuts come into. The vehicles are amazing and it's a gorgeous game. For sheer cinematic value on average hardware nothing can beat it.

That said War Thunder is far from perfect - the attention to crafting the vehicles and weapons is immersive. The battlefields might as well come from Star Fox or Battletech and the community can be more than a little toxic as it includes a lot of youngsters with out any supervision. 

Arcade mode is just that, and can be a blast - air arcade has some of the most imaginative battlefields and landscapes out there but it's also nuts and you have to just laugh when you get taken out. Ground arcade is just a simplified mode of ground 'Real Battle' with easier aiming and quicker game play. For old eyes like mine it's a go to. If you're not someone who needs a million miles a minute and can cope with slower gameplay, Naval is awesome - and some of the extended conflict matches (bigger maps ~ 2hr games, but you can duck out whenever) are the best game modes War Thunder devs have ever made. Depending on the state of the game it's possible for opposing spawn points (your choice to spawn there) to occur with in less than 5km of one another. For battleships this can be a thrilling point blank 'broadside' fight that is as much a test of fortitude as it is skill.

Calling a mode 'Real Battle' is a bit of a farce as well - air consists of a map for ~ 60 aircraft, 30 per side, lined up at 70km distance for jets, and a line of 'ground targets' (very simple firebases)  There are 'supply bases' that can be bombed, but both Air Arcade and air 'RB' are filled with dogfight obsessed players, many of whom cannot comprehend why aircraft are included (now to include strategic bombers) that cannot dogfight. High tier featuring many of the slick, modern aircraft featured in promos is nothing but 'missile spam.' Missiles begin flying like a medieval arrow storm at anywhere from 50km on in, and though some claim one can be skilled enough to avoid or dodge (and there is much insulting and name-calling if one cannot dodge how other players think it should be done.) At lower levels air RB can be fun but it gets repetitive. You have no choice of what map you're flying in and you must have your battle lineup selected before time. There is less focus on fighters only but bombers almost always fly alone as there is no real insentive to do otherwise. 

As a matter of fact there is no real reason to play the game according to militarily accurate tactics at all. Other than a voice comms linked group of up to four can utterly dominate air or ground if the players are adequate and good at covering one another. People from some areas in the world are accused at length of cheating because their gaming culture is competitive and collaborative - there are highly developed 'clans' or squadrons that have extremely well thought out and coordinated 'battle nets' allowing even randomly spawned 'allies' to coordinate and work efficiently. For lone wolf players this can be frustrating to the point of infuriating and cause...again...toxic behavior and words of team chat.

Sim is the 'redheaded stepchild' of War Thunder and only Air Sim is worth mentioning. Play is strictly first person (from the cockpit) and the maps range from 64 x 64km to 128 x 128km. Battles are long, and there is bigger balance between strike & bomber players, and fighter pilots. Flight models can vary radically from RB and often planes that are dogs in that mode shine in Sim. 90% of content creators, especially those famous for rating vehicles, ignore this mode as the younger crowd looking for short games considers it 'boring.' For the most part the sim community is small enough that you get to know other regular players - the best part being you aren't restricted to a random map and bunch of players. If you don't like a particular map, choose another. If you find someone you detest in the lobby, go to another one. 

Gaijin, War Thunder's developer, has a very puzzling if straight forward business model...and they also listen way too much to 'the mob' on their forums. Besides their ability to take any new game mode and ruin it: a new 'nuclear escalation' mode is populated by respawning and rage-inducingly accurate SAM sites that are very difficult to eliminate thanks to a unrealistic mechanic where something like 90% of the weapons launched at them are successfully intercepted. One of the main marketing tools is 'snail rage' (Gaijin's logo is a snail) where players end up so angry at the game they either uninstall...or buy a premium vehicle. Which used to help for a while as they tend to be more powerful, but not so much anymore. 

Further, today's 'top gun' will eventually get either raised in battle rating so it's operating against far tougher (to the point of invulnerable) opponents or have weapons 'nerfed.' Always claiming some new data, game devs routinely take a weapons system that preforms reliably better than others and make it worse. Sometimes it's because the hue and cry of the mob of players (most who are young and often toxic) sometimes it's to sell a new premium vehicle.

Last, a word of advice: Free to Play is wholly misleading. Some players pride themselves on climbing the ranks with out paying a dime. They cry about 'pay to win' players but often this is because they don't have a job and don't comprehend that the game is developed as a business. For those playing in places with depressed economies, there is no scaling of costs however and for someone somewhere else in the world paying $80 for a premium vehicle is insane, where as here it's less than a day's wages.

Ground arcade is just a simplified mode of ground 'Real Battle' with easier aiming and quicker game play. For old eyes like mine it's a go to. If you're not someone who needs a million miles a minute and can cope with slower gameplay, Naval is awesome - and some of the extended conflict matches (bigger maps ~ 2hr games, but you can duck out whenever) are the best game modes War Thunder devs have ever made. Depending on the state of the game it's possible for opposing spawn points (your choice to spawn there) to occur with in less than 5km of one another. For battleships this can be a thrilling point blank 'broadside' fight that is as much a test of fortitude as it is skill. Calling a mode 'Real Battle' is a bit of a farce as well - air consists of a map for ~ 60 aircraft, 30 per side, lined up at 70km distance for jets, and a line of 'ground targets' (very simple firebases) There are 'supply bases' that can be bombed, but both Air Arcade and air 'RB' are filled with dogfight obsessed players, many of whom cannot comprehend why aircraft are included (now to include strategic bombers) that cannot dogfight. High tier featuring many of the slick, modern aircraft featured in promos is nothing but 'missile spam.' Missiles begin flying like a medieval arrow storm at anywhere from 50km on in, and though some claim one can be skilled enough to avoid or dodge (and there is much insulting and name-calling if one cannot dodge how other players think it should be done.) At lower levels air RB can be fun but it gets repetitive. You have no choice of what map you're flying in and you must have your battle lineup selected before time. There is less focus on fighters only but bombers almost always fly alone as there is no real insentive to do otherwise. As a matter of fact there is no real reason to play the game according to militarily accurate tactics at all. Other than a voice comms linked group of up to four can utterly dominate air or ground if the players are adequate and good at covering one another. People from some areas in the world are accused at length of cheating because their gaming culture is competitive and collaborative - there are highly developed 'clans' or squadrons that have extremely well thought out and coordinated 'battle nets' allowing even randomly spawned 'allies' to coordinate and work efficiently. For lone wolf players this can be frustrating to the point of infuriating and cause...again...toxic behavior and words of team chat. Sim is the 'redheaded stepchild' of War Thunder and only Air Sim is worth mentioning. Play is strictly first person (from the cockpit) and the maps range from 64 x 64km to 128 x 128km. Battles are long, and there is bigger balance between strike & bomber players, and fighter pilots. Flight models can vary radically from RB and often planes that are dogs in that mode shine in Sim. 90% of content creators, especially those famous for rating vehicles, ignore this mode as the younger crowd looking for short games considers it 'boring.' For the most part the sim community is small enough that you get to know other regular players - the best part being you aren't restricted to a random map and bunch of players. If you don't like a particular map, choose another. If you find someone you detest in the lobby, go to another one. Gaijin, War Thunder's developer, has a very puzzling if straight forward business model...and they also listen way too much to 'the mob' on their forums. Besides their ability to take any new game mode and ruin it: a new 'nuclear escalation' mode is populated by respawning and rage-inducingly accurate SAM sites that are very difficult to eliminate thanks to a unrealistic mechanic where something like 90% of the weapons launched at them are successfully intercepted. One of the main marketing tools is 'snail rage' (Gaijin's logo is a snail) where players end up so angry at the game they either uninstall...or buy a premium vehicle. Which used to help for a while as they tend to be more powerful, but not so much anymore. Further, today's 'top gun' will eventually get either raised in battle rating so it's operating against far tougher (to the point of invulnerable) opponents or have weapons 'nerfed.' Always claiming some new data, game devs routinely take a weapons system that preforms reliably better than others and make it worse. Sometimes it's because the hue and cry of the mob of players (most who are young and often toxic) sometimes it's to sell a new premium vehicle. Last, a word of advice: Free to Play is wholly misleading. Some players pride themselves on climbing the ranks with out paying a dime. They cry about 'pay to win' players but often this is because they don't have a job and don't comprehend that the game is developed as a business. For those playing in places with depressed economies, there is no scaling of costs however and for someone somewhere else in the world paying $80 for a premium vehicle is insane, where as here it's less than a day's wages.

review:
★★★★★ — I came to save the world and ended up committing tax fraud against a chicken.

Started the game by getting arrested for apparently existing in the wrong place at the wrong time. About 5 minutes later, a dragon attacks and suddenly nobody gives a shit anymore. Immigration policy? Forgotten. Due process? Gone. Anyway, I'm the Dragonborn now.

Fast forward 20 hours and I've somehow just found out that horses and companions die. I also have a major hoarding problem and can't run anymore.

game: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review:
上古卷轴 5 作为一款 2011 年发布的游戏，其内容大致为扮演一个幸运的天选之人在开放世界地图上探索和冒险，顺着主线认识、寻找和完成自己的使命，并遇见不同的角色。

如果用一句话评价，我会说「这是一款具有开创性的商业化开放世界老式ARPG游戏」。

上古卷轴 5 有很多当时新鲜而现在看来则是细致的游戏机制，从在当时较为新鲜的基于双手的装备机制、各种各样的龙吼能力、有物理效果并且可交互的物品效果，到融合一体的战斗、炼药、武器打造、技能树系统，作为一个ARPG给了很高的游玩自由度，相似地玩法让人想起 Elona（一个2009年的回合制RPG，但同样有着甚至更为有趣的系统）。上古卷轴 5 的玩法即便放到今天依然不过时，可以称作是大师之作。

游戏的画面虽然在 2026 看来已经有些糟糕，但是其底子依旧有股神韵，尤其是当视角看向刚刚跳下的巨大雪山之时，看见山路和云雾缭绕很难想象刚从一个现在看起来很可能存在空气墙的地方跳下来。而除了山，各个城市的独特风光也让人印象深刻，最好的一点证明是我去一座城市就会明显感觉到这座城市和其他地方的明显不同。

因为这些基底，上古卷轴 5 即便放在今天依旧是一款不错的好游戏。但同时放在今天也会出现其所欠缺的设计问题以及其他问题。

game: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review:
适合老人用于怀旧和回忆青春，不适合新人游玩。基于其在游戏史上的崇高地位，在那个年代对比其他游戏无疑是开创性的，但用现在的游戏眼光看狗屎的地方太多。用现在的游戏标准来衡量它无疑是苛刻的，可毕竟我玩的老游戏也不算少了，我用同时代的游戏标准来简单说明一下它的缺点——毕竟这些缺点横跨至今，且用现在的眼光来看更加的恶劣。
1、狗屎的UI设计和UI逻辑：内容如此浩大的游戏UI做的跟屎一样，这点从老滚5开始到后面的辐射系列都没有改观。超级小陶希望你用超级大脑来记住你在游戏里面干过什么没干过什么，而不是简单的添加一个未查看的红点表明。装备和武器栏的堆叠比陶德全家的乱葬岗还要混乱，我见过按最近获得时间排序，也见过按装备价值排序，实在不行你按装备类型排序，哪怕是按首字母排序也好啊。你有这么多种选择方式，我CNMD老滚选择了乱序。我永远搞不清我的装备到底在哪里，法杖里面混合着近战又混着几张弓，更别提你这sm游戏压根没设计装备栏，你脱换装备还要去背包里面一个个找。那个偏爱设置简直脑瘫，你手柄配置十字键做一个上是近战，下是远程，左是魔法，右是药水很难吗？nmlg的全勾巴堆在一起，搞这么长一列，你不觉得反人类吗？那我问你，你空的另外按键是干嘛的？留着给你妈坟头种花吗？还有那个送信的，你妈逼的不能做个当场阅读吗？给你直接塞进背包，也不跟你说道具名字，然后让你在背包你捡的一堆垃圾书里面按照乱序来找到那封未读的信，我真是cnm了。
2、sm游戏流程：首先你勾巴主线支线能不能分两个栏呢，别有的在其他，有的又在任务总览里面？而且你勾巴接的支线能不能有点合理度？显摆自己有大地图：”哇撒我们的游戏太自由了，你开局想去哪里就去哪里“。那你能不能别他妈搞成我在地图左下角接个任务，告诉我任务点在地图右上角这种事？你自己在白漫接接支线看看，你看看你这些 sm任务都在地图的哪些地方？你一方面又有地区等级和难度的设置，一方面又搞这种满天星式的支线，是不是有点过于逆天了？你们自己做完游戏自己不玩的？你们的游戏规划做到随进度发放任务对你们来说很难吗？
3、cjb更新：你不会真觉得你游戏口碑销量双丰收，全是自己做的好吧？你B社能有现在的光景，那么多MOD作者给你们贡献了多少心血？所以我的意思，如果你们不是完全傻逼的话应该也知道mod对你们游戏的重要性。那既然如此，wcnmd你们这帮傻逼他妈的2026年还在这勾巴更新什么东西呢？你们这帮司马玩意真能更新出个三七二十一我也就不说话了，cnmd的隔三岔五搞个小补丁把mod全整失效，然后我登游戏一看：你BUG也没修啊？那我问你，你们这帮司马玩意到底在这里更新什么东西？不恶心人你们是难受是吗？
除了这三点是这款超越时代的游戏上的超越时代的问题，你在真正游玩过程中的小问题还有很多——像是什么疾跑的时候不能跳（我不知道为什么这种地方不去做）；偷窃和犯罪系统过于逆天（你永远不知道为什么没人看见也算犯罪以及罪行不被逮住永远不清零这种逆天设定）；不明所以的随从系统（你甚至不能像古早RPG一样随意更换他们的装备外观，以及小丑AI）等等等等。所以我还是那句话，老滚五适合当年那批人用于缅怀自己的青春，怀念曾经的青葱岁月，不适合现在以及以后的新人游玩。

review: 好玩，好玩，这个11年的老游戏是我之前国庆促销买的，一开始是看价格这么低评分又这么高买的。虽然我完全是一个老滚5小白，完全没有玩过之前b社的游戏，也不太了解陶德什么的，但是玩了147个小时后依旧意犹未尽。画质很古老，不过是11年的游戏可以理解，繁体有点难受，不过有很简单的简体汉化mod，我也只是打了这一个，毕竟我算一个比较纯粹的游戏玩家，喜欢玩纯粹一点。战斗操作手法确实很没有打击感，也很不习惯，玩这么久也没有发现身体部位暴击什么的，比如打头没有暴击的感觉，当然也有可能是因为没有伤害数字什么的，只能纯看敌人血量条来判断。负重什么的很难受，不过也很真实，不可能一开始就有无限背包，要加耐力点或者专门的装备才可以提升。至于升级只给一点属性和升级慢也确实难受，不过游戏里有很多训练老师可以帮忙升级，不过要钱，技能等级升得越高钱要得越多，不过有一点很好玩的就是，有的技能训练师可以招募为随从，然后花的钱可以拿回来，可以白嫖。个人感觉最好玩的是偷窃这个技能，非常不可思议，当我把技能点满后可以对大多数npc扒光，让我对于偷窃这个技能有非常强的交互感。然后就是开放程度，虽然感觉地图很小，骑马一个小时差不多可以横跨地图（马也是真的慢，不过爬山确实好用，玩家和马简直是岩羊来的，是坡就能爬），但是npc的生活轨迹确实存在，这是现在大部分我玩过的游戏都没有的感觉，特别是好感度这个东西，现在大部分游戏的好感度系统是显性的，就是确实可以看见的，但是老滚5的隐性的，表现在拿东西这个方面，npc并不是只会在特定地方，而是有自己的生活轨迹（这点让人又爱又恨，因为找人确实有点麻烦）。最好玩的应该是动态的任务与实力系统，简单说就是没有等级限制和必须要完成的任务说法，虽然龙裔确实是主线，但是你不推也可以玩下去，我现在玩147小时只是推到要猎杀第一条龙的地步。很多看起来非常强的boss靠磨也是可以推过去的，并不需要要很好的武器或者准备什么的，我到目前为止最难的一个任务也是3小时磨过去的，不过后面等级上去，也快了很多。还有就是在游戏里的书是真的有用，虽然有的书看了会升技能导致我之前一直认为书只是升技能的，但是在我无聊看书的时候确实发现很多东西确实可以用，比如神射手这本书，还有附魔标准（应该是这个名字吧，有点记不清了），讲的东西确实都有用，还有一些书让我很惊奇，就是猩红匕首这本书，里面的人物并不只是传说，游戏里面确确实实是有相关人物的........还有太多太多给我惊喜的地方。总的来说，老滚5游戏手感还有画质差了很多，但是其他方面方放到现在依旧是一个好游戏。

review:
我要给⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐五颗星
从13年传奇版玩到现在的游戏，本人特别喜欢开放世界RPG游戏，算是最喜欢的游戏之一。游戏剧情特别丰富，世界观也很特色，BGM也非常好听，有一种厚重的历史感和神话感，尤其游戏里夜晚的时候跑着跑着来到山顶或者大海那边，BGM响起的时候，感觉置身其中，有一种空灵的孤寂。游戏里有非常多的NPC，几乎每个有名字的NPC都有自己的故事和人设，就好像一个个真实存在的人，有各种各样的故事各种各样的性格，支线比主线量多很多。玩过很多这种类型的游戏，但是只有老滚是我觉得真的在扮演自己的角色。游戏开始没有什么新手教程，就直接开始了任务，但是其实玩完才发现，游戏设计很有巧思，所有新手教程都在路上，玩着玩着就会了。

玩过的所有游戏里这个游戏是我玩的时间最久的，开放时间RPG游戏启蒙，至今找不到完美代餐。所有主线和支线全部刷完，地图也清空了N遍，最后只剩下反反复复的工会和领主任务，这大概花了两三年吧，当然中间我是有作弊过的，不然正常玩的话没有三五年很难清完这么多任务，快死的时候我会开无敌因为不想读档，也不得不作弊，因为有的任务卡bug了，只能用代码跳过或者重来。而且很多任务都有二选一或者阵营这种情况，一般我都会保存然后玩两遍任务看到两种不同的结局，但是像帝国和风暴斗篷这种阵营的剧情线比较长就不得不开两个档玩了。我有点完美主义和强迫症和收集癖，其实在清完任务和地图后，又反反复复清图，希望找到没有探索到的领域或者物品可以收藏或者什么隐藏任务。真的希望地图能再大些任务能再多些，如果有做不完的任务探索不完的地图就好了。

游戏本身很优秀，但是对于现在想入坑的人，我只能说谨慎，因为游戏太老，对比现在的游戏，首先画质差，新手引导差，自由度过高不知道做什么，接不完的任务，走着走着就不小心接了几个任务越堆越多，引擎也老，bug很多，新人很容易劝退，有很多人听说这个游戏好玩耐玩来玩，结果发现根本不是这样，觉得别人吹太过了，容易半途而废，所以不是适合所有人。

整合包和MOD比较考验耐心，如果想接触整合包和MOD，不建议花钱，就算找人安装了，后面的事情也很多，自己早晚要学会安装，自给自足丰衣足食。整合包和MOD的安装其实非常简单一看就会，耐心点不要跳步骤。难的是自己乱安装MOD导致的MOD冲突和排序问题，新手不建议自己乱装东西，游戏引擎很老，MOD和MOD之间兼容性没那么好，如果有补丁可以修复。注意百分之九十九的MOD都是免费的。

game: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review:
一部把沉浸感做到极致的RPG，极致在主角没有名字没有过去，龙裔的一切都由玩家塑造，所以玩家就是龙裔，玩家就是活在天际省的那个人。滚5在我心中至今仍是一部无可替代的作品，玩老滚的那段时间正是我对现实感到最迷茫的日子（34h是补票以后玩的，在这之前我大概玩了一个多月，每天晚上都在通宵），沉浸在那个世界越久我越是对现实感到恍惚，有次我在三次元把什么事情搞砸了，我的大脑第一反应竟然是点F9。
马上就是15周年了，杯赛能不能像滚4重置那样再给我们一个惊喜？

game: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review: 上古卷轴5是真正最让我有一种自己穿越到了异世界的感受的游戏，B社在开放世界RPG中的诸多设计，都重在让玩家做自己而非扮演某个既定的角色，我可以随心所欲地自由探索、做任何事。一方面，这个世界不仅有着足够厚重的历史背景与世界观塑造，当下正在发生的、能参与的大小事件与故事也极其丰富；另一方面，它不像别的游戏那样有一个存在感非常强的主线脉络牵着你走、让人产生一种推“进度条”的感觉——上古卷轴5的主线任务本质上更像一条体量较大的支线，完成后旅程并不会就此结束，真正的主线其实是玩家自己在这个世界里体验所有内容的先后顺序，始终给人一种没有终点的漫游感。同时，玩上古卷轴5时的会有的一种沙盒的感觉也非常的重要，是能够即开即玩让我一秒沉浸，也可以随时放下的游戏，没有一点点的负担。因此对我个人来说，上古卷轴5的游玩感受是从系统层面和底层逻辑上就与其他游戏完全不一样，这种沉浸代入感是几乎完全无法被其他任何游戏替代的。

game: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review:
[h2]【Hey, you. You're finally awake.】[/h2] 
[h2]总分：88/100   校准分：1.1207[/h2]
tag：CRPG，开放世界，奇幻，剧情，Mod社区

[h3]游戏性：23/25[/h3]
从一开场，滚5就展现了高超的制作水平。你和你操控的角色都是初到天际，对背景故事一无所知，在马车上的交谈中窥见世界的一角，在刑场登记信息时捏脸，在逃离龙的袭击时学会移动，在与帝国兵的冲突中学会基本的战斗操作，在地牢中搜刮物品学会和环境互动和开锁，在躲藏熊的时候学会潜行……直到逃出洞穴，看到远处覆雪的荒瀑古坟，一首《Far Horizons》响起，你完全自由了，在这个陌生的天际。没有给定的任务路线，没有空气墙和等级限制，“看见那座山了吗？你可以爬上去。”
经验值不来自杀敌，不来自完成任务，不来自白痴学者，玩家变强的路只有一条：你玩得多。滚5的等级来自于你所有熟练项的熟练度的总和，刀剑、魔法、锻造、炼金、附魔……所有技能的起点都是一样的，玩家不需要在一开始就决定存档里要当什么职业吃什么增益，你只需要多尝试自然就会了。当然也不排除一些技能设计失衡，譬如无脑强的钳工流和三神左脚踩右脚。一些技能的形同滚木，滚5的口才系统相比于辐射实属是一坨，除了能少花点钱和跳过一些重复劳动以外毫无用处，无法获得任何额外的重要信息；开锁技能树更是全程几乎零收益。再由于开场中没有法术教学，加之剧情中诺德人的文化旋律，本游戏的法术系统一直都有些被忽视，大部分玩家包括我除非被堵路或推剧情都鲜少使用魔法。但起码在原版内容里，法术的丰富程度要远胜于冷兵器，五大学派的法术设计都很完善，输出、奶、幻术或是摇人，玩法选择比只有我砍我再砍的近战武器好太多了。
任务设计，优秀夹杂着平庸。滚5有大量剧情优秀体验沉浸的任务线，主线、内战、战友团、工会、兄弟会、学院、龙裔和黎明守卫8条中除了内战战友团学院稍逊，其余几条甚至足以拿来单开一部3A游戏。除此还有大量游离在线外的优秀魔神任务和城市任务。但还是有两大缺点：1.依旧有不少通马桶，事实上滚5的马桶是无限制的，在你把地图杀光前无限刷新。而精品支线是有限的，且大部分都可以在第一次抵达相关城市获取，因此不难感受到玩得越久、马桶含量越高。2.任务分支平淡，绝大多数任务都是线性的，不像辐射和博德任务的错综，实话讲滚5还远远没有摸到网状叙事的门槛，剩下的一小部分也常常只是一个道德层面的二择。
不避讳地说，和互联网大多数人的观点一样，滚5原版的打击感确实是一坨大便，但处决动画还挺帅的。如果你作为资深老屁股不在意这些便无所谓，如果在意可以通过打Attack MCO-DXP来解决。

[h3]美学：19/20[/h3]
天际，诺德，粗犷的北境。大地的绝大部分由白雪覆盖，冻岩冻土上永远飘荡着不死的冰雾，地势崎岖山峦耸立，天空绝大部分时间只雾蒙蒙，偶尔才能瞥见几眼太阳，让远处山的轮廓可见。星空，极光和两颗卫星之下，到处都是废弃的洞穴、古坟和矮人遗迹，被强盗和弃誓者盘踞，山花、浆果、草荚、松和其他枯树是主流的植被，远处时不时传来龙的吼叫。遍布薰衣草的白漫、四季如秋的裂谷、山岩拼接的马卡斯、偶然出现的巨大神像和湮灭领域风格迥异的建筑与装潢点缀这个冰冷的世界，天际的美术充满了灵魂。独自行走在其中，正如同本作11年11月11日的发售时间一般孤独。
叙事方面，许多任务线的叙事都相当优秀，保持了高度的戏剧冲突：玩家在黑暗兄弟会执行重大刺杀任务的同时不得不卷入组织内部的权力斗争、黎明守卫的推动就意味着和哈孔的对抗等；人物塑造也相当鲜明，瑟拉娜、帕图纳克斯、西塞罗等角色都令人印象深刻；但叙事节奏拉胯：全程站桩对话，NPC走路时而墨迹时而又不等人。环境本身也在叙事，一处强盗营地的信件、尸体和物品摆放，就可以让玩家推测这里发生了什么，一个疯乞丐的言语，就能透露村子尘封的历史，这些叙事不直接服务任务，却在细枝末节中透出世界的真实感。玩家也是一种叙事，你做过什么，城中的卫兵会对此夸赞或者讽刺，NPC会出现额外的对话选项。
上古卷轴的世界观是我见过最奇特的虚构世界观。在全天际中你能获得大量不同主题和类型的书籍，你会发现其中不同的种族对不同的神称呼、看法和历史记载均不一，模糊的历史为玩家提供了充分的想象空间和代入感。如同真实的世界一样，你不知道为什么遗迹会长成那样、为什么政治和宗教会在此冲突，但这确实发生了。这是一种相比碎片化叙事更高明的手法。

[h3]游戏哲学：10/10[/h3]
想尽办法让玩家沉浸在游戏其中，这是Bethesda长期坚持的设计理念中的首要一件。沉浸感，一切夸赞上古卷轴5的文案都会提及的部分。在游戏中，玩家不再是一个扮演主角剧本的外世之人，我就是龙裔本身，我做的就是龙裔做的，龙裔的行为就是我的行为，在小小的屏幕中，二者完全达成了统一。不知多少次当我关闭exe，转头望向窗外微白的天空时，猛然意识到又回到了原来的世界，变成了一个其他的角色。
NPC的灵性绝对是讨论上古卷轴5时无法绕开的。每个城市中数十个有名有姓的NPC都有一套自己的行程表，日出而作日入而息、偶尔去一趟城里的神殿祈祷、或在酒店做些站场子的工作，熟悉的人相互遇到的时候也会交流打趣，即使没有玩家，天际省的时间依旧能自然流动下去。当然玩家对NPC造成的交互也同样生动，会问是吸血鬼或狼人的玩家身上的某些特征，玩家掏出武器和魔法时让玩家放下或走开，根据玩家不同的技能水平做出点评；玩家直接或间接造成NPC的死亡，他的家人可能会改变对你的态度和台词，甚至改变自己的工作。当你路过路边两个天天争吵的NPC并插了一次话后，可能就会开启一小时甚至几小时的一条支线任务。NPC在玩家的眼中变得更加重要，而不是一堆围着转的工具人。这是一个你不用只盯着头上冒出感叹号的NPC的游戏，NPC的设计正是上古卷轴5沉浸感的第一大来源。
十五年后回头来看，滚5的城市简直就是一个破村子，村子更是两栋烂房子拼成的怎么看都像在从事非法活动的不明聚集点。但这在我看来完全不是缺点，NPC可以密集聚居，方便他们之间的演出，游戏里的几乎每栋房子都有有名有姓的NPC可以交流触发任务推动剧情。嘴一下Bethesda，这种良好习惯自辐射4就不再有了，为了扩充地图那个byd新手村康科德就开始加入一堆无法进入的房屋，实属破坏体验。野外的兴趣地点也相当丰富，可以说滚5用着系列最小的地图容纳了系列最丰富的内容，许多地点可能同时有二到三条任务一同指向，一个任务又涉及两三个地点，清晰又庞大的任务网便这么展开了。游戏后期打开地图，看着立体的3D地图和上面密密麻麻承载故事的地点，充实感油然而生。地图设计的优秀是沉浸感的另一大来源。
所见即所得。滚5的所有生物都有着和玩家一视同仁的逻辑，背包里有什么就用什么穿什么，掉落物品不再是一坨预设好的序列，你看到一个强盗头头有发光的宝剑，杀了他或偷过来就能拿到，看到一个贵族有钻石制的项链，杀了他或偷过来就能拿到，不会有随机爆神级戒指的小龙虾、不用天天蹲在性价比高的野怪刷新点。一切杂物都有自己的独立建模，可以被随意摆在桌上扔在地上或扣在NPC的头上，更好的盾牌不是仅仅数值高一点，你可以在物品栏打开它，放大查看细节、雕纹，就和在NPC和你手上拿的时候一样。这是第三大来源。

[h3]完成度：8/15[/h3]
Bug, bug never changes. 玩家会自己生产优化游戏的内容，这便是Bethesda所坚持的第二件。我的沉浸感不知多少次被Bug破坏得粉碎，九圣灵在上，不是所有bug都如同巨人航天一样有意思。
另外从不少代码和隐藏房间中可以看出，Bethesda自己也砍掉了不少有意思的支线，算是这个制作组的通病了。

[h3]内容量：10/10[/h3]
十五年已过，天际依旧是社区活力最强规模最庞大的单机游戏。可能这个title不会改变，如果你在滚6发行之前不幸趋势了。我全成就用了190h。具体内容可见“游戏哲学”一栏。
但是聊上古卷轴不可避免的便是它的mod社区。Creation Engine这个引擎就拥有这么一个神奇的魔力，一切都可以自己修改。画质上跟不上时代了？我们有高清纹理mod、光影优化mod、光追路追mod、高模mod、天气系统mod，角色改进更是完全开出了一片新领域。战斗太无聊了？我们有动作系统mod、伤害系统mod，你可完全把它改装成ARPG。内容不够玩？我们有数不清的内容拓展mod，新任务、新地区、新的剧情NPC。细节不够精致？站桩对话修改mod、丰富婚姻系统mod、自由视角mod、UImod……而且，模组前置的机制可以让mod身上再长出mod，把你想要的继续客制化。不少优秀的任务mod会被官方转正成游戏内容，甚至一个新的二创游戏。这是一个由玩家作为创作者的平台，但bethesda的吃相实在是太sm了，差评中99%都是有关这点的。

[h3]创新性：9/10[/h3]
第一个大满贯游戏，划时代的意义。把辐射3/新维加斯那种传统的桌游化的CRPG体系大幅改进，复杂的系统在新玩家眼中尽可能消失，但在老玩家眼中又不失深度，是一种相当适合电子游戏的设计理念。

[h3]黑箱：9/10[/h3]
陶大炮，我再信你一次。

任务设计，优秀夹杂着平庸。滚5有大量剧情优秀体验沉浸的任务线，主线、内战、战友团、工会、兄弟会、学院、龙裔和黎明守卫8条中除了内战战友团学院稍逊，其余几条甚至足以拿来单开一部3a游戏。除此还有大量游离在线外的优秀魔神任务和城市任务。但还是有两大缺点：1.依旧有不少通马桶，事实上滚5的马桶是无限制的，在你把地图杀光前无限刷新。而精品支线是有限的，且大部分都可以在第一次抵达相关城市获取，因此不难感受到玩得越久、马桶含量越高。2.任务分支平淡，绝大多数任务都是线性的，不像辐射和博德任务的错综，实话讲滚5还远远没有摸到网状叙事的门槛，剩下的一小部分也常常只是一个道德层面的二择。 不避讳地说，和互联网大多数人的观点一样，滚5原版的打击感确实是一坨大便，但处决动画还挺帅的。如果你作为资深老屁股不在意这些便无所谓，如果在意可以通过打attack mco-dxp来解决。 [h3]美学：19/20[/h3] 天际，诺德，粗犷的北境。大地的绝大部分由白雪覆盖，冻岩冻土上永远飘荡着不死的冰雾，地势崎岖山峦耸立，天空绝大部分时间只雾蒙蒙，偶尔才能瞥见几眼太阳，让远处山的轮廓可见。星空，极光和两颗卫星之下，到处都是废弃的洞穴、古坟和矮人遗迹，被强盗和弃誓者盘踞，山花、浆果、草荚、松和其他枯树是主流的植被，远处时不时传来龙的吼叫。遍布薰衣草的白漫、四季如秋的裂谷、山岩拼接的马卡斯、偶然出现的巨大神像和湮灭领域风格迥异的建筑与装潢点缀这个冰冷的世界，天际的美术充满了灵魂。独自行走在其中，正如同本作11年11月11日的发售时间一般孤独。 叙事方面，许多任务线的叙事都相当优秀，保持了高度的戏剧冲突：玩家在黑暗兄弟会执行重大刺杀任务的同时不得不卷入组织内部的权力斗争、黎明守卫的推动就意味着和哈孔的对抗等；人物塑造也相当鲜明，瑟拉娜、帕图纳克斯、西塞罗等角色都令人印象深刻；但叙事节奏拉胯：全程站桩对话，npc走路时而墨迹时而又不等人。环境本身也在叙事，一处强盗营地的信件、尸体和物品摆放，就可以让玩家推测这里发生了什么，一个疯乞丐的言语，就能透露村子尘封的历史，这些叙事不直接服务任务，却在细枝末节中透出世界的真实感。玩家也是一种叙事，你做过什么，城中的卫兵会对此夸赞或者讽刺，npc会出现额外的对话选项。 上古卷轴的世界观是我见过最奇特的虚构世界观。在全天际中你能获得大量不同主题和类型的书籍，你会发现其中不同的种族对不同的神称呼、看法和历史记载均不一，模糊的历史为玩家提供了充分的想象空间和代入感。如同真实的世界一样，你不知道为什么遗迹会长成那样、为什么政治和宗教会在此冲突，但这确实发生了。这是一种相比碎片化叙事更高明的手法。 [h3]游戏哲学：10/10[/h3] 想尽办法让玩家沉浸在游戏其中，这是bethesda长期坚持的设计理念中的首要一件。沉浸感，一切夸赞上古卷轴5的文案都会提及的部分。在游戏中，玩家不再是一个扮演主角剧本的外世之人，我就是龙裔本身，我做的就是龙裔做的，龙裔的行为就是我的行为，在小小的屏幕中，二者完全达成了统一。不知多少次当我关闭exe，转头望向窗外微白的天空时，猛然意识到又回到了原来的世界，变成了一个其他的角色。 npc的灵性绝对是讨论上古卷轴5时无法绕开的。每个城市中数十个有名有姓的npc都有一套自己的行程表，日出而作日入而息、偶尔去一趟城里的神殿祈祷、或在酒店做些站场子的工作，熟悉的人相互遇到的时候也会交流打趣，即使没有玩家，天际省的时间依旧能自然流动下去。当然玩家对npc造成的交互也同样生动，会问是吸血鬼或狼人的玩家身上的某些特征，玩家掏出武器和魔法时让玩家放下或走开，根据玩家不同的技能水平做出点评；玩家直接或间接造成npc的死亡，他的家人可能会改变对你的态度和台词，甚至改变自己的工作。当你路过路边两个天天争吵的npc并插了一次话后，可能就会开启一小时甚至几小时的一条支线任务。npc在玩家的眼中变得更加重要，而不是一堆围着转的工具人。这是一个你不用只盯着头上冒出感叹号的npc的游戏，npc的设计正是上古卷轴5沉浸感的第一大来源。 十五年后回头来看，滚5的城市简直就是一个破村子，村子更是两栋烂房子拼成的怎么看都像在从事非法活动的不明聚集点。但这在我看来完全不是缺点，npc可以密集聚居，方便他们之间的演出，游戏里的几乎每栋房子都有有名有姓的npc可以交流触发任务推动剧情。嘴一下bethesda，这种良好习惯自辐射4就不再有了，为了扩充地图那个byd新手村康科德就开始加入一堆无法进入的房屋，实属破坏体验。野外的兴趣地点也相当丰富，可以说滚5用着系列最小的地图容纳了系列最丰富的内容，许多地点可能同时有二到三条任务一同指向，一个任务又涉及两三个地点，清晰又庞大的任务网便这么展开了。游戏后期打开地图，看着立体的3d地图和上面密密麻麻承载故事的地点，充实感油然而生。地图设计的优秀是沉浸感的另一大来源。 所见即所得。滚5的所有生物都有着和玩家一视同仁的逻辑，背包里有什么就用什么穿什么，掉落物品不再是一坨预设好的序列，你看到一个强盗头头有发光的宝剑，杀了他或偷过来就能拿到，看到一个贵族有钻石制的项链，杀了他或偷过来就能拿到，不会有随机爆神级戒指的小龙虾、不用天天蹲在性价比高的野怪刷新点。一切杂物都有自己的独立建模，可以被随意摆在桌上扔在地上或扣在npc的头上，更好的盾牌不是仅仅数值高一点，你可以在物品栏打开它，放大查看细节、雕纹，就和在npc和你手上拿的时候一样。这是第三大来源。 [h3]完成度：8/15[/h3] bug, bug never changes. 玩家会自己生产优化游戏的内容，这便是bethesda所坚持的第二件。我的沉浸感不知多少次被bug破坏得粉碎，九圣灵在上，不是所有bug都如同巨人航天一样有意思。 另外从不少代码和隐藏房间中可以看出，bethesda自己也砍掉了不少有意思的支线，算是这个制作组的通病了。 [h3]内容量：10/10[/h3] 十五年已过，天际依旧是社区活力最强规模最庞大的单机游戏。可能这个title不会改变，如果你在滚6发行之前不幸趋势了。我全成就用了190h。具体内容可见“游戏哲学”一栏。 但是聊上古卷轴不可避免的便是它的mod社区。creation engine这个引擎就拥有这么一个神奇的魔力，一切都可以自己修改。画质上跟不上时代了？我们有高清纹理mod、光影优化mod、光追路追mod、高模mod、天气系统mod，角色改进更是完全开出了一片新领域。战斗太无聊了？我们有动作系统mod、伤害系统mod，你可完全把它改装成arpg。内容不够玩？我们有数不清的内容拓展mod，新任务、新地区、新的剧情npc。细节不够精致？站桩对话修改mod、丰富婚姻系统mod、自由视角mod、uimod……而且，模组前置的机制可以让mod身上再长出mod，把你想要的继续客制化。不少优秀的任务mod会被官方转正成游戏内容，甚至一个新的二创游戏。这是一个由玩家作为创作者的平台，但bethesda的吃相实在是太sm了，差评中99%都是有关这点的。 [h3]创新性：9/10[/h3] 第一个大满贯游戏，划时代的意义。把辐射3/新维加斯那种传统的桌游化的crpg体系大幅改进，复杂的系统在新玩家眼中尽可能消失，但在老玩家眼中又不失深度，是一种相当适合电子游戏的设计理念。 [h3]黑箱：9/10[/h3] 陶大炮，我再信你一次。

review: 第一人称最最最有代入感的游戏，初见第一眼直接五颗星，这就是我一直在寻找的游戏，根据环境零秒猜出自己要完蛋，想操作一下手让人捆上了，对的对的，转生到异世界被死刑，幻想直接变成现实，看着铡刀实在是太有意思了，就是这个剧情有点可惜，都在意料之内，人物塑造的很鲜活，本来虎视眈眈要我首级的大姐姐转头就去守护更重要的人们了，准备偷偷趁乱跑路，老哥们直接招呼我正大光明偷跑，听他叽里咕噜讲半天就记得跑了，给我物资挠挠头就收下了，还让我过去亲手解开捆我的绳子，这种听不懂又差点听懂的感觉真让人抓心挠肝啊，真的有初入异世界的感觉，寒冷，饥饿，还有魔法，对的对的对的，这就是新的生活，辗转到村口只能睡村外捡垃圾吃，以为接了个大活结果不包吃住，贤者之石历经艰险给你揣回来，没见着奖励你跟我说有新任务了，任务奖励是新任务，居然还能被npc压榨了，还准备看看新任务是啥呢直接给我困迷糊了，一看状态肚子都饿凹进去了，找那老商人npc居然不卖盐，我去了，兜里揣了瓶包治百病的万灵药，我一口下去给我那老风湿都治好了，结果不卖盐，我顶着砍头罪搁老dragon屁股底下偷了四包盐，你让我上哪吃饭去，欸哟我，不说了，我要饿晕了，我尝尝蘑菇啥味吧

review:
时至今日，当众多新作追逐华丽画面与强引导叙事，《上古卷轴 5：天际》依旧是奇幻 RPG 不可逾越的丰碑。这片风雪笼罩的天际省，并非简单的游戏地图，而是一个呼吸着的诺德史诗世界。雪山与古冢、城镇与荒野之间，巨龙的咆哮回荡群山，古老的预言与内战纠葛交织。

它最伟大之处，在于给予玩家全然的自由。你不必被迫成为英雄，可做莽夫、法师、盗贼，循着自己的意志漫游。卷帙浩繁的典籍、鲜活的众生，构筑起厚重的泰姆瑞尔传说。即便岁月流逝，依托庞大 MOD 社群，天际仍生生不息。这是一部可供亲身踏入的奇幻史诗，所有热爱欧美 RPG 之人，都应当造访这片风雪大地。龙裔的宿命悬于头顶，你却可以搁置屠龙大业，流连于白漫城的酒馆，听吟游诗人传唱古老歌谣；或是深入地下古墓，探寻诺德亡灵守护的秘密。这片土地里的每一个小人物都承载着细碎故事，农夫的争执、流亡者的求助、黑夜里盗贼的密谋，交织成主线之外鲜活的人间。泰姆瑞尔大陆漫长的历史藏在遍布全省的书本与遗迹之中。翻开发黄的书卷，便能窥见湮灭危机、龙战争的遥远过往，厚重的奇幻设定并非空洞的背景板，而是沉淀在山川遗迹里的真实。行走在群山之间，风穿过松涛，远处隐约传来龙吼，这种沉浸式的旷野体验，时至今日依旧动人。

以当下标准审视，重置版的画面、动作系统难免陈旧，地牢设计也偶有重复。但这些表层缺陷，无法撼动其灵魂。MOD 社群长久的耕耘，不断翻新视觉效果、扩充故事，让天际跨越时代。《上古卷轴 5》的伟大，是它守住了老式欧美 RPG 最珍贵的内核：冒险不是完成任务清单，而是一段独属于你的旅途与选择。

2026了，风雪长存，龙鸣仍犹在，这片北国大地永远等候冒险者前来，没有什么唯一正确的故事走向，只有你写下的经历，才是天际真正的传奇。

review:
缺点：1，画质还是差点意思。2，bug太多，各种任务卡bug，还有死灵法师吸血鬼之类，夜莺剑无法锻造，多得说不完。3，周年版非常不稳定，大概玩1小时就要闪退。4，没有简中。
优点：1，代入感极好，制作组呕心沥血编写的虚拟世界，体现在游戏内诸多方面，如大量书，极大的丰富了世界观，npc来自世界各地，旁敲侧击告诉你这里只是天际省，深入刻画各种npc的人生，以及npc自己的生活。2，升级系统十分合理，不仅体现在逻辑上，也体现在游玩过程上，你越使用一个技能，它就会越来越强，直到登峰造极。3，非常自由，选择权在你手里，对话选项不是做出来看着玩的，不仅是任务分支自由，还有就是战斗可以混搭，比如重甲毁法。而且不做等级限制，导致你熟悉套路可以各种开局

简单评价：你游玩在这里，你居住在这里，你创造在这里。愿你的前方是一片温暖的沙地。
补票后迫不及待打了全成就，遂把曾经在其他地方写的东西搬过来。

2022.5.12
昨天晚上，五十二级的我终于和男朋友威尔卡斯结婚了
说实话，一开始纯看脸选的他，后来觉得这个狼人弟弟真的蛮可爱，尤其是他看到我戴着玛拉护身符时说那句npc固定台词：“你居然没有结婚，真难得。”
他在神庙里说至死不渝，他说永不离开，他在说这些时还会偏着头看我

review:
My all-time favorite game, but I can only give it one star

I’ve put hundreds of hours into Skyrim across multiple saves. Two of my old playthroughs never hit the Chillrend sound bug at all, but my newest save finally ran into it, and it’s so frustrating.

Chillrend has a looping frost hiss sound when drawn. This bug happens when the audio stop command gets lost during cell changes, loading screens or quick weapon swaps. Unlike Dawnbreaker or most enchanted weapons that only play a short one-off sound, this is a looping effect. Once it glitches out, the sound sticks to your character forever. Sheathe the sword, drop it, even delete it — the noise stays. It survives restarts and save reloads. Open a menu and it quiets briefly, only to come back right after. Pull Chillrend out again while the bug is active and you stack multiple layers of the hiss, which gets painfully loud.

Since I play in third-person, I only noticed this Chillrend audio bug much later, forcing me to load a save from dozens of hours back and wasting days of my playtime.

The vanilla workarounds are janky at best. Using `sexchange` twice or turning into a werewolf can temporarily clear the sound, but it comes back on reload. Worse, `sexchange` breaks the Ranger archery perk and removes its movement speed boost. There’s no reliable native fix in the base game. Trying to force-trigger the stop command by sheathing and teleporting at the same time only makes it worse and adds more overlapping audio.

And it’s not just the Chillrend bug. The Creation Club homes are packed with well-known issues too. Weapon racks and plaques eat stored weapons, many display cases won’t accept gear. Dragon claws float off their mounts. Some adopted kids can’t move in, pets sometimes vanish or get sent to the wrong house. Mannequins lock onto one set of armor, push out any new gear you put on them, and duplicate that old armor when you leave the area and come back. Items jump all over the place every time you enter these homes, way more so than regular Hearthfire houses. Most display cases don’t work properly as displays at all.

Serana also has her own annoying bugs. She will stop following you in basements and can disappear randomly. Her hood duplicates infinitely, stacking hundreds of copies in her inventory and making trading items impossible.

On top of all these bugs, the base game volume is way too low. Compared to nearly every other game, even older ones like GTA V, Skyrim’s overall sound level feels like it’s only one third as loud. Every single time I boot it up, I have to crank my system volume. When I finish playing and jump on TikTok without turning it back down, the sudden blast of sound has startled me and even gotten me complaints from neighbours.
I don’t want to sound harsh, but it’s unbelievable that pirated versions of Skyrim can run better with fewer bugs. The only extra thing this official version offers is the pointless achievement system.

It feels like Bethesda just doesn’t care about polishing these long-standing quality-of-life problems. The community has to make mods to patch everything for them. Players end up doing the dev team’s job instead of just enjoying the game. It’s disappointing. GTA V is just as old, yet it feels polished and optimized. Meanwhile Bethesda chases big projects like Starfield. It’s like taking a warrior and forcing them to slog through boring, drawn-out religious texts.

It is my all-time favourite game, yet also the buggiest. Bethesda is just as arrogant as Valve is with CS2. But my negative review reflects my real experience. I’m here to play a game, to enjoy something as a person, not to suffer and do your work for you.

review:
[h1] NARAKA: BLADEPOINT — I Came for the Combat, Stayed for the Fashion, and Forgot How Clocks Work[/h1]

[b]784 hours played. 32 days and 16 hours of my life. Zero regrets. Mostly.[/b]
I've spent 784 hours playing NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, so I think I've earned the right to talk about it.

Is it enough time to master the game? Probably not. Is it enough time to develop an unhealthy attachment to virtual cosmetics? Absolutely.

NARAKA combines fast-paced melee combat, incredible mobility, beautiful character designs, tons of events, and enough content to keep you busy for an alarming amount of time.

You launch the game thinking, "I'll play for 30 minutes."

Three hours later, your dinner is cold, your sleep schedule has filed a missing person report, and you're saying, "Just one more match."

Welcome to NARAKA.

[h1] Character Customization: The REAL Endgame [/h1]

The character customization system offers plenty of options for facial features, hairstyles, colors, and other details. Add the gorgeous skins, outfits, and accessories, and you've got a recipe for disaster.

A very beautiful disaster.

Seriously, the art team deserves a raise.

You can spend hours creating the perfect character, adjusting every little detail until everything looks just right. Then you finish and realize you haven't actually played the game.

Your enemies are practicing combos. You're studying color theory.

They're preparing for battle. You're preparing a fashion show.

And somehow, you're having the time of your life.

After 784 hours, there's always another character to customize or another tiny detail that MUST be changed.

At this point, NARAKA is two games in a trench coat: a combat game and a character customization simulator.

And I'm not sure which one I'm better at.

[h1] Events Everywhere! (Goodbye, Free Time) [/h1]

NARAKA does a great job with events and seasonal content. There's always something to do, from completing missions to unlocking cosmetics.

You log in to complete your daily missions. Easy, right?

Wrong.

You notice an event, check the rewards, discover another mission, and spot a skin you absolutely need.

Suddenly, your original plan is gone, your bedtime is in danger, and you're doing missions you didn't even know existed five minutes ago.

Daily missions aren't missions anymore. They're a legally binding contract.

You don't log in to play. You report for duty.

Congratulations, NARAKA. You've reinvented unpaid overtime.

[h1] The Battle Pass: Your Wallet Is Safe. Your Free Time Isn't. [/h1]

You can purchase the Battle Pass with Gold and earn all that Gold back by completing all [b]115 levels[/b].

Finish the pass, recover your Gold, and put it toward the next one. Save it, and you can keep the cycle going without spending real money on every new pass.

Your wallet: "Finally, some peace and quiet."

Your free time: "I've been sacrificed for the greater good."

There's just one small detail: you have to complete all 115 levels.

[b]The Gold comes back. The hours don't.[/b]

Considering I've already played for 784 hours, I'm probably not the right person to ask for time-management advice.

[h1] Playing With Friends: Friendship Is Temporary, Chaos Is Eternal [/h1]

Playing with friends makes NARAKA even more fun. You can coordinate attacks, develop strategies, and save each other from terrible situations.

Of course, that assumes anyone remembers the plan once the first enemy appears.

One person is fighting, another is running in the opposite direction, and someone is asking what just happened.

Teamwork makes the dream work.

Unfortunately, nobody told the team what the dream was.

Winning together feels great, but sometimes the funniest matches are the ones where absolutely everything goes wrong.

[h1] RNG: Random Number Generator or Personal Enemy?[/h1]

Trying to get a specific cosmetic can be painful. You know exactly what you want, open your rewards full of hope, and the game gives you literally anything else.

You try again.

More disappointment.

Again.

Nothing.

At this point, you're conducting a scientific experiment on the relationship between hope and suffering.

You start wondering whether the game knows exactly what you want and deliberately avoids giving it to you.

When you finally get something amazing, it feels fantastic. Until then, you're questioning your luck and possibly the entire mathematical foundation of the universe.

You close the menu and reconsider your life choices.

Then you open it again.

Because apparently, we never learn.

After 784 hours, I've concluded that RNG and I have a complicated relationship.

I want the cosmetics. RNG wants me to suffer.

It's not healthy, but I'm too invested to leave.

[h1] So, Is NARAKA: BLADEPOINT Worth Playing? [/h1]

Absolutely.

The combat is exciting, the customization is extensive, the skins are gorgeous, the events keep things fresh, and playing with friends makes everything better.

Sure, RNG can be frustrating, but it doesn't take away from how enjoyable the game is overall.

If you enjoy action games, collecting cosmetics, customizing characters, and playing with friends, NARAKA is absolutely worth checking out.

Just be warned.

You start playing for the combat.

You stay for the cosmetics.

You spend an hour customizing a character, get distracted by an event, complete your daily missions, play with friends, and get wrecked by RNG.

Then you look at the clock and say:

"Okay, just one more match."

Congratulations. You've officially become part of the problem.

[h3]784 hours played. 32 days and 16 hours gone. Still playing.[/h3]

I could have learned a new language or become a responsible adult. Instead, I learned that the perfect shade of blue matters, daily missions are legally binding, and RNG is my natural enemy.

Would I do it all again? Absolutely.

[b]10/10 — Would lose track of time again.[/b]

Your wallet is safe. Your free time, however, is another story.

[h3]Send help. Or Gold. Preferably Gold.[/h3]

review:
I never put a review, but Naraka is a kind of game I've been looking for for a while. Despite it full of bots, I still find it quite fun. Until you reach around Solar rank, expect to have lobby's with only bots. 
If you're someone who likes to learn about mechanics, high skill ceiling gameplay, rock-paper-scissors/movement combat, competitive, and don't mind much about the bots, then this game is definitely worth a try.

PVE (rift traversal): I started off with the PVE aspects of the game, and there's not much of a player base in it. There are secrets and cool puzzles, but I had to look up how to do it because the game doesn't give you much time to figure it out unless if you replay the mission again and again. I find that the losing all your equipment can be pretty punishing especially since there is so much need for rare materials to get the equipment do the perilous or doomed paths. They give you free lo tier equipment, but as someone who isn't on the game 24/7, I can't spend my time on the PVE too much.

*This game is meant for PVP. There is plenty of content for PVE, but I only really do it for the event rewards.*

The gameplay and potential of the game is why I'm giving this game a good review. The community in-game felt very inviting, and everyone just seems to have the same interest(to play with people lol). Fighting games is already a niche genre, but personally this game really deserves more recognition. 

PS: Needs a west coast NA server

review:
After almost 250 hours on this game I've concluded the following: 
-
1) THE GAME IS IN DIRE NEED OF A DEDICATED 1V1 GAME MODE
-
The current "lobby" 1v1 game mode is very slow and bottle necked due to its current structure.
The current structure forces players trying to do a 1v1 battle to just sit there and watch as the whole lobby franticly fights to be next in que, waiting around 1 stone statue to be next in line. 
 A dedicated "1v1" game mode, that also gives you a rank like "bloodbath" game mode, would be an excellent addition to this game, Providing more dynamic choices for play styles.
-
2) THE GAME DOES NOT SUPPORT PLAYSTATION CONTROLLERS PLUGGED INTO PC.
-
 As an older gamer, i still enjoy using my controller on my pc when playing this game, however, due to the games lack of compatibility for different controller types, I am forced to whip out the old Xbox controller instead, which as much as we love Xbox, the controller is not my favorite for daily use. 
This game would benefit significantly by focusing on this patch note, thus be able to reach a larger player base for people coming from the console world and joining us in the pc world. 
-
3) POSTIVE FEED BACK AND RECOGNITION.
-
The game has been making successful updates for years now, which shows this piece of art work will continue to evolve as time progresses. This is very important for a player base that stays loyal to the platform over the years. ( we want to make sure we are not forgotten about).
 NARAKA BLADEPOINT has successfully shown us that they have not forgotten us and have done what they can to listen to the community and take our feedback in stride to help evolve the art work as time goes on. 
The in game fight animation and mechanics and overall game play in both PVP ONLINE, PVE OFFLINE, have made a touch to them that feel like the perfect diamond in a rough that will continue to shine for ages. I wish NARAKA all the success in the world for there future and provided these adjustments are made, I can see the game going to the next level of major adoption real soon!

"The absolute peak of action-packed, high-mobility battle royales."

If you're tired of standard gunplay-heavy battle royales and want a game where mechanical skill, martial arts combat, and fluid acrobatics decide the outcome, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT is an absolute masterpiece.  

Why You Should Play It ?
1. Incredible Mobility: Grappling hooks, wall-running, and fluid parkour make traversing the map feel like a martial arts movie.

2. Deep Combat System: The weapon dynamics built around Normal Attacks, Charged Focus Attacks, and Parries create genuine mind-games during high-stakes duels.  

3. Varied Roster: Every hero brings distinct skills and fight-altering ultimate abilities that encourage different playstyles and team synergies.  

4. Detailed Customization: Gorgeous East Asian mythical aesthetics paired with an amazingly flexible character creator and outfit selection.  

Quick Checklist
- Graphics: 9/10 — Beautiful environments, flashy skill effects, and sharp character designs.  

- Gameplay: 10/10 — High skill ceiling; steep learning curve, but extraordinarily rewarding once it clicks.  

- Sound/Music: 8/10 — Crisp weapon clashes and immersive atmospheric audio.  

- Replayability: 10/10 — Endless room for improvement in movement, comboing, and counter-play.  

A refreshing, high-adrenaline spin on the genre that rewards agility, timing, and precision over camping in a corner with a sniper rifle. 10/10 — Highly recommended for fans of fighting games, action RPGs, and competitive multiplayer!

9/10 I was not entirely convinced at first but upon learning the game, this has got to be the best battle royale ever made. Picture Sekiro-like combat on a set of different battle royale maps with a lot of characters, each having their own (gimmickey) set of abilities and playstyles that you can choose.
 It's melee favored, because ranged weapons are mainly used to poke the enemy before engaging or to catch them from escaping. Tare limited to durability and that takes time to replenish amidst the fight and to collect beforehand, upon other things that you will loot during the match. But that's of course not everything in the game.

The combat is really high quality and despite what noobs might want you to believe; button mashing will quite literally get you owned. There is an increidbly in depth attack system full of combos, for every single weapon that can dictate your entire playstyle or approach to combat and a set of souljades that go from neat stacking buffs to literal alterations that enhance your current weapon attacks.

There are some annoying and spammy ultimate abilities, however they can only  be used once per fight and most of them leave you unable to chase, which makes securing kills pretty hard, as the movement in this game is probably the most important part.

Whatever can't catch you, can't fight you. And whatever can't fight you, can't kill you. With that being said, when starting out freshly, there certainly should be a lot of players that will be able to defeat you, since that is how niche competetive games work. With not enough casuals the sweats start cannibalizing eachother and thats not even neccessarily a bad thing, but as a new player with an unrecognized MMR you will mostly fight against bots in the beginning until the game starts dropping in real opponents, Even if I know that the guy that chased me down through the whole match will probably end me, I can at least start learning his attack pattern, like with some Sekiro boss. Or maybe I could just sneak away and let him take out his wrath on some other unfortunate souls. That kind of experience is entirely unique to Naraka.

The game is completely Free to Play and everything I describe in the following segment are purely optional cosmetics that do not alter the mechanical gameplay. The in-game store is detailed and if you don't find luck with mostly free lootcrates that have an unmissable chance system, should you get unlucky enough, You could also purchase some cosmetics directly from the store for mostly real money. However, the game to me seems quite generous and whilst I spent some real currency, I also got multiple legendary outfits, weapon skins and cosmetic accessories and extremes (even rarer) just by playing. Since the community on asian servers (f.e. china) is so large, there are tons of events where they hand out free stuff and I managed to get quite lucky with some legacy lootboxes.

Sadly the only negatives I have to give is the games incredible size on my harddrive. Whilst that can be explained by tons of modes. Next to the usual battle royale casual, and ranked with solos, duos and trios, with some vanilla - like event modes or a team deathmatch. We also have f.e. the whole single player/ coop stuff the extraction mode, some event mode,.. Whilst everything is semi-regularly maintained, you can occasionally hit the 10-20+ GB seasonal patch, but that's probably just an internet (skill) issue on my end. It runs surprisingly stable and you will quickly have patched access to the newest settings (upscaling algorythms, etc)
The only real bad thing that to me isn't objective is, that the game keeps getting shoved into a direction that to me looks more like a mobile game. Flashy new characters that basically force a disengage when ultiling since they will statcheck you. That#s not really bothering me though. What's awkward to me is the powercreep that leaves older and more beloved (and balanced and more fun to fight) characters in the dust.  Then again, with enough gamesense on these aforementioned characters you can definitely still perform. Just maybe not as easily. It's a difficult debate and calling something "no skill" in an enviroment where "hold checking" has become the basic means of traveling the map on foot.

Overall the best free game that I haver ever played. And I definitely haven't played enough, If you can give this game a shot and learn just the basics of the simple movement tech or combat 1&1, you will find yourself become anime. And that's also a feeling that no other game can provide.

Also the trailers look dope every season.

⭐ Option 1 — Bold, energetic, hype-filled review
Naraka: Bladepoint is honestly one of the most refreshing battle royale experiences out there. The game blends gorgeous wuxia and kung‑fu action with a cast that’s incredibly diverse — different cultures, body types, personalities, and aesthetics all represented with real love. NetEase didn’t just make a stylish game; they built one of the most queer‑friendly and welcoming communities in the genre. As a player who values inclusivity, it’s amazing to see LGBTQ+ folks openly enjoying the game without the usual toxicity you see in other BRs.

The character creation freedom is wild. You can build beautiful, fierce, cute, masculine, feminine, and everything in-between. The sliders go deep, and the game actually lets you express yourself instead of forcing you into one look. And the skins? Let’s be real — Naraka has some of the hawtest outfits in any action game. Elegant robes, badass armor, seductive cosmetics, stylish streetwear… they know exactly what they’re doing.

The kung‑fu combat is fast, fluid, and feels like you’re in a martial arts movie. Every clash feels personal, every dodge feels intentional, and every victory feels earned. NetEase really crafted something special: a game that’s not just fun, but free, expressive, and welcoming to everyone — especially queer players and BIPOC gamers.

⭐ Option 2 — More polished, review-style tone
Naraka: Bladepoint stands out as a battle royale that celebrates diversity and player expression. Its roster features characters inspired by various Asian cultures, and the game’s deep kung‑fu and wuxia influences give every fight a cinematic flair. The character creation system is one of the best in the genre, offering players the freedom to craft unique identities rather than cookie‑cutter avatars.

NetEase deserves credit for fostering a genuinely queer‑friendly community. It’s rare to find a competitive game where LGBTQ+ players feel comfortable and supported, but Naraka’s player base is surprisingly welcoming. The cosmetic designs also deserve praise — the skins and outfits are stylish, bold, and undeniably attractive, adding personality and flair to every match.

Overall, Naraka is a standout title for players who value representation, creativity, and martial‑arts‑driven gameplay.

Naraka: Bladepoint is one of those games that feels strange at first, but once the combat finally clicks, it becomes incredibly hard to put down.

The biggest strength is definitely the combat. Fights are not just about having better gear — timing, positioning, counters and knowing when to attack actually matter. Every weapon feels different, and there is always something new to learn. The movement system makes it even better, especially the grappling hook and climbing. Chasing someone across the map or escaping a fight by flying over rooftops never gets old.

I also really like how much room there is for improvement. At the beginning, you will probably get destroyed by more experienced players, but after some practice you start understanding combos, spacing, counters and different hero abilities. Winning a difficult duel after that feels much more satisfying than winning a typical BR gunfight.

The game also has a great visual style. The characters, weapons, animations and environments give Naraka its own identity, and the combat often feels more like a martial arts movie than a traditional battle royale.

There are definitely some frustrating parts. The learning curve can be rough, matchmaking is not always fair, and ping/netcode issues can make certain fights feel completely out of your control. These problems can be especially annoying when you are trying to improve.

Still, the core gameplay is so unique that I think Naraka is worth trying even if you normally don't like battle royale games. If you enjoy competitive combat and games where getting better actually changes how you play, this one can be seriously addictive.

It was weird when it released, but it has gotten much better over  years. I’ve been playing on and off for years and finally decided to write a review.

On the plus side: The gameplay loop is fun, there is a plenty of different modes, and you don't even need to play against real players if you don't want to. (Expert bots are better than 70% of the playerbase, beware, they are scary). The game also has good optimization.

On the downside: Most players are on the asian server, so expect longer queue times if you are elsewhere. The learning curve is also rather steep; being stunlocked until you figure out all the animation cancels and timings is basically a given. (Again, expert bots are a good learning tool here).

Overall, if you are interested in wuxia themes, battle royale, or extraction modes, it's definitely worth a try. Game is f2p but you can only buy cosmetics, no gameplay related power items.

review:
⚔️ 武侠博弈是核心，公平与玩法也有亮点
- 博弈体验独特： 普攻、振刀、霸体的三角克制逻辑，再搭配飞索三维战场，冷兵器博弈的爽感是其他同类型游戏很难替代的。
- 付费公平无氪： 所有对局内战力相关内容全部免费，没有任何数值付费门槛，零氪玩家完全可以凭技术碾压氪金玩家。
- 玩法覆盖多元： 除了核心大逃杀模式，还有PVE闯关、娱乐乱斗、摸金等多种玩法，能同时满足硬核竞技和休闲刷图的需求。
- 硬件适配友好： 低配置设备也能稳定运行，不用为了玩游戏专门升级电脑，普通玩家也能获得流畅的操作体验。
⚠️ 上手、外挂、资源和社交，都是实际短板
- 新手门槛偏高： 核心的振刀、连招、身法需要大量练习，新手很容易被老玩家碾压，前期挫败感很强。
- 外挂治理有短板： 官方虽然持续封禁外挂账号，但高段位依然存在不少外挂，部分外挂甚至能锁定玩家追击，破坏竞技公平。
- 运营资源倾斜： 官方后续资源更多向手游倾斜，端游原创内容更新节奏变慢，部分老玩家的需求得不到及时响应。
- 社交体系薄弱： 缺少深度社交绑定的玩法，好友互动、公会战队相关功能不完善，玩家的社交粘性不足。
🧭 按玩法偏好选模式，再决定投入多少时间
- 如果你是第一次接触永劫无间，优先从三排模式入手。不用强行练高难度连招，先熟悉基础博弈逻辑，就能获得不错的体验。
- 如果你是单排爱好者，建议先在人机模式里把基础操作练熟，再逐步提升段位，避免刚进匹配就被老玩家碾压。
- 如果你对竞技公平性要求极高，建议先观察近期的外挂治理情况，再决定要不要长期投入时间游玩。

review:
I really want to recommend this game because I like roguelike games but I just cannot.  While there are many elements to this game which are fun the pacing is what kills it.  The time it takes to make any meaningful progress is absurd.  This results in running the same maps with the same enemies with relatively the same power level until your mind is numb.     

The amount of cells you need to unlock upgrades is too high which results in needing to do a ridiculous number of runs to get the currency needed to unlock them.  

While I plan on continuing to play this game again from time to time because you can see the secret sauce is there, its going to be an every once in a while sort of game.  I have better things to do with my time as this one is too much of a grind.  

If you are considering I'd say wait for a sale on this one.

review:
Dead Cells is probably my favorite *whatever*. Metroidvania? Rougelite? Platformer? Its all three in equal measure, and it does a fantastic job of blending them together in a rewarding way that seems to keep the player coming back for more punishment. The gameplay will largely revolve around what build you want to play, and features a really fun system with three archtypes that you can either focus individually on, or blend at your discretion. This system rewards experimentation, and you'll be unlocking new items and abilities as you progress. Weapons, magical abilities, passive/active buffs, traps, companions, and the means of unlocking new routes thru the game. I really enjoy the way this game *works*. 

There's always a part in my reviews where I say something akin to "this game is eye candy", and I feel the same way about Dead Cells. Most of this game is visually stunning, provided you enjoy pixel graphics. Light is thoughtfully distributed throughout the dark tunnels, stretching corridors and dead keeps of the castle walls. Each of the "biomes" are visually unique, sporting bright and well placed colors that please the ape brain. This only reinforces the varying challenges that different routes can present the player. I'm a sucker for good parallax scrolling and this game masterfully uses multiple layers in some areas to make the land feel expansive and lived in.

The story is probably the weakest part of Dead Cells, but I don't consider that to be a hard negative. While most of the "big reveal" is pretty upfront, there's a ton of hidden backstory and implications that revolve around the player character, the kingdom, and the king who ran it. I thought that was pretty fun, as I tend to enjoy *earning* my story breadcrumbs at a time. What I DON'T like about this is it means most people will never see the full picture, because they won't feel like completing this very challenging game upwards of 5 times, scrounging for flavor text and bits of lore along the way.

All in all this is a fantastic (now unhidden) gem that finds itself in my rotation every few years. 8/10

review:
Important for it's time, but also kind of overrated. A very "meh" thumbs-up.

The part that Dead Cells does well is that it actually tries to incorporate slightly different playstyle mechanics into it's myriad unlockable weapons and items. And this is neat because it shows the developers actually taking a moment to think about how weapons and mechanics from other platformers might mesh with their own game. This makes the game feel much less like a clumsy 'kitchen sink' crossover and instead actually influences how you might change your playstyle per-run or run-to-run.

The part that Dead Cells does badly is that the platforming gamefeel of it's native game just isn't that great. It's floaty and slippery. Damage scaling is utterly absurd in the sense that on later difficulty levels it is very very easy to go from full health to instantly-dead within just a second or two of being caught in between enemy attacks due to the nearly nonexistant contact iframes that one normally sees in a platformer of this kind.

There's perhaps an argument that this is where the more 'rogue' elements of the genre are paramount, that it's intended to foster a more careful play style and the development of a higher skill level. But for what, exactly? Replaying the same biomes again and again on an even higher difficulty level with even more masochistic gameplay? There isn't really a 'living' story of any note. Background details and 'lore' areas occasionally suggest at one which the game is otherwise fundamentally uninterested in exploring further. The entire last DLC literally just gave up and said 'We're doing Castlevania now'.

As one of the first notable examples of the genre, I applaud it's innovation. And the inclusion of so many different accessibility and custom run options is absolutely solid on the part of the developer. And so while I appreciate coming back and revisiting it ten years later, it's just not a game that's near and dear to my heart despite the clear passion that went into making it.

review:
I know Dead Cells is incredibly popular, but I honestly don't understand the overwhelming praise. The combat is fast and responsive, and the pixel art looks great, but once the initial excitement wears off, the game becomes an exhausting cycle of doing the same thing over and over again.

The biggest issue for me is how repetitive everything feels. Dying and starting over is obviously part of the roguelite formula, but that doesn't automatically make it enjoyable. Losing a good run and having to fight through familiar areas and enemies again becomes more frustrating than rewarding. The game expects you to enjoy repetition simply because each run is slightly different, but those differences weren't enough to keep me interested.

The difficulty also feels unnecessarily punishing at times. There's a difference between a challenging game that encourages you to improve and one that makes progress feel like a chore. Unlocking new weapons and abilities should make things more exciting, but the constant grind takes away much of that satisfaction.

I can appreciate the amount of work that went into the game, and I understand why some people love it. Unfortunately, I found the overall experience more tedious than fun.

review:
Short version: I'm no expert in the genre, but I'd probably put this on the Rushmore of runs-based roguelites with Hades, Rogue Legacy and Spelunky.

Longer: I went into this game thinking - perhaps due to the description on the storepage or the use-defined tag that stated as such - that this was a Metroidvania. It's not, not at all. There's very, very little backtracking and, similarly, no movement-unlocks that further open the world up to you. It is no more a Metroidvania than Rogue Legacy 2 would be (which, I see now, *also* has that user-defined tag; perhaps gamers just see a simple map and think 'ah, yep, that's the Metroid there').

What Dead Cells actually does, it does very well: it's a fun runs-based roguelite experience. It's frenetic, chaotic and a very good time. I have my issues with it (mostly movement related: you get 'locked out' of a double jump after falling long enough, your character feels a bit floating, you magnetically gravitate towards ladders if you hit down on a pass-through platform), but for anyone who likes runs-based games, this will certainly scratch the itch.

That said, I *don't* love runs-based roguelites, haha. I think that I'm probably done after completing it once. I am certain there's much, much more that is on offer here.

review:
I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive

Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of  great games that are very clear and understandable
In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks

And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends.
Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy

And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights
Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points

If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else

I played the game with all the DLCs installed so I don't know what the game is like without the DLCs but the base game itself is massive from what I have seen.

For the price and level of replayability, I would highly recommend it even at the base price but it does come on sale frequently.

review:
Probably going against the grain with a downvote here... maybe a me-problem? but anyway.

Is this a bad game? Maybe not objectively. Graphics style is cool, the controls feel fast and responsive, and it's got a whole lot of content. Music is manageable, but not memorable.

But am I having fun playing this? To be honest, not particularly. It's a combination of things. Just to ramble a bit:
- The game is designed to be grindy by design. You have to unlock every f--ing thing. If that's what keeps if interesting for you, sure. Otherwise: eh. It's really one big grind-a-thon, The roguelite genre taken to extremes.
- There may be a story somewhere, but i was just some headless dude fighting through dungeons until i killed a king. And then I was back at the start. Some vague lore drops are dropped here and there, but i didn't really care about it since it was never presented in a way that made me care. Or something. 
- Then you traverse a whole corridor only to find out you don't have the permanent upgrade unlocked that is required to keep going that way. Or worse, it leads to a door and when you try to enter it it says "DLC REQUIRED". Please.
- Partly a skill issue, but the combat system never really clicked for me either. When going 1 on 1, it's usually okay, but when it gets more frenzied a lot of stuff can be going on at the screen especially with gibs and effects. This can lead to bs like (for example) make it hard to see enemy projectiles. 

At the end of it all, the core gameplay loop doesn't seem to reward much other than feeding into itself for the sake of it. And I never really had that "just one more try" moment that some games give. I might throw a few more runs in after this review. But I don't expect it to cause me to drastically change my opinion from this.

review:
A masterclass in blending roguelite and Metroidvania into something that feels both fresh and endlessly replayable. The combat is the star here: fast, fluid, and brutally satisfying, with every dodge, parry, and weapon combination feeling weighty and responsive . The pixel art is gorgeous, the soundtrack slaps, and the progression system—unlocking new weapons and permanent upgrades between runs—keeps you coming back even after a hundred deaths .

The caveats are real: it's punishing, and the difficulty curve after the first clear is a genuine wall that demands patience and practice . Some weapons feel unbalanced, and the early biomes can get repetitive after dozens of hours . But with 97% positive Steam reviews from over 130,000 players and multiple Game of the Year awards, this is essential for anyone who loves action games that respect your skill . Just be ready to die. A lot.

review:
If you arent critical of Rougelikes as a genre, youll probably enjoy this game quite a bit. It has a lot going for it. Fun combat, endless unlocks, and good replayability

If you're like me, and critical of Rougelikes, you'll also feel like this game controls like a floaty platformer mobile game. That is because this is a floaty mobile game. Button presses such as attacks aren't very satisfying, and movement/platforming is very floatly

There's some stuff to like, its a decent game, but there's millions of better rougelikes. This would have objectively been a better game if it didn't have to compromise its gamefeel/controls just to be a mobile game, but that isn't the Dead Cells we got

review:
I bought this on release, played it for a bit, then dumped it after 5 hours.
Two years later, I picked up Hades, played it for a bit, and promptly dumped it after 5 hours.

Then randomly, about a year ago, I decided to pick up Hades again, played it for a bit... and I finally "got" it, I "got" the roguelite loop, got addicted and went on a massive roguelite binge that's lasted until now.

So, 8 years later, I'm finally revisiting Dead Cells. Full circle moment.

It's great. It's addicting. I love it some times, and I hate it some times.
I have a love-hate relationship with this one.

Hades, love it.
BlazBlue, love it.
Trinity Fusion, love it.
Oblivion Override, love it.

This one? I lovehate it.
It's an abusive relationship, where the roles swap back and forth.
Once I'm kinda done with this one, I think I can finally lay roguelites to rest for a bit, and go back to Soulslikes and RPGs again.

But, for now, still got some game here and some explosive barrels to get clipped by in the distillery!

  另外说是肉鸽游戏，但是重点是在动作上，肉鸽构筑深度很浅。战斗很爽，不过动作苦手上手不用辅助模式会比较困难（用了的话可以非常简单，所以现在上手其实没那么难了）。
  总之是非常值得购入的游戏，所以停止更新了也是让人非常遗憾（悲），好想看到有一天可以重启啊，，，

review:
Easily a top 5 horrible gaming community ever. The game itself is also pretty mid (however still fun with friends) but its not as bad if you just avoid trying to interact with the community.

The reasons for the community being bad is a long list and one I don't care to list out in its entirety and why I think its bad so ill just simplify it. Firstly the vast majority of survivor only players cry constantly and think the game is killer sided (its not at all) They cry when you don't follow their made up rules like not tunneling or they cry when you simply play a certain killer and use their power. Secondly the community tries to cancel people (most recently TheBurntPeanut) for just playing the game and the devs giving them stuff free to promote the game. More than just those reason like the community being way to [strike]woke[/strike] but moving on to why the game itself is mid....

The devs mainly focus on making sure the survivor player base is taken care of and babysitting them while leaving the killers to rot basically. Most of the nerfs in patches go to killers and most of the buffs to survivors, to simplify. Its very obvious to anyone who plays both sides or to anyone who is good to see that survivors are the ones with the massive advantage. The games graphics also just not good at all but that is getting worked on but I have doubts it will look good even after the graphics update. The grind to unlock all tier 3 perks for all killers alone is WAY to long and will take you hundreds of hours maybe even over 1k, and that's not counting the grind to unlock them all on survivors as well. Then to add to the grind, unlocking all the original killers and survivors will take just as long. Mix in the fact that they are starting to lose the licenses for all the non original killers like Chucky, Myers, and Pinhead so you cant buy them anymore, and the fact that they will add killers, you buy them cause they are decent, then they nerf them. Lots of reasons to stay away from this game!

With all that said if you are planning on buying it just to play with friends (like me) its not the worse game. But the game as a game you play normally.... well AVOID

review:
Dead by Daylight has an amazing concept, iconic horror characters, interesting killer abilities, and so much wasted potential.

Unfortunately, the experience for casual-beginers and returning players(after long time) can be absolutely miserable. You just want to enjoy a couple of matches after a long day, but instead you get matched against experienced players who know every map, every perk, and every trick in the book.

The gameplay also gets incredibly repetitive. Repair generators, run, hide, get hooked, repeat.

And here's my biggest complaint: WHY IS THERE STILL NO PROPER SINGLE-PLAYER MODE?

I would happily play hundreds of hours against AI survivors and AI killers with adjustable difficulty, from Easy to Nightmare, proper progression, Bloodpoints, Prestige, and unlockable perks.

I don't want to compete with strangers who spend their lives mastering every single mechanic. I want to enjoy the fantastic horror characters I've paid for, at my own pace.

Yes, custom matches with survivor bots exist. But without proper difficulty settings, progression, rewards, or AI killers, they're no substitute for a real single-player experience.

I want to win sometimes and not everytime play against professional flashlight enthusiasts and unbeatable killers.

Until then, uninstalling. Maybe I'll see you next Halloween.

review:
玩了这么久杀机，官方能做到最稳定的游戏内容就是“稳定不平衡”和混日子客服。
游戏平衡改来改去，总能精准做到一边坐牢另一边也不爽。
账号出了问题去找客服也挺有意思：
这个不能办，那个也没办法，最后问题还在，工单先解决了。
玩家的问题不一定能解决，但工单肯定能解决。
挺好的，玩游戏练抗压，找客服练心态，一份钱体验两种折磨。


After playing for this long, I think the two most consistent features of this game are bad balance and customer support.
The balance changes somehow always manage to make one side miserable while the other side is unhappy too.
And contacting support when you have an account issue is also a pretty interesting experience:
“This can’t be done.”
“That isn’t possible either.”
The problem is still there, but somehow the ticket gets marked as solved.
Your problem may not get solved, but the support ticket definitely will.
Pretty impressive, honestly.
You play the game to train your patience, then contact support to train it even more.
Two different kinds of suffering for the price of one.


長く遊んできましたが、このゲームで一番安定しているのは「バランスの悪さ」と「サポート」かもしれません。
バランス調整は何度やっても、片方が苦しんで、もう片方も結局不満になるという絶妙な仕上がり。
アカウントに問題が起きてサポートに問い合わせるのもなかなか面白いです。
「これはできません」
「それも対応できません」
そして問題は何も解決していないのに、チケットだけは解決済みになります。
プレイヤーの問題が解決するとは限りませんが、サポートチケットだけはちゃんと解決されます。
素晴らしいですね。
ゲームで忍耐力を鍛えて、サポートでもう一度メンタルを鍛えられます。
一本のゲームで二種類の苦行を体験できます。

review:
This was my Diablo when I couldn't afford to play Diablo, and it could even run on my old PC, which would start heating up if I opened too many Chrome tabs.
What hooked me was the skill tree, the spell combinations, and the global chat, which was always funny and chill (apart from the occasional bot spam).
It's also quite impressive how the developers keep pumping out quality content and new mechanics every season, giving players new things to interact with without making older content obsolete. The devs are also pretty smart when it comes to planning their expansions so they don't overlap with PoE 2. This way, you'll have a steady supply of PoE crack all year round.

My main issue is having to replay the whole damn campaign for what feels like the 50th time. But I also understand why they do it: it forces you to become more familiar with your build, experiment with different setups, and maybe even come up with something innovative.

I highly recommend this game, especially if you already have experience with this genre of games
